# Magcoupler guidance, slice 2: implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** The teaching notes say what to change. Each note has:
- "What it is";
- "What to change", with input links, a step direction and the result each one moves;
- "Watch out";
- sources in a closed fold;
- live values from the user's own design.

Three new notes are added: how the coupling makes torque, the hot-low/cold-high torque band, and what happens when it slips. Every input gets help in plain words, with hint lines on the key controls. One display name is used per quantity. The spreadsheet details sit behind a "Show spreadsheet details" toggle, and the status line reads "Example design". Why links reach the notes from the Size tab, the end-effect banner and the empty Equation panel.

**Architecture:**
- **Engine:**
  - the plain-words guard (`engine::explain::plain`);
  - the note struct with change entries (`engine::explain::notes`);
  - live-value placeholders (`engine::explain::note_text`);
  - five probe designs (`engine::explain::probes`);
  - the part-pick map (`engine::picks`).
- **GUI:** a display-name, help and hint overlay (`gui::plain_text`) keeps the Python-locked engine labels and help unchanged. The note renderer is in `gui/explorer.rs`, with held states for inputs that Auto or a pick sets. The provenance toggle is in the panel.
- **Review:** every note passes a per-note physics review, and every help, hint and GUI string batch passes a G-3 review. The owner signs off a before/after sheet before the merge.

**Tech Stack:** Rust; egui 0.32 / egui_plot 0.33; the headless egui harness in `magcoupling-rs/src/gui/test_support.rs`; `linkage-sim-rs/scripts/gate.sh`, where gate 12 runs the Python oracle from `reference/magcoupling-py/.venv`.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-magcoupler-guidance-2-design.md` (decisions S2-1..S2-10, rulings R1-R14). The research is in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-magcoupler-guidance-2-research/`.

**How this plan was made:**
1. Eleven session-model drafters wrote T1-T21 against a fixed interface contract. Most of them checked their red/green cycles or engine claims in scratch copies of the crate.
2. A consistency and physics critic checked every task against the code, the contract, the spec and the trap lists.
3. The controller ruled on the critic's amendments.

**The "Amendments" section below is binding.** Where an amendment and a task's text disagree, the amendment wins. Where a line number or anchor has moved because of an earlier task, trust the code and keep the intent.

## Global Constraints

These come from the plan contract and bind every task.

- **Commit trailers**, exactly:
  ```
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
  Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UW1Rcc7PfLxGH7NQJ5srin
  ```
- **TDD:** write the failing test, see it fail for the expected reason, implement, see it pass.
- **Before each commit**, run all of these:
  - the touched suites;
  - `cargo clippy --manifest-path magcoupling-rs/Cargo.toml --all-targets --features app -- -D warnings`;
  - the same clippy without `--features app`;
  - `cargo fmt --manifest-path magcoupling-rs/Cargo.toml`.
- **Docs change with the code, in the same task**, wherever the task changes what they describe:
  - README test tables and counts;
  - `docs/ai/02-system.yaml`, `03-structure.yaml`, `04-memory.yaml`, `05-update-tracker.md`;
  - the BL-056 notes.
- **Never edit:**
  - Python-locked input labels, help, cells and choices (`tests/python_schema.rs`);
  - engine verdict strings (`tests/differential.rs`);
  - `reference/`;
  - `tests/data/python_schema.json`;
  - the untracked `docs/analyses/2026-05-28-press-4bar-analysis.md`, which belongs to the owner. Never stage it: stage files by name, never with `git add -A` or `git add .`.
- **On-screen text written by this slice:**
  - plain words for engineers who are not magnetics specialists;
  - no spreadsheet cells, correction or audit ids, file or code names;
  - numbers come from results (live placeholders or computed), never as typed default values;
  - glyphs only from the set the existing tests accept: write `->` and `<=`; no ∝, ϑ or U+207B in any sentence 0;
  - `plain_text_violations` returns nothing for every new string.

  **This applies to note `sources` as well (A-13).**
- **Caps:**

  | Text | Limit |
  |---|---|
  | Note sentences | 3–5, each at most 25 words |
  | Change entries | 1–5, text at most 25 words |
  | Watch-outs | 0–2, each at most 30 words |
  | Help | at most 30 words, 1–2 sentences |
  | Hints | at most 12 words |
- **Physics traps** must never be written:
  - spec section 8;
  - slice-1 spec section 8;
  - `phys-new-notes.md` section 2 (T-A to T-P);
  - and one added here: **"more magnets make the coupling stiffer"** is false at low fill. At a 20 mm ring radius, going from 10 to 12 magnets raises the twist at pull-out from 10.6° to 15.0°.
- **Input labels are never typed** into notes, fixes or hints; they come from `label_for`.
- **Doc comments:** indented lines become doctests, so use ```` ```text ```` fences.
- **Tests assert computed values** (from `compute_all` or metadata), not copied literals, unless the literal is the thing under test (a pinned string).
- **Implementers never spawn subagents.**
- **Branch and checkout:** branch `magcoupling/guidance-2` in the main checkout. Never switch branches, push, merge or `git worktree prune`.
- **Gate 1 rewrites** `docs/chebyshev_lambda/*.png`. Restore them with `git checkout -- docs/chebyshev_lambda`; never commit them.

The critic's full findings are in `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-magcoupler-guidance-slice-2/critique.md` (pre-flight table, contract violations, spec gaps, physics, test strength).

1. **A-1 to A-25 and A-27 are accepted as written.** Their text is reproduced below under "Amendments", unchanged. Where an amendment and a task's text disagree, **the amendment wins**.
2. **A-26 owner-level deviations.** The owner pre-approved "apply all recommended rulings" for slice 2. The controller decides these four and records them in BL-056 and in the T21 report:
   - **D-1 (A-26a).** T1 matches "Metal design", "Temperature design" and "Shaft clamps" only as sheet references: followed by `!`, ` C`+digit, ` (C`+digit or ` sheet`. Matching them bare would break the C-3 fix text "Raise Boss outside diameter (Shaft clamps)" and the "By original sheet" headings.
   - **D-2 (A-26b).** Add `Step::Enter` (a number entered from a measurement or an outside calculation: no direction, no aim). Also add the model-assumption exception to "aim Some for Raise/Lower" (A-1).
   - **D-3 (A-26c).** The three Size-tab hint keys (`size_tab.*`) are not input paths. They are collected in `SIZE_TAB_HINT_KEYS` and exempted by T2's key test (A-6).
   - **D-4 (A-26d).** R9 reaches beyond the dashboard (A-9). The results table and the Equation panel draw the cup-wall verdict in plain words. CSV, JSON and the spreadsheet keep the engine text.
3. **A-26e is DEFERRED**: no "Clamp boss diameter" display label in this slice. It is folded into BL-060 (the clamp boss link). Once the clamp's boss is linked to the drawn shaft boss, the two names collapse into one; renaming now would move the C-3 headed list and T2's `LABELS.len()` pin with no exact code in any draft. Instead, T16's `clamp_preload` change texts must make the two bosses distinct in words: the clamp's own boss against the shaft boss drawn on the Size tab. T20 appends this to BL-060's notes.
4. **Should-fix seeds (A-24 S-1..S-17)** go to the owning task's per-note or G-3 reviewer. The reviewer accepts or rejects each one with a reason, recorded in the review file.
5. **Drafter open questions not covered by the critique:**
   - (T3) The marker hover's closing scope line is accepted as drafted. Search still matches cells hidden while the details are off, because spec 3.6 leaves search unchanged.
   - (T3/T2) No "spreadsheet name" line in tooltips this slice. This is deferred: it is not in the spec, and no draft has exact code.
   - (T7 Q4) Delete the redundant Minimum OD line at `size_controls.rs:343` as T7 drafts; its hint says the same thing.
   - (T8 Q1) No "Corrected note" toggle line (YAGNI; not in spec 3.5).
   - (T8 Q2) Three engine gaps go to the backlog in T20 as BL-061..BL-063, each marked "verify first". T20 checks each claim against the code before writing it, and drops any it cannot confirm:
     - BL-061: the space-claim diameter leaves out the shaft boss (`metal_design.rs:432`);
     - BL-062: ferrite eddy heat uses the NdFeB conductivity;
     - BL-063: the daily-cycle bondline screen uses the recommended bondline, not the entered one.
   - (T16 note 7) `docs/ai/04-memory.yaml:58` gives the 2:17 SmCo 26 offset as -18.6 °C. T20 recomputes it with `compute_all` and corrects the line if it is stale (T16's drafter found -60.2 °C at b0166ad).
   - (T17 Q4) The reviewer may soften the non-ferromagnetic note's "the expansion caution fires" to "usually".
   - (T21) The release does not wait for BL-059 (the gearbox limit). The STOP message asks the owner separately.
6. **Model per task** (CLAUDE.md section 5; the contract's table):
   - Sonnet implementers: T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T18, T20.
   - Session-model implementers: T6, T7–T17, T19, and every fix round.
   - Escalate, never downgrade.
   - Per-note and G-3 reviewers always run on the session model.
7. **Review loops.**
   - **T7–T17 and T19** follow the in-task review choreography in their briefs. The implementer works in the tree WITHOUT committing, writes the dump and stops with `READY_FOR_REVIEW`. The workflow then dispatches a fresh session-model reviewer whose instructions are the prompt in the brief's review step, as amended by A-13 (sources are checked like every other field) and A-24 (seeds). The implementer applies the reviewer's must-fix items exactly. This runs at most 3 rounds; then come the flip to Reviewed, the review record, the docs and one commit. A third failing round stops the build for the controller.
   - **After each commit**, the usual task code review runs, with at most 5 fix rounds.
   - **A fix round that changes reviewed note text** reruns that note's per-note review. Its report is appended under the note's existing section as `### Re-review: <why>`, never as a second `## <id>`.

## Amendments (binding; they override the task text)

Reproduced unchanged from the critique (section 6), with the rulings above applied: A-26(a)-(d) accepted as D-1..D-4; A-26(e) deferred to BL-060.

A-1. Add `Step::Enter` and a model-assumption exception to the change rules (T4; contract "Interfaces T4"; spec 3.1 deviation, owner nod A-26b).
Why: T4's always-on `every_change_entry_names_an_input_and_the_result_it_moves` rejects Choose on a number and Raise/Lower without an aim; T13 (`calibration.f_cal_original`, Lower, no aim), T14 (`calibration.alpha_br_per_C`, Raise, no aim), T15 (`metal.measured_drag_Nm`, Choose, twice) and T16 (`temperature.demag.h_rev_likepole_kA_m`, Choose, twice; `clamps.clamp_length_mm`, Raise, no aim) each go red at their own commit. Both no-aim inputs are flagged `.assumption()` (`calibration.rs:68, 75`); their effect depends on the design (a prototype match, a picked grade), so their notes' own claims tests pin them design by design.
Code (T4 Step 4):
```rust
pub enum Step {
    /// One slider step up.
    Raise,
    /// One slider step down.
    Lower,
    /// Another choice of a selector, or another part, grade or material pick.
    Choose,
    /// A number entered from a measurement or an outside calculation: no direction, no aim.
    Enter,
}

impl Step {
    pub const fn word(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Step::Raise => "Raise",
            Step::Lower => "Lower",
            Step::Choose => "Choose",
            Step::Enter => "Enter",
        }
    }

    pub const fn up(self) -> Option<bool> {
        match self {
            Step::Raise => Some(true),
            Step::Lower => Some(false),
            Step::Choose | Step::Enter => None,
        }
    }
}
```
T4 Step 1, `change_problems`, the match becomes:
```rust
match (change.step, choice) {
    (Step::Choose, true) | (Step::Enter, false) => {
        if change.aim.is_some() {
            problems.push(format!("{} {}: names no aim", change.step.word(), change.input));
        }
    }
    (Step::Raise | Step::Lower, false) => {
        if input.meta.range.is_none() {
            problems.push(format!("{} has no slider to step", change.input));
        }
        match change.aim {
            // A model assumption's effect can depend on the design (a prototype match, a picked
            // grade): its note's own claims test pins it design by design.
            None if input.meta.assumption => {}
            None => problems.push(format!(
                "{} {}: a step names the result it moves",
                change.step.word(),
                change.input
            )),
            Some((aim, _)) => { /* unchanged */ }
        }
    }
    (step, choice) => problems.push(format!(
        "{} on {}, a {}",
        step.word(),
        change.input,
        if choice { "choice" } else { "number" }
    )),
}
```
Tests: `a_step_reads_as_its_word_and_goes_its_way` over `[Step::Raise, Step::Lower, Step::Choose, Step::Enter]` -> `["Raise", "Lower", "Choose", "Enter"]` and `[Some(true), Some(false), None, None]`; in `the_change_rules_name_each_kind_of_mistake` add goods `entry("metal.measured_drag_Nm", Step::Enter, None)` and `entry("calibration.f_cal_original", Step::Lower, None)`, bads `(entry("materials.parts.back_iron", Step::Enter, None), "Enter on materials.parts.back_iron, a choice")` and `(entry("metal.measured_drag_Nm", Step::Enter, up), "names no aim")`, and change the expectation `"a choice names no aim"` to `"names no aim"`. Contract: `pub enum Step { Raise, Lower, Choose, Enter }`. (T5 needs no change: `step.up()` is `None`, so `step_input` returns `Unmoved::Choice` and `unlinked_reason` draws a link.)

A-2. The entries A-1 changes (T13, T14, T15, T16).
- T13 calibration change[1]: `Change { input: "calibration.measured_torque_Nm", step: Step::Enter, aim: None, text: "the measured bench pull-out, never a value for your design; the measured factor rises with it, and only a prototype match uses it." }` (23 words); change[2]: `Change { input: "calibration.test_temp_C", step: Step::Enter, aim: None, text: "the recorded bench magnet temperature; a warmer test weakens the modelled prototype, so the measured factor rises." }` (17). In `the_calibration_note_s_levers_and_rule_hold_at_every_probe_design` replace the step and aim asserts with `assert!(matches!(note.change[0].step, Step::Lower)); assert!(note.change[1..].iter().all(|c| matches!(c.step, Step::Enter))); assert!(note.change.iter().all(|c| c.aim.is_none()));` (the design-by-design checks stay). Why: "Raise <Measured pull-out torque>" reads as the trap "edit the calibration inputs to match your design".
- T14 br_temperature change[1]: structure unchanged (legal under A-1); text per A-22.
- T15 slip_heating change[0]: `step: Step::Enter`, text "your bench value from a slipping test; it replaces the estimated loss and its high case in the temperature results." (20); thermal_time_constant change[1]: `step: Step::Enter`, text "your bench value from a slipping test; the loss and its high case then follow the measurement." (17).
- T16 demagnetization change[2] and ferrite_cold_demag change[2]: `step: Step::Enter` (texts unchanged).
- T16 clamp_preload change[1]: `Change { input: "clamps.clamp_length_mm", step: Step::Raise, aim: Some(("clamps.key_pressure_MPa", Sense::Down)), text: "a longer clamp fits more screws, a whole screw at a time, and lowers the key's bearing pressure; it needs more boss length." }` (23). Key pressure = 2 T / (d · contact · length) (`clamps.rs:472-474`): it moves at every step, so T5's aim test checks it.

A-11. "No prediction" for values computed from an out-of-range end effect (T5; spec 5).
Code (explorer.rs):
```rust
pub fn live_value(results: &DesignResults, path: &str) -> Option<String> {
    if end_effect_out_of_range(results).is_some()
        && (after_the_end_factor().contains(path) || greyed_by_end_effect(results, path))
    {
        return None;
    }
    match results.get(path)? {
        Value::Num(x) if x.is_finite() => Some(result_text(results, path)),
        Value::Int(_) => Some(result_text(results, path)),
        Value::Num(_) | Value::Text(_) | Value::None => None,
    }
}

/// Every result computed from the end-effect factor (the registry is fixed: computed once).
fn after_the_end_factor() -> &'static std::collections::BTreeSet<String> {
    static AFTER: std::sync::OnceLock<std::collections::BTreeSet<String>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    AFTER.get_or_init(|| registry().downstream("model.f_end"))
}
```
(import `end_effect_out_of_range`, `greyed_by_end_effect` from `gui::dashboard`). Test:

A-16. Shared word and sentence counters (T1; used by T2, T4, T7, T9).
Code (plain.rs, pub, pure std):
```rust
/// The words of `text` as the caps count them: the runs between whitespace.
pub fn word_count(text: &str) -> usize {
    text.split_whitespace().count()
}

/// The sentences of `text`: each '.', '?' or '!' that ends the text or is followed by
/// whitespace (so neither "0.1 mm" nor "1.35e6" ends one).
pub fn sentence_count(text: &str) -> usize {
    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    chars
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|&(i, c)| ".!?".contains(*c) && chars.get(i + 1).is_none_or(|n| n.is_whitespace()))
        .count()
}
```
Move T7's and T9's example asserts into plain.rs's tests; T9 uses `magcoupling::engine::explain::plain::{sentence_count, word_count}` instead of new `tests/common` copies; T4's `words` and T7's `sentence_count` go.

```rust
use crate::engine::clamps::SCREW_SIZES;

/// What [`plain_text_violations`] looks for, in its order. Each entry names its pattern:
///
/// ```text
/// C\d{2,3}             a cell: C and two or more digits
/// E\d{1,2}             a correction id: E, one or two digits, then no letter, digit or _
/// workbook             the word, in any case, but in the status line's "Workbook example"
/// Addendum             the spec's addenda
/// Rust-only            the engine's provenance
/// Calculator!          a Calculator sheet cell
/// M1 audit             the math audit
/// skeptic              an audit role: the word or "skeptics", in any case
/// Plan A-              a plan id, "plan" in any case
/// decision \d          a numbered decision: "decision" or "decisions" in any case, a space
///                      and a digit
/// drawing.py           the original drawing script
/// \.rs\b               a Rust source file: ".rs", then no letter, digit or _
/// Metal design         three sheet names, each only where it points into the spreadsheet:
/// Temperature design   followed by "!", by " C" or " (C" and a digit, or by " sheet"; on
/// Shaft clamps         its own a sheet name is an input group's heading and plain
/// Calibration!         a Calibration sheet cell
/// correction E\d       a correction by id, "correction" in any case
/// \bM\d{1,3}\b         an audit or milestone id (M1, M9, M43-13): M and one to three digits
///                      as a whole word, unless a decimal size (M2.5), a screw size of the
///                      clamp's table (SCREW_SIZES) or followed by "x" or "×" and a digit
///                      (M41 x 0.5); a part name has four digits (M5045) and never matches
/// ```
pub const BANNED: [&str; 18] = [
    "C\\d{2,3}",
    "E\\d{1,2}",
    "workbook",
    "Addendum",
    "Rust-only",
    "Calculator!",
    "M1 audit",
    "skeptic",
    "Plan A-",
    "decision \\d",
    "drawing.py",
    "\\.rs\\b",
    "Metal design",
    "Temperature design",
    "Shaft clamps",
    "Calibration!",
    "correction E\\d",
    "\\bM\\d{1,3}\\b",
];

/// The phrase that may say "workbook": the design status line's ("Workbook example design"),
/// until slice 2 renames that line (spec S2-5) and drops this exception.
const ALLOWED_WORKBOOK: &str = "Workbook example";

/// The [`BANNED`] patterns `text` contains, in [`BANNED`]'s order, each once. Every text the
/// calculator draws for its users (guides, notes, help, hover texts) is held to an empty list.
pub fn plain_text_violations(text: &str) -> Vec<&'static str> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    let lower = text.to_lowercase();
    let hits = [
        cell(&chars),
        correction_id(&chars),
        lower.matches("workbook").count() > text.matches(ALLOWED_WORKBOOK).count(),
        text.contains("Addendum"),
        text.contains("Rust-only"),
        text.contains("Calculator!"),
        text.contains("M1 audit"),
        words(&lower).any(|word| word == "skeptic" || word == "skeptics"),
        lower.contains("plan a-"),
        followed_by_digit(&lower, "decision ") || followed_by_digit(&lower, "decisions "),
        text.contains("drawing.py"),
        rust_file(text),
        sheet_reference(text, "Metal design"),
        sheet_reference(text, "Temperature design"),
        sheet_reference(text, "Shaft clamps"),
        text.contains("Calibration!"),
        followed_by_digit(&lower, "correction e"),
        audit_id(&chars),
    ];
    BANNED
        .iter()
        .zip(hits)
        .filter_map(|(&pattern, hit)| hit.then_some(pattern))
        .collect()
}

/// Whether `c` continues a word: a letter, a digit or an underscore.
fn is_word(c: char) -> bool {
    c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_'
}

/// The number of ASCII digits in `chars` from index `start` on.
fn digits_from(chars: &[char], start: usize) -> usize {
    chars.get(start..).map_or(0, |rest| {
        rest.iter().take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).count()
    })
}

/// `C\d{2,3}`: a C followed by two or more digits.
fn cell(chars: &[char]) -> bool {
    (0..chars.len()).any(|i| chars[i] == 'C' && digits_from(chars, i + 1) >= 2)
}

/// `E\d{1,2}\b`: an E, one or two digits, then no word character.
fn correction_id(chars: &[char]) -> bool {
    (0..chars.len()).any(|i| {
        let digits = digits_from(chars, i + 1);
        chars[i] == 'E'
            && (1..=2).contains(&digits)
            && chars.get(i + 1 + digits).is_none_or(|&next| !is_word(next))
    })
}

/// The words of `text`: its runs of letters and digits.
fn words(text: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
    text.split(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric())
        .filter(|word| !word.is_empty())
}

/// Whether `needle` occurs in `text` with an ASCII digit right after it.
fn followed_by_digit(text: &str, needle: &str) -> bool {
    text.match_indices(needle)
        .any(|(at, _)| text[at + needle.len()..].starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit()))
}

/// `\.rs\b`: ".rs" with no word character after it, a Rust source file's name.
fn rust_file(text: &str) -> bool {
    text.match_indices(".rs").any(|(at, _)| {
        text[at + 3..]
            .chars()
            .next()
            .is_none_or(|next| !is_word(next))
    })
}

/// Whether the sheet name `sheet` occurs in `text` pointing into the spreadsheet: followed by
/// "!" (a cell), by " C" or " (C" and a digit (a cell after the sheet's name), or by " sheet".
fn sheet_reference(text: &str, sheet: &str) -> bool {
    text.match_indices(sheet).any(|(at, _)| {
        let rest = &text[at + sheet.len()..];
        let cell_after = |prefix: &str| {
            rest.strip_prefix(prefix)
                .is_some_and(|after| after.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit()))
        };
        rest.starts_with('!') || cell_after(" C") || cell_after(" (C") || rest.starts_with(" sheet")
    })
}

/// `\bM\d{1,3}\b`: an audit or milestone id (M1, M9, M43-13), M and one to three digits as a
/// whole word. A decimal size (M2.5), a screw size of the clamp's table ([`SCREW_SIZES`]) and a
/// size followed by "x" or "×" and a digit (M41 x 0.5, M4 x 14) are plain; a part name has four
/// digits (M5045), so it never matches.
fn audit_id(chars: &[char]) -> bool {
    (0..chars.len()).any(|i| {
        let digits = digits_from(chars, i + 1);
        let word_start = i == 0 || !is_word(chars[i - 1]);
        if chars[i] != 'M' || !word_start || !(1..=3).contains(&digits) {
            return false;
        }
        let end = i + 1 + digits;
        let decimal = chars.get(end) == Some(&'.') && digits_from(chars, end + 1) > 0;
        let whole_word = chars.get(end).is_none_or(|&next| !is_word(next));
        if decimal || !whole_word {
            return false;
        }
        let token: String = chars[i..end].iter().collect();
        let screw = SCREW_SIZES.iter().any(|size| size.name == token);
        let mut after = chars[end..].iter().copied().filter(|&c| c != ' ');
        let designation = matches!(after.next(), Some('x' | '×'))
            && after.next().is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_digit());
        !screw && !designation
    })
}

```rust
// ------------------------------------------------------------------ plain words

/// What [`plain_text_violations`] looks for, in its order: a workbook cell reference
/// (`C\d{2,3}`), a correction id (`E\d{1,2}` as a whole id), the word "workbook" in any case
/// (but in [`WORKBOOK_EXAMPLE`]'s exact phrase), and three names of the engine's provenance.
pub const BANNED: [&str; 6] = [
    "C\\d{2,3}",
    "E\\d{1,2}",
    "workbook",
    "Addendum",
    "Rust-only",
    "Calculator!",
];

/// The phrase that may say "workbook": the design status line's.
const ALLOWED_WORKBOOK: &str = "Workbook example";

/// The [`BANNED`] patterns `text` contains, in [`BANNED`]'s order, each once. The guidance
/// text is for engineers who are not reading the workbook: the tests of every task of the
/// slice hold its strings to an empty list.
pub fn plain_text_violations(text: &str) -> Vec<&'static str> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    let digits_after = |i: usize| {
        chars[i + 1..]
            .iter()
            .take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit())
            .count()
    };
    // C followed by two or more digits holds C\d{2,3}; E with one or two digits and then no
    // letter, digit or underscore is E\d{1,2}\b.
    let cell = chars
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .any(|(i, &c)| c == 'C' && digits_after(i) >= 2);
    let correction = chars.iter().enumerate().any(|(i, &c)| {
        let digits = digits_after(i);
        c == 'E'
            && (1..=2).contains(&digits)
            && chars
                .get(i + 1 + digits)
                .is_none_or(|&next| !next.is_alphanumeric() && next != '_')
    });
    let workbook =
        text.to_lowercase().matches("workbook").count() > text.matches(ALLOWED_WORKBOOK).count();
    let hits = [
        cell,
        correction,
        workbook,
        text.contains("Addendum"),
        text.contains("Rust-only"),
        text.contains("Calculator!"),
    ];
    BANNED
        .iter()
        .zip(hits)
        .filter_map(|(&pattern, hit)| hit.then_some(pattern))
        .collect()
}

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::engine::explain::plain::plain_text_violations;
    use crate::gui::results_table::table_entries;
    use crate::gui::size_controls::{GAP, MAGNETS};
    use crate::gui::test_support::assert_glyphs;
    use std::collections::BTreeSet;

    /// Every row of the three tables, tagged with its table.
    fn every_row() -> Vec<(&'static str, &'static str, &'static str)> {
        [("label", LABELS), ("help", HELP), ("hint", HINTS)]
            .into_iter()
            .flat_map(|(table, rows)| rows.iter().map(move |&(path, text)| (table, path, text)))
            .collect()
    }

    fn is_input(path: &str) -> bool {
        InputCatalogue::get().entry(path).is_some()
    }

    fn is_result(path: &str) -> bool {
        result_info(path).is_some()
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_overlay_row_names_a_real_path_once() {
        // Spec 3.5 coverage test, its always-on half: no stray key, no key twice, no empty
        // text, and no help row that only repeats the engine's help. A hint sits under an
        // input row or a Size-tab control, so its key is an input.
        for (table, rows, inputs_only) in [
            ("label", LABELS, false),
            ("help", HELP, false),
            ("hint", HINTS, true),
        ] {
            let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
            for &(path, text) in rows {
                assert!(seen.insert(path), "{table}: {path} twice");
                assert!(
                    is_input(path) || (!inputs_only && is_result(path)),
                    "{table}: {path} is no input{}",
                    if inputs_only { "" } else { " or result" }
                );
                assert!(!text.trim().is_empty(), "{table}: {path} is empty");
            }
        }
        for &(path, text) in HELP {
            assert_ne!(
                Some(text),
                metadata(path).map(|(_, help)| help),
                "{path}: the row repeats the engine's help"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_canonical_names_are_the_spec_s() {
        // Spec 3.5's table: one name per quantity. The spec writes the ring radius's meaning
        // in parentheses ("the shaft centre to the back of the inner magnets"); that is help
        // (T7), the name is "Ring radius".
        let want = [
            ("coupling.inner_back_apothem_mm", "Ring radius"),
            ("coupling.npole", "Magnets per ring"),
            ("metal.face_gap_mm", "Magnet face gap"),
            ("metal.required_min_Nm", "Required torque"),
            ("metal.variation", "Production variation allowance"),
            ("model.gap_radius_mm", "Gap radius R_g"),
            ("model.pullout_Nm", "Pull-out torque (nominal)"),
            ("metal.torque_hot_low_Nm", "Hot-low torque"),
            ("metal.torque_cold_high_Nm", "Cold-high torque"),
        ];
        for (path, label) in want {
            assert_eq!(label_for(path), label, "{path}");
        }
        assert_eq!(LABELS.len(), want.len(), "no row beyond the spec's table");
        // The Size tab names its gap and magnet-count controls as the input rows do.
        assert_eq!(GAP, label_for("metal.face_gap_mm"));
        assert_eq!(MAGNETS, label_for("coupling.npole"));
        // No torque is ever called guaranteed (slice-1 spec 8).
        for &(path, label) in LABELS {
            assert!(!label.to_lowercase().contains("guarantee"), "{path}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn label_for_falls_back_to_the_metadata_and_never_to_the_path() {
        // An input and a result the overlay leaves out read as the engine names them.
        let drive = InputCatalogue::get()
            .entry("coupling.drive_torque_Nm")
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(label_for("coupling.drive_torque_Nm"), drive.meta.label);
        let f_end = result_info("model.f_end").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(label_for("model.f_end"), f_end.meta.label);
        // A path that is neither has no name on screen: "", never the path.
        assert_eq!(label_for("no.such"), "");
        assert_eq!(label_for(""), "");
        // Every overlay label replaces its catalogue label and is never longer (the inputs
        // side is 320 points wide, audit UI-34); display_label agrees with label_for.
        for &(path, label) in LABELS {
            let (catalogue, _) = metadata(path).unwrap();
            assert_ne!(label, catalogue, "{path}");
            assert!(
                label.chars().count() <= catalogue.chars().count(),
                "{path}: {label:?} is longer than {catalogue:?}"
            );
            assert_eq!(display_label(path, catalogue), label, "{path}");
        }
        assert_eq!(
            display_label("coupling.drive_torque_Nm", drive.meta.label),
            drive.meta.label
        );
    }

    /// A stand-in overlay: the mechanism is tested on it while `HELP` fills (T7, T8). One row
    /// over an input with engine help, one over an input without, one over a result.
    const TEST_HELP: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
        ("metal.face_gap_mm", "Stand-in help over a non-empty engine help."),
        ("metal.runout_mm", "Stand-in help over an empty engine help."),
        ("model.pullout_Nm", "Stand-in help over a result's help."),
    ];

    #[test]
    fn help_reads_the_overlay_then_the_engine_and_keeps_the_original() {
        let engine = |path: &str| metadata(path).unwrap().1;
        // The stand-in rows sit over what the test says they sit over.
        assert!(!engine("metal.face_gap_mm").is_empty());
        assert!(engine("metal.runout_mm").is_empty());
        assert!(!engine("model.pullout_Nm").is_empty());
        for &(path, text) in TEST_HELP {
            assert_eq!(help_in(TEST_HELP, path), text, "{path}");
        }
        // The original is kept only where the overlay replaces a non-empty engine help.
        assert_eq!(
            original_in(TEST_HELP, "metal.face_gap_mm"),
            Some(engine("metal.face_gap_mm"))
        );
        assert_eq!(original_in(TEST_HELP, "metal.runout_mm"), None);
        assert_eq!(
            original_in(TEST_HELP, "model.pullout_Nm"),
            Some(engine("model.pullout_Nm"))
        );
        // A path the overlay leaves out shows the engine's help and has no original.
        assert_eq!(help_in(TEST_HELP, "coupling.npole"), engine("coupling.npole"));
        assert_eq!(original_in(TEST_HELP, "coupling.npole"), None);
        // A path that is neither: no help, no original, no hint.
        assert_eq!(help_in(TEST_HELP, "no.such"), "");
        assert_eq!(original_in(TEST_HELP, "no.such"), None);
        assert_eq!(hint_for("no.such"), None);
        // The public accessors read HELP itself, for every input.
        for entry in InputCatalogue::get().all() {
            assert_eq!(help_for(&entry.path), help_in(HELP, &entry.path));
            assert_eq!(original_help(&entry.path), original_in(HELP, &entry.path));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_overlay_text_is_plain_words_with_glyphs_and_within_its_caps() {
        // Spec 3.5 and 6 test 9: every label, help and hint passes the plain-words guard and
        // the glyph test, and keeps the caps (help <= 30 words in 1-2 sentences, a hint <= 12
        // words, a label a name, not a sentence).
        let ctx = egui::Context::default();
        let _ = ctx.run(egui::RawInput::default(), |_| {});
        for (table, path, text) in every_row() {
            let what = format!("{table} of {path}");
            assert_eq!(
                plain_text_violations(text),
                Vec::<&str>::new(),
                "{what}: {text:?}"
            );
            assert_glyphs(&ctx, text, &what);
            for c in ['\u{3d1}', '\u{207b}', '\u{221d}', '\u{2192}', '\u{2264}'] {
                assert!(!text.contains(c), "{what}: {c:?}; write -> and <=");
            }
            assert!(
                !text.contains('\n') && text.trim() == text,
                "{what}: one line, no outer blanks"
            );
            let words = text.split_whitespace().count();
            match table {
                "label" => assert!(!text.ends_with('.'), "{what}: a name, not a sentence"),
                "help" => {
                    assert!(words <= 30, "{what}: {words} words");
                    assert!(text.ends_with('.'), "{what}: a sentence");
                    assert!(text.matches(". ").count() <= 1, "{what}: at most two sentences");
                }
                _ => assert!(words <= 12, "{what}: {words} words"),
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn each_display_label_names_one_quantity() {
        // No overlay label is any other input's or result's name on screen, ignoring case.
        let inputs = InputCatalogue::get().all().map(|e| e.path.as_str());
        let results = table_entries().iter().map(|e| e.path.as_str());
        let all: Vec<&str> = inputs.chain(results).collect();
        for &(path, label) in LABELS {
            for &other in all.iter().filter(|&&other| other != path) {
                assert!(
                    !label_for(other).eq_ignore_ascii_case(label),
                    "{path} and {other} both read {label:?}"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    #[ignore = "prints the overlay for the physics review; run by hand"]
    fn overlay_strings_for_review() {
        let rows = every_row();
        for &(table, path, text) in &rows {
            let (label, help) = metadata(path).unwrap_or(("", ""));
            let was = match table {
                "label" => label,
                "help" => help,
                _ => "",
            };
            println!("[{table}] {path}\n  now: {text}\n  was: {was}");
        }
        println!("TOTAL ROWS: {}", rows.len());
    }
}

Insert above the tests module in `magcoupling-rs/src/gui/plain_text.rs`:

```rust
//! The names and help the panel shows for the inputs and results (guidance slice 2, spec 3.5;
//! rulings R1, S2-4, S2-7): a GUI-side overlay over the engine's metadata, keyed by path.
//!
//! The engine's labels and help keep the workbook wording: `tests/python_schema.rs` holds every
//! ported one to the Python engine byte for byte, and the results table, the exports, design
//! files and share links keep them. On screen, [`label_for`] gives one name per quantity
//! (`LABELS`, spec 3.5's canonical names) and [`help_for`] the overlay's help (`HELP`)
//! where the engine's is empty, terse, stale or wrong; [`original_help`] keeps the engine's
//! text for the spreadsheet-details toggle, and [`hint_for`] the short line under a Key design
//! input or a Size-tab control (`HINTS`). Every lookup falls back to the metadata, so a path
//! the overlay leaves out reads as the engine names it.
//!
//! The Size tab's Outside diameter is a control, not an input: it moves the ring radius through
//! `engine::size_controls`, so it has no row here. A fix on the ring radius names that control
//! (`guidance::SIZE_TAB_ALIASES`, which wins over `LABELS` in fix text only); the input row,
//! the equation terms and the tooltips call it Ring radius.
//!
//! Search matches the display label, the catalogue label, the path and the cell
//! (`format::search_haystack`). No egui.

use crate::gui::dashboard::result_info;
use crate::gui::inputs::InputCatalogue;

/// The display label of an input or a result, by path: spec 3.5's canonical names. A row is
/// never longer than the catalogue label it replaces and names one quantity only (tests).
const LABELS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    ("coupling.inner_back_apothem_mm", "Ring radius"),
    ("coupling.npole", "Magnets per ring"),
    ("metal.face_gap_mm", "Magnet face gap"),
    ("metal.required_min_Nm", "Required torque"),
    ("metal.variation", "Production variation allowance"),
    ("model.gap_radius_mm", "Gap radius R_g"),
    ("model.pullout_Nm", "Pull-out torque (nominal)"),
    ("metal.torque_hot_low_Nm", "Hot-low torque"),
    ("metal.torque_cold_high_Nm", "Cold-high torque"),
];

/// The overlay help of an input or a result, by path: 1-2 sentences of at most 30 words, what
/// it physically is, what it moves and which way, and the trade-off (spec 3.5). Filled by the
/// slice-2 help batches; while a path has no row its engine help shows.
const HELP: &[(&str, &str)] = &[];

/// The hint line under a Key design input or a Size-tab control, by input path: at most 12
/// words (spec 3.5). Filled by the slice-2 help batches.
const HINTS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[];

/// The text of `path`'s row in `table`, if it has one.
fn row(table: &[(&'static str, &'static str)], path: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    table
        .iter()
        .find(|(key, _)| *key == path)
        .map(|(_, text)| *text)
}

/// The metadata label and help of an input or a result path; `None` for neither.
fn metadata(path: &str) -> Option<(&'static str, &'static str)> {
    result_info(path)
        .map(|info| (info.meta.label, info.meta.help))
        .or_else(|| {
            InputCatalogue::get()
                .entry(path)
                .map(|entry| (entry.meta.label, entry.meta.help))
        })
}

/// The display label of the input or result at `path`: its `LABELS` row, else its metadata
/// label; `""` for a path that is neither, never the path itself.
pub fn label_for(path: &str) -> &'static str {
    row(LABELS, path).unwrap_or_else(|| metadata(path).map_or("", |(label, _)| label))
}

/// [`label_for`] for a caller that holds the path's metadata label `catalogue`: the `LABELS`
/// row, else `catalogue`. The input catalogue builds its search text with it while it is being
/// built, when [`label_for`] cannot ask it; C-3 compares every input's with it.
pub(crate) fn display_label(path: &str, catalogue: &'static str) -> &'static str {
    row(LABELS, path).unwrap_or(catalogue)
}

/// The help of the input or result at `path`: its `HELP` row, else its metadata help; `""`
/// for none.
pub fn help_for(path: &str) -> &'static str {
    help_in(HELP, path)
}

/// The engine's help of `path` where `HELP` replaces a non-empty one, shown under the
/// spreadsheet-details toggle as the original note; `None` where the overlay fills an empty
/// help or has no row.
pub fn original_help(path: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    original_in(HELP, path)
}

/// The hint line under the input at `path`, if `HINTS` has one.
pub fn hint_for(path: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    row(HINTS, path)
}

/// [`help_for`] over `table`.
fn help_in(table: &[(&'static str, &'static str)], path: &str) -> &'static str {
    row(table, path).unwrap_or_else(|| metadata(path).map_or("", |(_, help)| help))
}

/// [`original_help`] over `table`.
fn original_in(table: &[(&'static str, &'static str)], path: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    row(table, path)?;
    metadata(path)
        .map(|(_, help)| help)
        .filter(|help| !help.is_empty())
}
```

```rust
/// What a search box matches an input or a result by: its display label (`gui::plain_text`),
/// its catalogue label when the overlay renames it, its path and its workbook cell, one per
/// line, lowercase. The results search and the inputs filter share it, so both match alike, and
/// an old label, a path or a cell still finds a renamed input (spec 3.5).
pub(crate) fn search_haystack(
    display: &str,
    label: &str,
    path: &str,
    cell: Option<&str>,
) -> String {
    let names = if display == label {
        label.to_owned()
    } else {
        format!("{display}\n{label}")
    };
    format!("{names}\n{path}\n{}", cell.unwrap_or("")).to_lowercase()
}
```

```rust
fn fix_label(path: &str) -> String {
    if let Some(&(_, alias)) = SIZE_TAB_ALIASES
        .iter()
        .find(|&&(aliased, _)| aliased == path)
    {
        return alias.to_owned();
    }
    let catalogue = InputCatalogue::get();
    let Some(entry) = catalogue.entry(path) else {
        return path.to_owned();
    };
    // C-3 compares the labels drawn on screen: the display labels (spec 3.5).
    let label = display_label(path, entry.meta.label);
    let shared = catalogue.all().any(|other| {
        other.path != path
            && ends_with_label(display_label(&other.path, other.meta.label), label)
    });
    let heading = path
        .rsplit_once('.')
        .and_then(|(group, _)| section_label(group));
    match heading {
        Some(heading) if shared => format!("{label} ({heading})"),
        _ => label.to_owned(),
    }
}
```

#### Drafter notes

**Assumptions about other tasks**
- T1 lands first and exposes `crate::engine::explain::plain::plain_text_violations` (`pub mod plain;` in `src/engine/explain/mod.rs`). If T1 names the module differently, only the `use` line in `plain_text.rs`'s tests changes.
- T1's new banned pattern "Shaft clamps" (spec 3.4) would trip the C-3 fix text "Raise Boss outside diameter (Shaft clamps)" (`guidance.rs:2430`, a static fix of the clamp guide, so it is in `every_text()`). T2 keeps that text; T1 must already have resolved it (ban only the sheet form, e.g. "Shaft clamps!" or "Shaft clamps C\d", or rename the C-3 heading). If T1 bans the bare phrase, T2's `the_fix_label_is_...` still passes but guidance's `no_guide_text_carries_workbook_jargon` fails at T1, not here.
- T3 edits `input_tooltip` and `result_tooltip` again (gating the path and cell lines, adding "Original spreadsheet note: " + `original_help`). T2 changes only their first lines; T3 should keep `help_for` / `display_label` there.
- T4/T5/T11-T17 draw change-entry labels with `label_for(input)`; T6 applies the display names to the remaining surfaces (equation header line, plot readouts and legends, the Size tab's Required and Hot-low readouts).
- T7 fills `HELP` rows and `HINTS`; T8 fills the rest of `HELP` and un-ignores `every_input_has_help_from_the_engine_or_the_overlay`.

**Rulings (proposed; reviewer please confirm)**
1. "Ring radius" is the label; spec 3.5's "(the shaft centre to the back of the inner magnets)" is help content for T7 (labels are short: UI-34, and the never-longer test). Same for "Outside diameter (the largest of cup, cap and boss; ...)", which T6 puts in a hover.
2. The Size tab's Outside diameter has no `LABELS` row (no path of its own); `SIZE_TAB_ALIASES` stays in `guidance.rs` and wins over `LABELS` in fix text only ("Raise Outside diameter" names the control the user moves; its link opens the Size tab). Everywhere else the input is "Ring radius".
3. The results table rows keep the catalogue labels (it is the spreadsheet-faithful view; its CSV/JSON come from the same rows). Search finds rows by either name and the row hover opens with the display name, which bridges the two.
4. `DashboardLine::label` stays the catalogue label because `spreadsheet.rs:350` writes it into the Summary sheet; the dashboard draws `label_for(line.path)`.
5. `HELP` and `HINTS` ship empty: all help is physics wording under G-3 review in T7/T8. The mechanism is tested on a stand-in table (`TEST_HELP`), so T2 has no help content to review.
6. `label_for` returns `""` (never the path) for an unknown path, per the contract; `term_label` and `fix_label` keep their existing "the path itself" fallback so a stray path never blanks a frame.
7. Re-entrancy: `InputCatalogue::new` must not call `label_for` (it would re-enter `InputCatalogue::get`'s OnceLock), hence `display_label(path, catalogue_label)`; documented in the item and in 02-system.

**Risks**
- The help-site wiring (input tooltip, Size-tab hovers, result tooltip help line) cannot be red-first while `HELP` is empty; `a_tooltip_opens_with_the_help_the_overlay_gives` and `the_size_tab_s_gap_and_count_labels_show_the_overlay_help` are equivalence guards that bite once T7 adds rows. Step 6 says so.
- `guidance.rs` test line numbers after ~1440 move by T1's deletion; anchors are quoted.
- Panel tests rely on "the inputs side paints first" when `label_for(FACE_GAP)` ("Magnet face gap") is also drawn as the Size tab's label; every changed site is on the Geometry or Results view (Size controls not drawn) or filters by `r.left() < INPUTS_WIDTH`.

    #[test]
    fn a_hover_text_is_built_with_the_frame_s_details_setting() {
        // The header's Show spreadsheet details reaches every readout's hover text through the
        // frame's readouts (spec S2-5); readouts made without it have it off.
        assert!(!Readouts::default().show_details());
        let size = egui::vec2(800.0, 600.0);
        for show_details in [false, true] {
            let ctx = egui::Context::default();
            ctx.style_mut(|s| {
                s.interaction.tooltip_delay = 0.0;
                s.interaction.show_tooltips_only_when_still = false;
            });
            let frame = |time: f64, events: Vec<egui::Event>| {
                let mut rect = Rect::NOTHING;
                let output = sized_frame_at(&ctx, size, Some(time), events, |ui| {
                    let mut readouts = Readouts::new(TermColors::default(), show_details);
                    assert_eq!(readouts.show_details(), show_details);
                    rect = ui.label("2.688 N·m").rect;
                    readouts.show_over(ui, rect, "model.pullout_Nm", |details| {
                        format!("details shown: {details}")
                    });
                });
                (output, rect)
            };
            let (_, rect) = frame(0.0, Vec::new());
            frame(0.1, vec![egui::Event::PointerMoved(rect.center())]);
            let (output, _) = frame(0.2, Vec::new());
            let want = format!("details shown: {show_details}");
            assert!(drawn_texts(&output).contains(&want), "{want}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_result_s_hover_names_its_path_cell_and_corrections_only_with_the_details() {
        // Spec S2-5: the path, the original spreadsheet cell (or the line that says there is
        // none) and the corrections that change the value show with Show spreadsheet details;
        // without them the hover is the same text with exactly those lines left out.
        for entry in crate::gui::results_table::table_entries() {
            let path = entry.path.as_str();
            let on = hover_text(path, true).expect("every table row is a result");
            let off = hover_text(path, false).expect("every table row is a result");
            let marks = CorrectionIndex::get().marks(entry.info.cell.as_deref());
            let marker_lines = if marks.is_empty() {
                0
            } else {
                marker_tooltip(marks).lines().count()
            };
            assert_eq!(
                on.lines().count(),
                off.lines().count() + 2 + marker_lines,
                "{path}: {on:?} against {off:?}"
            );
            assert!(on.lines().any(|line| line == path), "{path}: {on:?}");
            assert!(!off.lines().any(|line| line == path), "{path}: {off:?}");
            if let Some(cell) = entry.info.cell.as_deref() {
                assert!(on.lines().any(|line| line == cell), "{path}: {on:?}");
                assert!(!off.lines().any(|line| line == cell), "{path}: {off:?}");
            }
            assert_eq!(on.contains(MARKER_HEADING), !marks.is_empty(), "{path}");
            assert!(!off.contains(MARKER_HEADING), "{path}");
            assert!(
                off.lines().all(|line| on.lines().any(|o| o == line)),
                "{path}: {off:?} is not part of {on:?}"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn hovering_a_dimension_shows_its_result_s_hover_text() {
        use crate::gui::typeset::TermColors;
        let inputs = DesignInputs::default();
        let size = egui::vec2(1000.0, 700.0);
        let results = compute_all(&inputs);
        // With and without the spreadsheet details (spec S2-5): the path only with them.
        for show_details in [false, true] {
            let ctx = egui::Context::default();
            ctx.style_mut(|s| {
                s.interaction.tooltip_delay = 0.0;
                s.interaction.show_tooltips_only_when_still = false;
            });
            let (_, layout) = frame(&ctx, &inputs, size, Vec::new());
            let (_, rect) = layout
                .dimensions
                .iter()
                .find(|(tag, _)| *tag == 1)
                .copied()
                .expect("the face gap is drawn");
            let at = rect.center();
            let want = hover_text("model.face_gap_mm", show_details).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(
                want.lines().any(|line| line == "model.face_gap_mm"),
                show_details,
                "{want}"
            );
            let (before, _) = frame(&ctx, &inputs, size, vec![egui::Event::PointerMoved(at)]);
            assert!(
                !drawn_texts(&before).contains(&want),
                "not before the pointer is there"
            );
            let mut output = None;
            for dt in [0.1, 0.2] {
                output = Some(sized_frame_at(&ctx, size, Some(dt), Vec::new(), |ui| {
                    let mut readouts = Readouts::new(TermColors::default(), show_details);
                    geometry_ui(ui, &inputs, &results, &mut readouts);
                }));
            }
            assert_eq!(
                want.lines().next(),
                Some("Gap at the flat centres (effective gap)"),
                "{want}"
            );
            let texts = drawn_texts(&output.unwrap());
            assert!(texts.contains(&want), "no hover text in {texts:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_details_toggle_starts_off_and_a_click_turns_it_on_and_off() {
        let mut harness = Harness::new();
        assert!(!harness.panel.show_details);
        assert!(!MagcouplingPanel::default().show_details);
        tooltips_at_once(&harness);
        let output = harness.frame(Vec::new());
        assert_eq!(count(&output, SHOW_DETAILS), 1);
        // Its hover says what it shows.
        let at = text_rect(&output, SHOW_DETAILS).unwrap().center();
        harness.frame(vec![egui::Event::PointerMoved(at)]);
        let output = harness.frame(Vec::new());
        assert_eq!(count(&output, SHOW_DETAILS_HINT), 1);
        harness.click_text(SHOW_DETAILS);
        assert!(harness.panel.show_details);
        harness.click_text(SHOW_DETAILS);
        assert!(!harness.panel.show_details);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_details_toggle_is_a_view_choice_in_no_file_link_or_undo_step() {
        // Spec S2-5: GUI-only state, like the welcome strip's: the design, its file, its link
        // and the undo history are untouched, and a load, undo, reset all or a share link
        // opened as the session's start keep it; only a new panel starts with it off.
        let kept = |harness: &mut Harness, after: &str| {
            harness.frame(Vec::new());
            assert!(harness.panel.show_details, "{after}");
        };
        let mut harness = Harness::new();
        let file = design_to_json(&harness.panel.design());
        let link = harness.panel.share_link();
        harness.click_text(SHOW_DETAILS);
        assert!(harness.panel.show_details);
        assert_eq!(harness.panel.design(), Design::default());
        assert_eq!(design_to_json(&harness.panel.design()), file);
        assert_eq!(harness.panel.share_link(), link);
        assert_eq!(harness.panel.history.undo_len(), 0);
        assert!(!harness.panel.history.can_undo(&Design::default()));
        harness
            .panel
            .load_design_file(&design_to_json(&gap_design(2.0)))
            .unwrap();
        kept(&mut harness, "a loaded design file");
        harness.click_text(UNDO);
        assert_eq!(harness.panel.design(), Design::default());
        kept(&mut harness, "undo");
        harness.click_text(RESET_ALL);
        kept(&mut harness, "reset all");
        harness
            .panel
            .open_share_payload(&encode_share_payload(&gap_design(1.6)))
            .unwrap();
        kept(&mut harness, "a share link opened as the session's start");
        assert!(!MagcouplingPanel::new().show_details, "a new session");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_value_s_hover_names_its_path_cell_and_corrections_only_with_the_spreadsheet_details() {
        use crate::gui::corrections::MARKER_HEADING;
        use crate::gui::dashboard::{dashboard_lines, hover_text};
        // The pull-out on the dashboard and on the Size tab: one result, two readouts.
        let path = "model.pullout_Nm";
        let cell = result_info(path)
            .unwrap()
            .cell
            .clone()
            .expect("the pull-out has a cell");
        let shown = displayed_pullout(&DesignInputs::default());
        for show_details in [false, true] {
            let mut harness = Harness::first_view();
            harness.panel.show_details = show_details;
            tooltips_at_once(&harness);
            let output = harness.frame(Vec::new());
            let row = dashboard_lines(harness.panel.results())
                .into_iter()
                .find(|line| line.path == path)
                .expect("a dashboard row")
                .tooltip(show_details);
            let readout = hover_text(path, show_details).expect("a result");
            for want in [&row, &readout] {
                assert_eq!(want.lines().any(|l| l == path), show_details, "{want}");
                assert_eq!(want.lines().any(|l| l == cell), show_details, "{want}");
                assert_eq!(want.contains(MARKER_HEADING), show_details, "{want}");
            }
            // The Size tab's readout in the centre, the dashboard's row on the right.
            let mut rects = text_rects(&output, &shown);
            rects.sort_by(|a, b| a.left().total_cmp(&b.left()));
            assert_eq!(rects.len(), 2, "{rects:?}");
            let (on_size_tab, on_dashboard) = (rects[0], rects[1]);
            // At the text's right end (a wrapped label's rect starts at the row's left), with
            // a frame for the last tooltip to close.
            for (rect, want) in [(on_size_tab, &readout), (on_dashboard, &row)] {
                let at = egui::pos2(rect.right() - 4.0, rect.center().y);
                harness.frame(vec![egui::Event::PointerMoved(at)]);
                harness.frame(Vec::new());
                let output = harness.frame(Vec::new());
                assert!(drawn_texts(&output).contains(want), "{want:?}");
            }
        }
    }

```rust
/// The tooltip lines of the markers: per correction its id and title, the workbook and
/// corrected values where it changes the cell at the default design, and its evidence. The
/// corrected value is the one with that correction alone (as the registry and the golden
/// files record it), so on a cell two corrections change neither is the value shown.
pub fn marker_tooltip(marks: &[Mark]) -> String {
    let mut lines = vec!["Corrected vs workbook:".to_owned()];
    for mark in marks {
        let deviation = &REGISTRY[mark.id.index()];
        lines.push(format!("{}: {}", mark.id, deviation.title));
        if let Tie::AtDefaults {
            workbook,
            corrected,
        } = &mark.tie
        {
            lines.push(format!(
                "  at the default design, with {} alone: workbook {}, corrected {}",
                mark.id,
                format_value(workbook),
                format_value(corrected)
            ));
        }
        lines.push(format!("  {}", deviation.evidence()));
    }
    lines.join("\n")
}
```

with

```rust
/// The first line of a marked value's hover text (spec 3.6), before a colon.
pub const MARKER_HEADING: &str = "Differs from the original spreadsheet";

/// The last line of a marked value's hover text when a correction gives its values.
pub const MARKER_SCOPE: &str =
    "Was and now are values at the default design, with only that correction applied.";

/// A correction as the hover texts name it: its id and its title.
pub fn correction_title(id: DeviationId) -> String {
    format!("{id}: {}", REGISTRY[id.index()].title)
}

/// The hover lines of the markers (spec 3.6; shown only with the spreadsheet details): the
/// heading, then per correction its id and title, with ", was X, now Y" where it changes the
/// cell at the default design, and then what those values are. The "now" value is the one with
/// that correction alone (as the registry and the golden files record it), so on a cell two
/// corrections change neither is the value shown. No repo path: the export keeps the evidence.
pub fn marker_tooltip(marks: &[Mark]) -> String {
    let mut lines = vec![format!("{MARKER_HEADING}:")];
    for mark in marks {
        let title = correction_title(mark.id);
        lines.push(match &mark.tie {
            Tie::AtDefaults {
                workbook,
                corrected,
            } => format!(
                "{title}, was {}, now {}",
                format_value(workbook),
                format_value(corrected)
            ),
            Tie::Named => title,
        });
    }
    if marks
        .iter()
        .any(|mark| matches!(mark.tie, Tie::AtDefaults { .. }))
    {
        lines.push(MARKER_SCOPE.to_owned());
    }
    lines.join("\n")
}

    #[test]
    fn tooltips_name_the_path_cell_and_original_note_only_with_the_spreadsheet_details() {
        // Spec S2-5 and 3.5: with Show spreadsheet details the tooltip adds, after the help,
        // the original spreadsheet's note where the GUI's help replaced it, the path and the
        // cell (or the line that says there is none); without them exactly those lines go.
        let catalogue = InputCatalogue::new();
        for entry in catalogue.all() {
            let path = entry.path.as_str();
            let on = input_tooltip(entry, true);
            let off = input_tooltip(entry, false);
            let original = original_help(path).map(|note| format!("{ORIGINAL_NOTE}: {note}"));
            let added = 2 + usize::from(original.is_some());
            assert_eq!(
                on.lines().count(),
                off.lines().count() + added,
                "{path}: {on:?} against {off:?}"
            );
            assert!(on.lines().any(|line| line == path), "{on:?}");
            assert!(!off.lines().any(|line| line == path), "{off:?}");
            if let Some(cell) = entry.meta.cell {
                assert!(on.lines().any(|line| line == cell), "{on:?}");
                assert!(!off.lines().any(|line| line == cell), "{off:?}");
            }
            if let Some(original) = &original {
                assert!(on.lines().any(|line| line == original), "{on:?}");
            }
            assert!(!off.contains(ORIGINAL_NOTE), "{off:?}");
            assert!(
                off.lines().all(|line| on.lines().any(|o| o == line)),
                "{path}: {off:?} is not part of {on:?}"
            );
        }
    }

```rust
/// The widths of the label, value, cell and marker columns of a table `available` points wide
/// with `spacing` points between columns (decision M42-8): the label column flexes, at least
/// [`LABEL_MIN_WIDTH`], so a narrow centre region (a ~930 px window, where the M4-1 table showed
/// only its labels) still shows the label and the value without scrolling.
pub fn column_widths(available: f32, spacing: f32) -> [f32; 4] {
    let fixed = VALUE_WIDTH + CELL_WIDTH + MARKER_WIDTH + 3.0 * spacing;
    [
        (available - fixed).max(LABEL_MIN_WIDTH),
        VALUE_WIDTH,
        CELL_WIDTH,
        MARKER_WIDTH,
    ]
}
```

with

```rust
/// The widths of the label, value, cell and marker columns of a table `available` points wide
/// with `spacing` points between columns (decision M42-8): the label column flexes, at least
/// [`LABEL_MIN_WIDTH`], so a narrow centre region (a ~930 px window, where the M4-1 table showed
/// only its labels) still shows the label and the value without scrolling. Without the
/// spreadsheet details (`show_details`, spec S2-5) the cell and marker columns are not drawn:
/// their widths are 0 and the label takes their room.
pub fn column_widths(available: f32, spacing: f32, show_details: bool) -> [f32; 4] {
    let (cell, marker) = if show_details {
        (CELL_WIDTH, MARKER_WIDTH)
    } else {
        (0.0, 0.0)
    };
    let gaps = if show_details { 3.0 } else { 1.0 };
    let fixed = VALUE_WIDTH + cell + marker + gaps * spacing;
    [
        (available - fixed).max(LABEL_MIN_WIDTH),
        VALUE_WIDTH,
        cell,
        marker,
    ]
}

/// The width of a row of columns `widths` ([`column_widths`]) with `spacing` points between
/// the columns drawn (a column 0 wide is not drawn).
pub fn row_width(widths: [f32; 4], spacing: f32) -> f32 {
    let drawn = widths.iter().filter(|&&width| width > 0.0).count();
    widths.iter().sum::<f32>() + spacing * drawn.saturating_sub(1) as f32
}
```

    #[test]
    fn a_step_reads_as_its_word_and_goes_its_way() {
        let steps = [Step::Raise, Step::Lower, Step::Choose];
        assert_eq!(steps.map(Step::word), ["Raise", "Lower", "Choose"]);
        assert_eq!(steps.map(Step::up), [Some(true), Some(false), None]);
    }

    /// What is wrong with a change entry (slice-2 spec 3.1 and section 6 test 2): an input
    /// that is no input; Choose on a number, or Raise or Lower on a choice (a selector or a
    /// part, grade or material name); a number with no slider to step; an aim on a choice or
    /// none on a step; an aim that is no number result of the default design.
    fn change_problems(change: &Change) -> Vec<String> {
        use crate::engine::api::{DesignInputs, compute_all};
        use crate::engine::meta::{FieldType, input_rows, result_rows};
        let inputs = input_rows(&DesignInputs::default());
        let Some(input) = inputs.iter().find(|r| r.path == change.input) else {
            return vec![format!("{} is no input", change.input)];
        };
        let choice = !input.meta.choices.is_empty() || input.meta.ty == FieldType::Text;
        let mut problems = Vec::new();
        match (change.step, choice) {
            (Step::Choose, true) => {
                if change.aim.is_some() {
                    problems.push(format!("Choose {}: a choice names no aim", change.input));
                }
            }
            (Step::Raise | Step::Lower, false) => {
                if input.meta.range.is_none() {
                    problems.push(format!("{} has no slider to step", change.input));
                }
                match change.aim {
                    None => problems.push(format!(
                        "{} {}: a step names the result it moves",
                        change.step.word(),
                        change.input
                    )),
                    Some((aim, _)) => {
                        let results = result_rows(&compute_all(&DesignInputs::default()));
                        match results.iter().find(|r| r.path == aim) {
                            None => problems.push(format!("aim {aim} is no result")),
                            Some(r)
                                if !matches!(
                                    r.meta.ty,
                                    FieldType::F64 | FieldType::I64 | FieldType::NumOrText
                                ) =>
                            {
                                problems.push(format!("aim {aim} is not a number"))
                            }
                            Some(_) => {}
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            (step, choice) => problems.push(format!(
                "{} on {}, a {}",
                step.word(),
                change.input,
                if choice { "choice" } else { "number" }
            )),
        }
        problems
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_change_rules_name_each_kind_of_mistake() {
        let entry = |input, step, aim| Change {
            input,
            step,
            aim,
            text: "",
        };
        let up = Some(("model.pullout_Nm", Sense::Up));
        for good in [
            entry("metal.face_gap_mm", Step::Lower, up),
            entry("coupling.npole", Step::Raise, up),
            entry("coupling.magnets.axial_length_mm", Step::Raise, up),
            entry("materials.parts.back_iron", Step::Choose, None),
            entry("coupling.magnets.part_inner", Step::Choose, None),
            entry("coupling.backiron", Step::Choose, None),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(change_problems(&good), Vec::<String>::new(), "{good:?}");
        }
        for (bad, why) in [
            (entry("no.such.input", Step::Raise, up), "is no input"),
            (entry("model.pullout_Nm", Step::Raise, up), "is no input"),
            (
                entry("materials.parts.back_iron", Step::Raise, up),
                "Raise on materials.parts.back_iron, a choice",
            ),
            (
                entry("metal.face_gap_mm", Step::Choose, None),
                "Choose on metal.face_gap_mm, a number",
            ),
            (
                entry("materials.parts.back_iron", Step::Choose, up),
                "a choice names no aim",
            ),
            (
                entry("metal.face_gap_mm", Step::Lower, None),
                "a step names the result it moves",
            ),
            (
                entry(
                    "metal.face_gap_mm",
                    Step::Lower,
                    Some(("coupling.npole", Sense::Up)),
                ),
                "aim coupling.npole is no result",
            ),
            (
                entry(
                    "metal.face_gap_mm",
                    Step::Lower,
                    Some(("materials.cup_wall_check", Sense::Up)),
                ),
                "aim materials.cup_wall_check is not a number",
            ),
        ] {
            let problems = change_problems(&bad);
            assert!(
                problems.iter().any(|p| p.contains(why)),
                "{bad:?}: {problems:?}"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_change_entry_names_an_input_and_the_result_it_moves() {
        let failures: Vec<String> = NOTES
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|n| {
                n.change
                    .iter()
                    .flat_map(change_problems)
                    .map(move |p| format!("{}: {p}", n.id))
            })
            .collect();
        assert!(failures.is_empty(), "{failures:#?}");
    }

    /// Whitespace-separated words, as the caps count them.
    fn words(text: &str) -> usize {
        text.split_whitespace().count()
    }

    /// The one note that may have no change entry: its warning never fires on the library
    /// (slice-2 ruling R13).
    const NO_CHANGE_NOTE: &str = "a5.ferromagnetic_sleeve_or_liner";

    #[test]
    #[ignore = "un-ignored in T18 when every note is rewritten"]
    fn every_note_keeps_to_the_slice_2_caps() {
        let mut failures = Vec::new();
        for n in NOTES {
            if !(3..=5).contains(&n.sentences.len()) {
                failures.push(format!(
                    "{}: {} sentences, not 3 to 5",
                    n.id,
                    n.sentences.len()
                ));
            }
            for (i, s) in n.sentences.iter().enumerate() {
                if words(s) > 25 {
                    failures.push(format!("{}: sentence {i} has {} words", n.id, words(s)));
                }
            }
            let fewest = usize::from(n.id != NO_CHANGE_NOTE);
            if !(fewest..=5).contains(&n.change.len()) {
                failures.push(format!(
                    "{}: {} change entries, not {fewest} to 5",
                    n.id,
                    n.change.len()
                ));
            }
            for c in n.change {
                if words(c.text) > 25 {
                    failures.push(format!(
                        "{}: the {} entry has {} words",
                        n.id,
                        c.input,
                        words(c.text)
                    ));
                }
            }
            if n.watch_out.len() > 2 {
                failures.push(format!("{}: {} watch-outs", n.id, n.watch_out.len()));
            }
            for (i, w) in n.watch_out.iter().enumerate() {
                if words(w) > 30 {
                    failures.push(format!("{}: watch-out {i} has {} words", n.id, words(w)));
                }
            }
        }
        assert!(failures.is_empty(), "{failures:#?}");
    }

    /// What makes a sentence 0 more than plain words (slice-2 spec 3.1, F10), each named once:
    /// a live value, a formula sign or a symbol's subscript, a Greek letter (a symbol), a glyph
    /// the panel redraws (ϑ, the superscript minus, ∝; sentence 0 is counted as drawn).
    fn sentence_zero_problems(sentence: &str) -> Vec<&'static str> {
        let has = |bad: fn(char) -> bool| sentence.chars().any(bad);
        let mut problems = Vec::new();
        if has(|c| matches!(c, '{' | '}')) {
            problems.push("a live value");
        }
        if has(|c| matches!(c, '=' | '_' | '^')) {
            problems.push("a formula sign or subscript");
        }
        if has(|c| ('\u{0370}'..='\u{03FF}').contains(&c)) {
            problems.push("a Greek letter");
        }
        if has(|c| matches!(c, '\u{03D1}' | '\u{207B}' | '\u{221D}')) {
            problems.push("a glyph the panel redraws");
        }
        problems
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_sentence_zero_rule_names_what_it_finds() {
        assert!(
            sentence_zero_problems("The coupling slips when the load passes its pull-out torque.")
                .is_empty()
        );
        assert!(
            sentence_zero_problems("At 20 °C the torque is about 7 % higher, 1.2 N·m.").is_empty()
        );
        assert_eq!(
            sentence_zero_problems("Here {metal.variation}."),
            ["a live value"]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            sentence_zero_problems("T = σ A r."),
            ["a formula sign or subscript", "a Greek letter"]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            sentence_zero_problems("S_n falls."),
            ["a formula sign or subscript"]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            sentence_zero_problems("torque ∝ Br²"),
            ["a glyph the panel redraws"]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            sentence_zero_problems("at ϑ"),
            ["a Greek letter", "a glyph the panel redraws"]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    #[ignore = "un-ignored in T18 when every note is rewritten"]
    fn every_sentence_zero_is_plain_words() {
        let failures: Vec<String> = NOTES
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|n| {
                let problems = sentence_zero_problems(n.sentences.first().copied().unwrap_or(""));
                (!problems.is_empty()).then(|| format!("{}: {problems:?}", n.id))
            })
            .collect();
        assert!(failures.is_empty(), "{failures:#?}");
    }
}

    Choose,

impl Step {
    /// The word an entry starts with on screen.
    pub const fn word(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Step::Raise => "Raise",
            Step::Lower => "Lower",
            Step::Choose => "Choose",

    /// slider).
    pub const fn up(self) -> Option<bool> {
        match self {

            Step::Lower => Some(false),
            Step::Choose => None,

with:

```rust
pub struct SliderRange {
    pub min: f64,
    pub max: f64,
    pub step: f64,
    pub log: bool,
}

impl SliderRange {
    /// `x` one step of the slider up (`up`) or down, kept on the slider: `None` at the
    /// slider's end that way and for a number that is not one; a value typed past the slider's
    /// other end comes back onto it. A check guide's fix (`gui::guidance`) and a teaching
    /// note's change entry take this step.
    pub fn step_from(self, x: f64, up: bool) -> Option<f64> {
        let next = if up {
            (x < self.max).then_some(x + self.step)
        } else {
            (x > self.min).then_some(x - self.step)
        }?;
        Some(next.clamp(self.min, self.max))
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 11: Make the check guides' `step` take it** (one rule, no copy). In
  `magcoupling-rs/src/gui/guidance.rs` replace (lines 790-800):

```rust
/// `x` one step of the slider `range` up (Raise) or down (Lower), kept on the slider: `None`
/// at the slider's end that way, for a number that is not one, and for a choice. A value
/// typed past the slider's end comes back onto it.
fn step(x: f64, range: SliderRange, direction: Direction) -> Option<f64> {
    let next = match direction {
        Direction::Raise if x < range.max => x + range.step,
        Direction::Lower if x > range.min => x - range.step,
        _ => return None,
    };
    Some(next.clamp(range.min, range.max))
}
```

with:

```rust
/// `x` one step of the slider `range` up (Raise) or down (Lower), kept on the slider: `None`
/// at the slider's end that way, for a number that is not one, and for a choice. A value
/// typed past the slider's end comes back onto it ([`SliderRange::step_from`], the step a
/// teaching note's change entry takes too).
fn step(x: f64, range: SliderRange, direction: Direction) -> Option<f64> {
    match direction {
        Direction::Raise => range.step_from(x, true),
        Direction::Lower => range.step_from(x, false),
        Direction::Change | Direction::CustomHotterGrade => None,
    }
}
