```rust
//! Which inputs a part pick sets in place of the user's value (guidance slice 2, spec 3.1 and
//! section 5): a teaching note's "What to change" entry whose input a pick sets is drawn as
//! plain text with the reason, never as a link to a row that changes nothing, and the
//! change-direction test skips it there.
//!
//! The rules are the engine's own: `material_library::resolve` for the back-iron and the
//! sleeve-and-liner picks, `model::resolve_magnets` for each ring's part and grade. The tests
//! nudge every input [`set_by_pick`] names, on every pick, and require that no result moves;
//! and they require every other input a pick leaves without effect to be named here, or listed
//! with the reason it is unused.

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use std::collections::BTreeSet;

    use super::*;
    use crate::engine::api::compute_all;
    use crate::engine::material_library::CAP_HOUSING_CHOICES;
    use crate::engine::meta::{InputSet, ResultRow, Value, input_rows, result_rows};

    /// The cap pick.
    const CAP_PICK: &str = "materials.parts.cap_housing";

    /// Inputs a non-ferromagnetic back iron leaves without effect that no pick sets: the steel
    /// circuit's stored slip-loss fields, unused under the free-space circuit (as Back iron =
    /// no back iron leaves them).
    const UNUSED_WITHOUT_STEEL: [&str; 3] = [
        "temperature.slip_loss.b_hub_T",
        "temperature.slip_loss.b_cup_T",
        "temperature.slip_loss.web_integral_T2m2",
    ];

    /// Any change at all; two NaNs are no change.
    fn changed(a: &Value, b: &Value) -> bool {
        match (a, b) {
            (Value::Num(x), Value::Num(y)) => {
                x.to_bits() != y.to_bits() && !(x.is_nan() && y.is_nan())
            }
            _ => a != b,
        }
    }

    /// The values the input at `path` is nudged to on `inputs`: a slider step both ways and the
    /// slider's ends for a number, a step both ways for a count, every other choice for a
    /// selector, two grades and a blank for a grade; none for a part name or an unset number
    /// (no pick sets either).
    fn nudges(inputs: &DesignInputs, path: &str) -> Vec<Value> {
        let row = input_rows(inputs)
            .into_iter()
            .find(|r| r.path == path)
            .expect("an input");
        match row.value {
            Value::Int(code) if !row.meta.choices.is_empty() => row
                .meta
                .choices
                .iter()
                .map(|&(c, _)| c)
                .filter(|&c| c != code)
                .map(Value::Int)
                .collect(),
            Value::Int(n) => {
                let step = row.meta.range.expect("a count has a slider").step as i64;
                vec![Value::Int(n + step), Value::Int(n - step)]
            }
            Value::Num(x) => {
                let r = row.meta.range.expect("a number has a slider");
                [x + r.step, x - r.step, r.min, r.max]
                    .into_iter()
                    .filter(|&y| y != x)
                    .map(Value::Num)
                    .collect()
            }
            Value::Text(_) if row.meta.name.starts_with("grade_") => ["N52", "Y30", ""]
                .map(|g| Value::Text(g.to_owned()))
                .to_vec(),
            Value::Text(_) | Value::None => Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Whether some nudge of the input at `path` changes some result of `inputs`, whose
    /// results are `base`.
    fn moves_a_result(inputs: &DesignInputs, base: &[ResultRow], path: &str) -> bool {
        nudges(inputs, path).into_iter().any(|value| {
            let mut nudged = inputs.clone();
            nudged.set(path, value).is_ok()
                && result_rows(&compute_all(&nudged))
                    .iter()
                    .zip(base)
                    .any(|(a, b)| changed(&a.value, &b.value))
        })
    }

    /// Every pick off its default, one at a time: each other back-iron, sleeve-and-liner and
    /// cap choice; then the inner ring, the outer ring and both on custom dimensions, with a
    /// grade and without.
    fn pick_designs() -> Vec<(String, DesignInputs)> {
        let mut designs = Vec::new();
        for (pick, choices) in [
            (BACK_IRON_PICK, &BACK_IRON_CHOICES[..]),
            (SLEEVE_LINER_PICK, &SLEEVE_LINER_CHOICES[..]),
            (CAP_PICK, &CAP_HOUSING_CHOICES[..]),
        ] {
            for &(code, id) in &choices[1..] {
                let mut inputs = DesignInputs::default();
                inputs.set(pick, Value::Int(code)).unwrap();
                designs.push((format!("{pick} = {id}"), inputs));
            }
        }
        for grade in ["Y30", ""] {
            for rings in [&RINGS[..1], &RINGS[1..], &RINGS[..]] {
                let mut inputs = DesignInputs::default();
                for ring in rings {
                    inputs.set(ring.part, Value::Text(String::new())).unwrap();
                    inputs
                        .set(ring.grade, Value::Text(grade.to_owned()))
                        .unwrap();
                }
                let parts: Vec<&str> = rings.iter().map(|r| r.part).collect();
                designs.push((format!("custom {parts:?}, grade {grade:?}"), inputs));
            }
        }
        designs
    }

    /// The inputs a pick sets on `inputs`, with the pick.
    fn held(inputs: &DesignInputs) -> BTreeSet<(String, &'static str)> {
        input_rows(inputs)
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|r| set_by_pick(inputs, &r.path).map(|pick| (r.path, pick)))
            .collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_path_named_here_is_an_input() {
        let paths: BTreeSet<String> = input_rows(&DesignInputs::default())
            .into_iter()
            .map(|r| r.path)
            .collect();
        let named = STEEL_INPUTS
            .iter()
            .chain(&SLEEVE_LINER_INPUTS)
            .chain(&[
                DESIGN_FLUX_INPUT,
                CIRCUIT_INPUT,
                BACK_IRON_PICK,
                SLEEVE_LINER_PICK,
            ])
            .copied()
            .chain(
                RINGS
                    .iter()
                    .flat_map(|r| [r.part, r.grade].into_iter().chain(r.manual)),
            );
        for path in named {
            assert!(paths.contains(path), "{path}");
        }
    }

    fn at_the_default_design_only_the_library_parts_set_inputs() {
        let (inner, outer) = ("coupling.magnets.part_inner", "coupling.magnets.part_outer");
        let want: BTreeSet<(String, &str)> = [
            ("coupling.magnets.manual_inner_length_mm", inner),

    #[test]
    fn each_material_pick_names_what_it_sets() {
        let back_iron = |code: i64| {
            let mut inputs = DesignInputs::default();
            inputs.materials.parts.back_iron = code;
            inputs
        };
        let set = |inputs: &DesignInputs, pick: &str| -> BTreeSet<String> {
            held(inputs)
                .into_iter()
                .filter(|(_, p)| *p == pick)
                .map(|(path, _)| path)
                .collect()
        };
        let strings = |paths: &[&str]| -> BTreeSet<String> {
            paths.iter().map(|p| (*p).to_owned()).collect()
        };
        for &(code, id) in &BACK_IRON_CHOICES[1..] {
            let material = chosen(&BACK_IRON_CHOICES, code).unwrap();
            let mut want = if material.ferromagnetic {
                strings(&STEEL_INPUTS)
            } else {
                strings(&[CIRCUIT_INPUT])
            };
            if material.design_flux_density_T.is_some() {
                want.insert(DESIGN_FLUX_INPUT.to_owned());
            }
            assert_eq!(set(&back_iron(code), BACK_IRON_PICK), want, "{id}");
        }
        // 1018 is the one steel with a design flux density of its own; 304 and 6061 are the two
        // non-ferromagnetic picks.
        assert!(set(&back_iron(2), BACK_IRON_PICK).contains(DESIGN_FLUX_INPUT));
        assert_eq!(
            set(&back_iron(7), BACK_IRON_PICK),
            strings(&[CIRCUIT_INPUT])
        );
        for &(code, id) in &SLEEVE_LINER_CHOICES[1..] {
            let mut inputs = DesignInputs::default();
            inputs.materials.parts.sleeve_liner = code;
            assert_eq!(
                set(&inputs, SLEEVE_LINER_PICK),
                strings(&SLEEVE_LINER_INPUTS),
                "{id}"
            );
        }
        for &(code, _) in &CAP_HOUSING_CHOICES[1..] {
            let mut inputs = DesignInputs::default();
            inputs.materials.parts.cap_housing = code;
            assert_eq!(
                held(&inputs),
                held(&DesignInputs::default()),
                "the cap sets nothing"
            );
        }
        // A grade on custom dimensions supplies the Br; the dimensions stay the user's.
        let mut y30 = DesignInputs::default();
        y30.coupling.magnets.part_inner.clear();
        y30.coupling.magnets.grade_inner = "Y30".to_owned();
        assert_eq!(
            set(&y30, "coupling.magnets.grade_inner"),
            strings(&["coupling.magnets.manual_inner_br_T"])
        );
        assert!(set(&y30, "coupling.magnets.part_inner").is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_code_outside_the_choices_sets_nothing() {
        let mut inputs = DesignInputs::default();
        inputs.materials.parts.back_iron = 99;
        inputs.materials.parts.sleeve_liner = 99;
        for path in STEEL_INPUTS
            .iter()
            .chain(&SLEEVE_LINER_INPUTS)
            .chain(&[DESIGN_FLUX_INPUT, CIRCUIT_INPUT])
        {
            assert_eq!(set_by_pick(&inputs, path), None, "{path}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn no_input_a_pick_sets_moves_a_result() {
        let mut designs = pick_designs();
        designs.push(("defaults".to_owned(), DesignInputs::default()));
        let failures: Vec<String> = std::thread::scope(|s| {
            let handles: Vec<_> = designs
                .iter()
                .map(|(label, inputs)| {
                    s.spawn(move || {
                        let base = result_rows(&compute_all(inputs));
                        held(inputs)
                            .into_iter()
                            .filter(|(path, _)| moves_a_result(inputs, &base, path))
                            .map(|(path, pick)| {
                                format!("{label}: {pick} sets {path}, yet it moves a result")
                            })
                            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                    })
                })
                .collect();
            handles
                .into_iter()
                .flat_map(|h| h.join().expect("a design's thread"))
                .collect()
        });
        assert!(failures.is_empty(), "{failures:#?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_input_a_pick_leaves_without_effect_is_named() {
        let defaults = DesignInputs::default();
        let base = result_rows(&compute_all(&defaults));
        let live: Vec<String> = input_rows(&defaults)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|r| r.path)
            .filter(|path| moves_a_result(&defaults, &base, path))
            .collect();
        for path in UNUSED_WITHOUT_STEEL {
            assert!(
                live.iter().any(|p| p == path),
                "{path} moves a result at the defaults"
            );
        }
        let designs = pick_designs();
        let failures: Vec<String> = std::thread::scope(|s| {
            let handles: Vec<_> = designs
                .iter()
                .map(|(label, inputs)| {
                    let live = &live;
                    s.spawn(move || {
                        let base = result_rows(&compute_all(inputs));
                        let free_space =
                            chosen(&BACK_IRON_CHOICES, inputs.materials.parts.back_iron)
                                .is_some_and(|m| !m.ferromagnetic);
                        let mut failures = Vec::new();
                        for path in live {
                            let unused =
                                free_space && UNUSED_WITHOUT_STEEL.contains(&path.as_str());
                            let named = set_by_pick(inputs, path).is_some();
                            let moves = moves_a_result(inputs, &base, path);
                            if !moves && !named && !unused {
                                failures.push(format!(
                                    "{label}: {path} moves nothing, and no pick is named for it"
                                ));
                            }
                            if unused && moves {
                                failures.push(format!(
                                    "{label}: {path} is listed unused, yet it moves a result"
                                ));
                            }
                        }
                        failures
                    })
                })
                .collect();
            handles
                .into_iter()
                .flat_map(|h| h.join().expect("a design's thread"))
                .collect()
        });
        assert!(failures.is_empty(), "{failures:#?}");
    }
}
```

```rust
use super::api::DesignInputs;
use super::grades;
use super::library;
use super::material_library::{BACK_IRON_CHOICES, SLEEVE_LINER_CHOICES, chosen};

/// The back-iron pick: the hub, cup and boss material.
pub const BACK_IRON_PICK: &str = "materials.parts.back_iron";

/// The sleeve-and-liner pick.
pub const SLEEVE_LINER_PICK: &str = "materials.parts.sleeve_liner";

/// The steel values a ferromagnetic back-iron pick other than the default supplies from the
/// library in place of these inputs: density, conductivity, specific heat, expansion and
/// modulus.
const STEEL_INPUTS: [&str; 5] = [
    "metal.steel_density_g_mm3",
    "materials.steel.conductivity_S_m",
    "materials.steel.specific_heat_J_kgK",
    "materials.steel.cte_per_C",
    "materials.steel.modulus_GPa",
];

/// The wall check's design flux density: a back-iron pick with a design flux density of its
/// own (in the library, 1018) supplies it.
const DESIGN_FLUX_INPUT: &str = "materials.steel.bsat_T";

/// The circuit selector: a non-ferromagnetic back-iron pick selects the free-space circuit
/// whatever it says.
const CIRCUIT_INPUT: &str = "coupling.backiron";

/// The sleeve and liner values a pick other than the default supplies: density, conductivity
/// and specific heat.
const SLEEVE_LINER_INPUTS: [&str; 3] = [
    "metal.sleeve_density_g_mm3",
    "temperature.slip_loss.sigma_316_S_m",
    "temperature.thermal.c_316",
];

/// One magnet ring's inputs: its part and its grade, and the manual fields a library part
/// replaces (length, width, thickness, then Br).
struct Ring {
    part: &'static str,
    grade: &'static str,
    manual: [&'static str; 4],
}

/// The inner ring, then the outer ring.
const RINGS: [Ring; 2] = [
    Ring {
        part: "coupling.magnets.part_inner",
        grade: "coupling.magnets.grade_inner",
        manual: [
            "coupling.magnets.manual_inner_length_mm",
            "coupling.magnets.manual_inner_width_mm",
            "coupling.magnets.manual_inner_thickness_mm",
            "coupling.magnets.manual_inner_br_T",
        ],
    },
    Ring {
        part: "coupling.magnets.part_outer",
        grade: "coupling.magnets.grade_outer",
        manual: [
            "coupling.magnets.manual_outer_length_mm",
            "coupling.magnets.manual_outer_width_mm",
            "coupling.magnets.manual_outer_thickness_mm",
            "coupling.magnets.manual_outer_br_T",
        ],
    },
];

/// The pick input whose current choice on `inputs` sets the input at `path` in place of its
/// own value, or `None` when no pick does:
///
/// - a back-iron pick other than the default (4140): a ferromagnetic one supplies the steel's
///   density, conductivity, specific heat, expansion and modulus; a non-ferromagnetic one (304,
///   6061) selects the free-space circuit, so the Back iron selector has no effect; either
///   supplies the wall check's design flux density where the library has one (1018);
/// - a sleeve-and-liner pick other than the default (316L): their density, conductivity and
///   specific heat;
/// - a ring's library part: its manual dimensions, its manual Br and its grade; with no
///   library part, a grade of the grade table: its manual Br.
///
/// The cap pick sets no input on its own (the hub, cup and boss still read the aluminium
/// values it replaces for the cap), and a selector code outside its choices sets none (the
/// results are then not numbers, and validation names the code).
pub fn set_by_pick(inputs: &DesignInputs, path: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let parts = &inputs.materials.parts;
    if parts.back_iron != BACK_IRON_CHOICES[0].0
        && let Some(material) = chosen(&BACK_IRON_CHOICES, parts.back_iron)
    {
        let own = if material.ferromagnetic {
            STEEL_INPUTS.contains(&path)
        } else {
            path == CIRCUIT_INPUT
        };
        let flux = path == DESIGN_FLUX_INPUT && material.design_flux_density_T.is_some();
        if own || flux {
            return Some(BACK_IRON_PICK);
        }
    }
    if parts.sleeve_liner != SLEEVE_LINER_CHOICES[0].0
        && chosen(&SLEEVE_LINER_CHOICES, parts.sleeve_liner).is_some()
        && SLEEVE_LINER_INPUTS.contains(&path)
    {
        return Some(SLEEVE_LINER_PICK);
    }
    let magnets = &inputs.coupling.magnets;
    let picked = [
        (&magnets.part_inner, &magnets.grade_inner),
        (&magnets.part_outer, &magnets.grade_outer),
    ];
    for (ring, (part, grade)) in RINGS.iter().zip(picked) {
        let [.., br] = ring.manual;
        if library::lookup(part).is_some() {
            if path == ring.grade || ring.manual.contains(&path) {
                return Some(ring.part);
            }
        } else if grades::grade(grade).is_some() && path == br {
            return Some(ring.grade);
        }
    }
    None
}
```

```rust
/// Whether Auto holds the input at `path` on `state`: in Torque -> Magnets, one of the inputs
/// the design shown sets ([`set_by_auto`]). Its row is locked at the value shown, and a teaching
/// note's change entry draws it as plain text, "held by Auto".
pub(crate) fn held_by_auto(state: &SizingState, path: &str) -> bool {
    state.mode == SizingMode::TorqueToMagnets && set_by_auto(state.variable).any(|p| p == path)
}
```

```rust
    /// One frame of `note` drawn against `view` with `events`: what egui painted and the link a
    /// click asked for.
    fn note_frame(
        ctx: &egui::Context,
        note: &Note,
        view: &NoteView<'_>,
        events: Vec<egui::Event>,
    ) -> (egui::FullOutput, Option<NoteLink>) {
        use crate::gui::test_support::{SCREEN, sized_frame};
        let mut link = None;
        let output = sized_frame(ctx, SCREEN, events, |ui| {
            if let Some(clicked) = note_ui(ui, note, view) {
                link = Some(clicked);
            }
        });
        (output, link)
    }

    /// Clicks the first drawn text equal to `text` (move, press, release): the link the click
    /// asked for, and a frame drawn once a fold the click opened has settled.
    fn click_in_note(
        ctx: &egui::Context,
        note: &Note,
        view: &NoteView<'_>,
        text: &str,
    ) -> (Option<NoteLink>, egui::FullOutput) {
        use crate::gui::test_support::{primary_button, text_rect};
        let (output, _) = note_frame(ctx, note, view, Vec::new());
        // A text in a wrapped row is laid out from the row's start, so the left part of its rect
        // covers the widgets before it on that row: click its last character.
        let rect = text_rect(&output, text).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no text {text:?}"));
        let at = egui::pos2(rect.max.x - 2.0, rect.center().y);
        note_frame(ctx, note, view, vec![egui::Event::PointerMoved(at)]);
        note_frame(ctx, note, view, vec![primary_button(at, true)]);
        let (_, link) = note_frame(ctx, note, view, vec![primary_button(at, false)]);
        let mut output = note_frame(ctx, note, view, Vec::new()).0;
        for _ in 0..15 {
            output = note_frame(ctx, note, view, Vec::new()).0;
        }
        (link, output)
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_note_draws_its_parts_in_order_with_its_sources_folded_until_clicked() {
        use crate::gui::test_support::{drawn_texts, text_color, text_rect};
        let ctx = egui::Context::default();
        let (inputs, results) = design();
        let view = NoteView {
            inputs: &inputs,
            results: &results,
            held: &nothing_held,
        };
        note_frame(&ctx, &RENDER_NOTE, &view, Vec::new());
        let (output, _) = note_frame(&ctx, &RENDER_NOTE, &view, Vec::new());
        let texts = drawn_texts(&output);
        let count = |text: &str| texts.iter().filter(|t| *t == text).count();
        let once = [RENDER_NOTE.title, WHAT_TO_CHANGE, WATCH_OUT, WHERE_FROM]
            .into_iter()
            .chain(RENDER_NOTE.sentences.iter().copied())
            .chain(RENDER_NOTE.watch_out.iter().copied());
        for text in once {
            assert_eq!(count(text), 1, "{text}");
        }
        for change in RENDER_NOTE.change {
            assert_eq!(
                count(&format!("{} ", change.step.word())),
                1,
                "{}",
                change.input
            );
            assert_eq!(count(label_for(change.input)), 1, "{}", change.input);
            assert_eq!(count(&format!(": {}", change.text)), 1, "{}", change.input);
        }
        for source in RENDER_NOTE.sources {
            assert_eq!(count(source), 0, "the fold starts closed: {source}");
        }
        // Top to bottom: what it is, what to change, watch out, where this comes from.
        let top = |text: &str| text_rect(&output, text).unwrap().min.y;
        let order = [
            RENDER_NOTE.sentences[1],
            WHAT_TO_CHANGE,
            label_for(RENDER_NOTE.change[2].input),
            WATCH_OUT,
            RENDER_NOTE.watch_out[1],
            WHERE_FROM,
        ];
        for pair in order.windows(2) {
            assert!(top(pair[0]) < top(pair[1]), "{pair:?}");
        }
        let warn = ctx.style().visuals.warn_fg_color;
        for line in RENDER_NOTE.watch_out {
            assert_eq!(text_color(&output, line), Some(warn), "{line}");
        }
        let (link, output) = click_in_note(&ctx, &RENDER_NOTE, &view, WHERE_FROM);
        assert_eq!(link, None, "the fold is no link to an input");
        let texts = drawn_texts(&output);
        for source in RENDER_NOTE.sources {
            assert!(texts.iter().any(|t| t == source), "{source}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_entry_whose_input_cannot_move_its_way_names_why() {
        use crate::engine::explain::notes::Step;
        let range = |path: &str| {
            InputCatalogue::get()
                .entry(path)
                .unwrap()
                .meta
                .range
                .unwrap()
        };
        let entry = |input, step| Change {
            input,
            step,
            aim: None,
            text: "",
        };
        let reason = |inputs: &DesignInputs, change: &Change| {
            let results = compute_all(inputs);
            let view = NoteView {
                inputs,
                results: &results,
                held: &nothing_held,
            };
            unlinked_reason(change, &view)
        };
        let gap = "metal.face_gap_mm";
        let (lowest, highest) = (range(gap).min, range(gap).max);
        let mut inputs = DesignInputs::default();
        assert_eq!(reason(&inputs, &entry(gap, Step::Raise)), None);
        assert_eq!(reason(&inputs, &entry(gap, Step::Lower)), None);
        inputs.set(gap, Value::Num(highest)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            reason(&inputs, &entry(gap, Step::Raise)).as_deref(),
            Some(AT_TOP)
        );
        assert_eq!(reason(&inputs, &entry(gap, Step::Lower)), None);
        inputs.set(gap, Value::Num(lowest)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            reason(&inputs, &entry(gap, Step::Lower)).as_deref(),
            Some(AT_BOTTOM)
        );
        assert_eq!(reason(&inputs, &entry(gap, Step::Raise)), None);
        // A count at its end; a choice and a blank optional number are never at an end.
        let mut poles = DesignInputs::default();
        poles.coupling.npole = range("coupling.npole").max as i64;
        assert_eq!(
            reason(&poles, &entry("coupling.npole", Step::Raise)).as_deref(),
            Some(AT_TOP)
        );
        let defaults = DesignInputs::default();
        assert_eq!(
            reason(&defaults, &entry("materials.parts.back_iron", Step::Choose)),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            reason(
                &defaults,
                &entry("coupling.magnets.axial_length_mm", Step::Raise)
            ),
            None
        );
        // A held input names why it is held, whatever its slider says.
        let held = |_: &str| Some(HELD_BY_AUTO.to_owned());
        let results = compute_all(&inputs);
        let view = NoteView {
            inputs: &inputs,
            results: &results,
            held: &held,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            unlinked_reason(&entry(gap, Step::Lower), &view).as_deref(),
            Some(HELD_BY_AUTO)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn held_reason_names_auto_and_the_pick_that_sets_an_input() {
        use crate::engine::explain::plain::plain_text_violations;
        use crate::engine::picks::BACK_IRON_PICK;
        use crate::engine::sizing::FreeVariable;
        use crate::gui::sizing::SizingMode;
        let inputs = DesignInputs::default();
        let off = SizingState::default();
        let auto = SizingState {
            mode: SizingMode::TorqueToMagnets,
            variable: FreeVariable::AxialLength,
        };
        let length = FreeVariable::AxialLength.path();
        assert_eq!(held_reason(&off, &inputs, length), None);
        assert_eq!(
            held_reason(&auto, &inputs, length).as_deref(),
            Some(HELD_BY_AUTO)
        );
        assert_eq!(held_reason(&auto, &inputs, "metal.face_gap_mm"), None);
        let part_pick = format!(
            "set by the {} pick",
            label_for("coupling.magnets.part_inner")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            held_reason(&off, &inputs, "coupling.magnets.manual_inner_br_T"),
            Some(part_pick.clone())
        );
        let steel = "materials.steel.cte_per_C";
        assert_eq!(held_reason(&off, &inputs, steel), None);
        let mut picked = inputs.clone();
        picked.materials.parts.back_iron = 2;
        let steel_pick = format!("set by the {} pick", label_for(BACK_IRON_PICK));
        assert_eq!(held_reason(&off, &picked, steel), Some(steel_pick.clone()));
        for reason in [
            HELD_BY_AUTO.to_owned(),
            part_pick,
            steel_pick,
            AT_TOP.into(),
            AT_BOTTOM.into(),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(
                plain_text_violations(&reason),
                Vec::<&str>::new(),
                "{reason}"
            );
        }
    }
```

with:

```rust
/// What a note's change entries are drawn against: the design shown, its results, and why an
/// input is not free on it (`held`: Auto holds it or a part pick sets it, [`held_reason`];
/// `None` for a free input).
pub struct NoteView<'a> {
    pub inputs: &'a DesignInputs,
    pub results: &'a DesignResults,
    pub held: &'a dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>,
}

/// What a click in a teaching note asks for.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum NoteLink {
    /// Highlight this input's row, as a leaf term does ([`Explorer::follow_note_link`]).
    Input(&'static str),
}

/// Why the input at `path` is not free on the design `inputs` shown with `sizing`, for a note's
/// change entry ([`NoteView::held`]): Auto sets it in Torque -> Magnets ([`HELD_BY_AUTO`]), or
/// a part pick sets it in place of its own value ("set by the <pick's label> pick",
/// [`set_by_pick`]); `None` when it is free.
pub fn held_reason(sizing: &SizingState, inputs: &DesignInputs, path: &str) -> Option<String> {
    if held_by_auto(sizing, path) {
        return Some(HELD_BY_AUTO.to_owned());
    }
    set_by_pick(inputs, path).map(|pick| format!("set by the {} pick", label_for(pick)))
}

/// Why a change entry draws its input as plain text on `view`'s design: the input is not free
/// there (`view.held`), or one more slider step its way is past its slider ([`AT_TOP`],
/// [`AT_BOTTOM`]; the step a check guide's fix takes, `SliderRange::step_from`). `None` when the
/// input is a link: a choice, and an optional number left blank (it enters at a result), are
/// never at an end.
fn unlinked_reason(change: &Change, view: &NoteView<'_>) -> Option<String> {
    if let Some(reason) = (view.held)(change.input) {
        return Some(reason);
    }
    let up = change.step.up()?;
    let range = InputCatalogue::get().entry(change.input)?.meta.range?;
    let x = match view.inputs.get(change.input)? {
        Value::Num(x) if x.is_finite() => x,
        Value::Int(n) => n as f64,
        _ => return None,
    };
    if range.step_from(x, up).is_some() {
        return None;
    }
    Some(if up { AT_TOP } else { AT_BOTTOM }.to_owned())
}

/// A teaching note (slice-2 spec 3.1): its title; what it is (its sentences) and its diagram;
/// "What to change", each entry "<Step> <input's label>: <text>", the label a link to the
/// input's row unless `unlinked_reason` gives a reason (then plain text with the reason);
/// "Watch out" and its lines; and the "Where this comes from" fold, closed until clicked,
/// holding its sources. Every text is drawn through `glyph_safe`. Returns the link clicked.
pub fn note_ui(ui: &mut egui::Ui, note: &Note, view: &NoteView<'_>) -> Option<NoteLink> {
    let mut clicked = None;
    ui.strong(glyph_safe(note.title));
    for sentence in note.sentences {
        ui.add(egui::Label::new(glyph_safe(sentence)).wrap());
    }
    if let Some(diagram) = note.diagram {
        diagram_ui(ui, diagram);
    }
    if !note.change.is_empty() {
        ui.strong(WHAT_TO_CHANGE);
        for change in note.change {
            if change_ui(ui, change, view) {
                clicked = Some(NoteLink::Input(change.input));
            }
        }
    }
    if !note.watch_out.is_empty() {
        let warn = ui.visuals().warn_fg_color;
        ui.label(egui::RichText::new(WATCH_OUT).strong().color(warn));
        for line in note.watch_out {
            ui.add(egui::Label::new(egui::RichText::new(glyph_safe(line)).color(warn)).wrap());
        }
    }
    egui::CollapsingHeader::new(WHERE_FROM)
        .id_salt(("magcoupling_note_sources", note.id))
        .default_open(false)
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            for source in note.sources {
                ui.add(
                    egui::Label::new(egui::RichText::new(glyph_safe(source)).small().weak()).wrap(),
                );
            }
        });
    clicked
}

/// One change entry on one wrapped line: its step word, its input's display label (a link, or
/// plain text and the reason), then ": " and its text. True when the link was clicked.
fn change_ui(ui: &mut egui::Ui, change: &Change, view: &NoteView<'_>) -> bool {
    let label = glyph_safe(label_for(change.input));
    let mut clicked = false;
    ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
        ui.spacing_mut().item_spacing.x = 0.0;
        ui.label(format!("{} ", change.step.word()));
        match unlinked_reason(change, view) {
            Some(reason) => {
                ui.label(label);
                ui.weak(format!(" ({reason})"));
            }
            None => clicked = ui.link(label).clicked(),
        }
        ui.add(egui::Label::new(format!(": {}", glyph_safe(change.text))).wrap());
    });
    clicked
}

fn note_alone_ui(
    ui: &mut egui::Ui,
    note: &Note,
    view: &NoteView<'_>,
) -> (Option<String>, Option<NoteLink>) {
```

```rust
        let mut harness = Harness::on_screen(egui::vec2(1280.0, 3000.0));
```

  this module, followed by one blank line:

```rust
/// The notes as they stood before guidance slice 2, for the owner's sign-off sheet (task T20):
/// the format of `docs/analyses/2026-10-14-magcoupler-notes-before.txt` and its reader. A
/// header line, then per note a heading `## <id>` and one `<field>: <text>` line per title,
/// sentence, watch-out and source (fields `title`, `sentence`, `watch out`, `source`), in that
/// order, and a blank line. Tests only.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod before {
    use super::NOTES;

    /// The current notes in the snapshot's format.
    pub(crate) fn snapshot_text() -> String {
        let mut text = String::from(
            "# Teaching notes before guidance slice 2 (the text of commit b0166ad), written once by notes::tests::notes_before_snapshot\n",
        );
        for n in NOTES {
            text.push_str(&format!("\n## {}\n", n.id));
            let mut line = |field: &str, value: &str| {
                assert!(
                    !value.contains('\n'),
                    "{}: a line break in its {field}",
                    n.id
                );
                text.push_str(&format!("{field}: {value}\n"));
            };
            line("title", n.title);
            for sentence in n.sentences {
                line("sentence", sentence);
            }
            for watch_out in n.watch_out {
                line("watch out", watch_out);
            }
            for source in n.sources {
                line("source", source);
            }
        }
        text
    }

    /// A snapshot read back: each note's id and its `(field, text)` lines, in order.
    pub(crate) fn parse(text: &str) -> Vec<(&str, Vec<(&str, &str)>)> {
        let mut notes: Vec<(&str, Vec<(&str, &str)>)> = Vec::new();
        for line in text.lines() {
            if let Some(id) = line.strip_prefix("## ") {
                notes.push((id, Vec::new()));
            } else if let (Some(field_text), Some(note)) = (line.split_once(": "), notes.last_mut())
            {
                note.1.push(field_text);
            }
        }
        notes
    }
}
```

#### Drafter notes

**Assumptions about other tasks.**
- T2 ships `gui::plain_text::label_for(path) -> &'static str`; for a pick input with no overlay row it
  returns the catalogue label ("Back iron material (hub, cup and boss)", "Inner magnet part"), so the
  pick reason reads "set by the Back iron material (hub, cup and boss) pick". T6 may give those inputs
  shorter display labels; the reason follows with no change here.
- T1 ships `engine::explain::plain::plain_text_violations` (one explorer test runs the reason texts
  through it).
- T3 may add a provenance parameter to `explorer_ui`, `equation_body` or `no_equation_body` (see the
  note at the top of the task). Nothing here draws provenance.
- T5 builds on `NoteView`, `note_ui`, `unlinked_reason`, the test helpers `nothing_held`,
  `note_frame` and `RENDER_NOTE`, and on `Step::up`, `SliderRange::step_from` and `set_by_pick`.
- T20's sign-off sheet reads the snapshot through `notes::before::{SNAPSHOT, parse}` (format: a header
  line, then per note a heading `## <id>` (the form T20's draft reads) and one `<field>: <text>` line
  per title, sentence, watch-out and source; fields `title`, `sentence`, `watch out`, `source`). New
  notes (T11, T14, T15) have no section.
- T18's `only_the_review_tools_are_ignored` must list `notes_before_snapshot` (in `notes.rs`) among
  its `TOOLS`: it only writes the snapshot, once. Its other ignored tests here carry the reason
  `"un-ignored in T18 when every note is rewritten"`, which T18 searches for.

**Decisions made here (each verified in the scratch replay).**
1. *Slider end.* Spec section 5 lists "at its slider end" beside Auto and the picks. The contract's
   `held` closure takes only a path, so the slider end is decided in `note_ui` from the entry's
   `Step`, with the same step a check guide's fix takes: the old private `guidance::step` became
   `SliderRange::step_from` (one rule; the guidance suite passes unchanged). Reasons: "at the top of
   its range", "at the bottom of its range". A choice and a blank optional number are never at an end.
2. *Picks live in the engine* (`engine::picks`), so T5's engine-only aim test can skip a held input.
   The rules were found by nudging every input on every pick, then written as `set_by_pick`; two
   tests keep them true: every input it names moves no result on any pick, and every input a pick
   leaves without effect is named (or listed in `UNUSED_WITHOUT_STEEL`: the steel circuit's stored
   slip fields, which 304 or 6061 leaves unused as "no back iron" does; they are not "set by the
   pick", so a note never says so). Findings: 2-6 (steels) hold the five steel values, 1018 also the
   design flux density; 304 and 6061 hold only the circuit selector (the steel inputs stay live); the
   cap pick holds nothing on its own; a library part holds its ring's four manual fields and grade; a
   grade on custom dimensions holds the manual Br.
3. *Auto.* `held_by_auto` is the rule `input_row_ui` used inline (`mode == TorqueToMagnets &&
   set_by_auto(variable)`), now shared, so the locked row and the note's reason cannot disagree.
4. *Layout.* The diagram moves up under the sentences (it illustrates "what it is"); "Watch out" is a
   heading over its lines in the warning colour (was "Watch out: <text>" in one label). Sentence 0 is
   still one label, so the three tests that count it raw still pass.
5. *Snapshot timing.* It is written after the mechanical conversion. Step 6 proves the conversion
   moved no text, and the counts in Step 30 match b0166ad (17 notes, 61 sentences, 10 watch-outs, 46
   sources). The writer refuses to overwrite.
6. *Test clicks.* egui lays a label in a wrapped row out from the row's start, so its rect covers the
   widgets before it; the test helper clicks a text's last character. The link itself is hit
   correctly (found while writing the tests).

**Risks.** CRLF working tree: the Step 6 grep relies on `git diff` printing LF lines (it does with
`core.autocrlf=true`). `include_str!` in `notes.rs` (test builds only) needs the committed file; a
checkout without `docs/analyses/` fails `cargo test` at compile time, which is the intent.

**Open questions, with my proposed ruling.**
- Q1. Are `temperature.demag.hcj20_kA_m` and `beta_hcj_per_C` "held"? While every ring has a grade and
  the coercivity choice reads "magnet grade" (the defaults), they move nothing, but no part pick sets
  them. Ruling: not in T4. If T16 writes an entry on them, it uses `Choose temperature.demag.coercivity_source`
  instead, or extends `set_by_pick` and its tests with the coercivity designs.
- Q2. Should the reason name the pick's chosen material ("set by the 1018 hot rolled pick")? Ruling:
  no; the contract text names the picker label. Revisit in T6 with the display labels.

**Review Focus candidates (an input or condition no test here exercises that would bite a user).**
- RF1. Auto on (Torque -> Magnets, axial length free) and a shipped note whose entry names the axial

- RF2. A part pick on a shipped note (for example a 1018 back iron and an a5 note entry on a steel

- RF3. A narrow Equation panel (about 400 points wide): a long entry wraps and its link must still

- RF4. A change link clicked while the Size tab is shown: the inputs side opens "Detailed inputs" for

```rust
/// What a placeholder reads where its result has no prediction on the design shown.
pub const NO_VALUE: &str = "no prediction";

/// A piece of note text: literal text, or the path of the result whose value stands there.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Segment<'a> {
    Text(&'a str),
    Value(&'a str),
}

/// `text` split into literal text and placeholders, in order (no empty literal piece). The
/// error names the first fault: a `}` with no `{` before it, a `{` with no `}` after it or with
/// another `{` inside, an empty `{}`, or a placeholder that is not a path (ASCII letters,
/// digits, `_`, `.`, `[` and `]` only, so a formula such as `{= a / b}` is refused).
pub fn segments(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Segment<'_>>, String> {
    let mut pieces = Vec::new();
    let mut rest = text;
    while let Some(open) = rest.find(['{', '}']) {
        if rest[open..].starts_with('}') {
            return Err(format!("a '}}' with no '{{' before it in {text:?}"));
        }
        if open > 0 {
            pieces.push(Segment::Text(&rest[..open]));
        }
        let after = &rest[open + 1..];
        let close = match after.find(['{', '}']) {
            Some(i) if after[i..].starts_with('}') => i,
            Some(_) => return Err(format!("a '{{' inside a placeholder in {text:?}")),
            None => return Err(format!("a '{{' with no '}}' after it in {text:?}")),
        };
        let path = &after[..close];
        if path.is_empty() {
            return Err(format!("an empty placeholder in {text:?}"));
        }
        let path_byte = |b: u8| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(b, b'_' | b'.' | b'[' | b']');
        if !path.bytes().all(path_byte) {
            return Err(format!("{{{path}}} is not a result path, in {text:?}"));
        }
        pieces.push(Segment::Value(path));
        rest = &after[close + 1..];
    }
    if !rest.is_empty() {
        pieces.push(Segment::Text(rest));
    }
    Ok(pieces)
}

/// `text` with each placeholder replaced by `value(path)`, or by [`NO_VALUE`] where that is
/// `None`. A text [`segments`] refuses comes back as it is (the note tests refuse it first).
pub fn render(text: &str, value: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>) -> String {
    match segments(text) {
        Ok(pieces) => pieces
            .into_iter()
            .map(|piece| match piece {
                Segment::Text(literal) => literal.to_owned(),
                Segment::Value(path) => value(path).unwrap_or_else(|| NO_VALUE.to_owned()),
            })
            .collect(),
        Err(_) => text.to_owned(),
    }
}

/// The texts of `note` drawn with live values: its sentences, its change entries' texts, then
/// its watch-outs, in that order.
pub fn rendered_texts(note: &Note) -> Vec<&'static str> {
    let (sentences, change, watch_out) = (note.sentences, note.change, note.watch_out);
    sentences
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .chain(change.iter().map(|c| c.text))
        .chain(watch_out.iter().copied())
        .collect()
}

/// Every placeholder's path in `note`'s [`rendered_texts`], in order, as often as it appears
/// (a text [`segments`] refuses adds none; the note tests refuse it).
pub fn placeholders(note: &Note) -> Vec<&'static str> {
    rendered_texts(note)
        .into_iter()
        .flat_map(|text| segments(text).unwrap_or_default())
        .filter_map(|piece| match piece {
            Segment::Value(path) => Some(path),
            Segment::Text(_) => None,
        })
        .collect()
}
```

```rust
//! The five probe designs (guidance slice 2, spec 3.2): where the note tests and each note's
//! physics review read every note, so a sentence true only at the defaults shows. Also the
//! move those checks make: one slider step of one input ([`step_input`]). Pure std: the engine
//! tests (`tests/explain.rs`) and the GUI tests (`gui::explorer`) both use them.

use super::notes::Step;
use crate::engine::api::{DesignInputs, OPTIONAL_SEEDS, compute_all};
use crate::engine::material_library::BACK_IRON_CHOICES;
use crate::engine::meta::{InputSet, ResultSet, Value, input_rows};
use crate::engine::picks::set_by_pick;
use crate::engine::size_controls::with_ring_radius;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::engine::grades;
    use crate::engine::material_library::chosen;
    use crate::engine::meta::SliderRange;
    use crate::engine::size_controls::dimensions;
    use crate::engine::sizing::is_valid;

    /// The slider of the input at `path`.
    fn slider(path: &str) -> SliderRange {
        input_rows(&DesignInputs::default())
            .into_iter()
            .find(|r| r.path == path)
            .and_then(|r| r.meta.range)
            .expect("an input with a slider")
    }

    /// A finite number result.
    fn number(design: &DesignInputs, path: &str) -> f64 {
        match compute_all(design).get(path) {
            Some(Value::Num(x)) if x.is_finite() => x,
            other => panic!("{path}: {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_probes_are_the_five_designs_their_names_say() {
        let designs = probe_designs();
        let names: Vec<&str> = designs.iter().map(|(name, _)| *name).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, PROBE_NAMES);
        let default = DesignInputs::default();
        let [magnets, back_iron, ferrite, ring] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(|i| &designs[i].1);
        assert_eq!(designs[0].1, default);
        // The count alone changes.
        assert_eq!(magnets.coupling.npole, PROBE_MAGNETS);
        let mut back = magnets.clone();
        back.coupling.npole = default.coupling.npole;
        assert_eq!(back, default);
        // A non-ferromagnetic pick: the free-space circuit is in effect.
        let pick = chosen(&BACK_IRON_CHOICES, back_iron.materials.parts.back_iron).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(pick.id, PROBE_BACK_IRON);
        assert!(!pick.ferromagnetic);
        assert_eq!(
            compute_all(back_iron).get("materials.circuit_backiron"),
            Some(Value::Int(0))
        );
        // Both rings in the grade mode, with the grade's remanence, and the cold check runs.
        let y30 = grades::grade(PROBE_GRADE).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(number(ferrite, "model.inner_br_T"), y30.br_T);
        assert_eq!(number(ferrite, "model.outer_br_T"), y30.br_T);
        assert!(number(ferrite, "temperature.demag.cold_limit_C").is_finite());
        // The ring radius as the Size tab sets it: the cap follows the cup.
        assert_eq!(ring.coupling.inner_back_apothem_mm, PROBE_RING_RADIUS_MM);
        assert!(ring.metal.cap_od_mm > default.metal.cap_od_mm);
        assert_eq!(
            with_ring_radius(&default, PROBE_RING_RADIUS_MM).as_ref(),
            Some(ring)
        );

        let default = DesignInputs::default();
        let gap = "metal.face_gap_mm";
        let lower = step_input(&default, gap, Step::Lower).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            lower.metal.face_gap_mm,
            default.metal.face_gap_mm - slider(gap).step
        );
        let mut back = lower.clone();
        back.metal.face_gap_mm = default.metal.face_gap_mm;
        assert_eq!(back, default, "nothing else moves");
        let raise = step_input(&default, gap, Step::Raise).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            raise.metal.face_gap_mm,

        );
        assert_eq!(
            step_input(&default, "no.such.input", Step::Raise),
            Err(Unmoved::NoSuchInput)
        );
        for not_a_number in ["materials.parts.back_iron", "coupling.magnets.part_inner"] {
            assert_eq!(
                step_input(&default, not_a_number, Step::Raise),

        assert_eq!(

                &default,
                "coupling.magnets.manual_inner_length_mm",

            ),

        );
        let mut top = default.clone();
        top.metal.face_gap_mm = slider(gap).max;
        assert_eq!(step_input(&top, gap, Step::Raise), Err(Unmoved::AtEnd));
        assert!(step_input(&top, gap, Step::Lower).is_ok());
        let (_, steel_304) = &probe_designs()[2];
        assert_eq!(
            step_input(steel_304, "coupling.backiron", Step::Raise),
            Err(Unmoved::Held("materials.parts.back_iron"))
        );
    }
}
```

```rust
pub const PROBE_NAMES: [&str; 5] = [
    "default",
    "8 magnets per ring",
    "304 back iron",
    "Y30 ferrite, custom dimensions",
    "20 mm ring radius",
];

/// free-space circuit is in effect.

/// The fourth probe's grade, on both rings with their manual dimensions: hard ferrite.
pub const PROBE_GRADE: &str = "Y30";

/// The fifth probe's ring radius (`coupling.inner_back_apothem_mm`) [mm]: a larger ring, at
/// the dip in torque between about 14 and 20 mm (spec section 8).
pub const PROBE_RING_RADIUS_MM: f64 = 20.0;

/// The five probe designs, named, in [`PROBE_NAMES`]' order: the default (Example) design; the
/// default at [`PROBE_MAGNETS`] magnets per ring; the default with a [`PROBE_BACK_IRON`] back
/// iron; [`PROBE_GRADE`] on both rings, on their custom (manual) dimensions; the default at a
/// [`PROBE_RING_RADIUS_MM`] ring radius, as the Size tab's Outside diameter slider sets it (the
/// cap OD and thread follow the cup: `size_controls::with_ring_radius`). Each computes, counts
/// for inverse sizing and draws on the Size tab (the tests check it).
pub fn probe_designs() -> Vec<(&'static str, DesignInputs)> {
    let default = DesignInputs::default();
    let mut magnets = default.clone();
    magnets.coupling.npole = PROBE_MAGNETS;
    let mut back_iron = default.clone();
    back_iron.materials.parts.back_iron = BACK_IRON_CHOICES
        .iter()
        .find(|&&(_, id)| id == PROBE_BACK_IRON)
        .map(|&(code, _)| code)
        .expect("304 stainless is a back-iron choice (the tests check it)");
    let mut ferrite = default.clone();
    ferrite.coupling.magnets.part_inner.clear();
    ferrite.coupling.magnets.part_outer.clear();
    ferrite.coupling.magnets.grade_inner = PROBE_GRADE.to_owned();
    ferrite.coupling.magnets.grade_outer = PROBE_GRADE.to_owned();
    let ring = with_ring_radius(&default, PROBE_RING_RADIUS_MM)
        .expect("the Size tab reaches a 20 mm ring radius from the default (the tests check it)");
    PROBE_NAMES
        .into_iter()
        .zip([default, magnets, back_iron, ferrite, ring])
        .collect()
}

/// Why [`step_input`] leaves an input where it is.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Unmoved {
    /// The entry chooses; it does not step.
    Choice,
    /// No input has the path.
    NoSuchInput,
    /// A part pick sets the input on this design ([`set_by_pick`]): the pick's input path.
    Held(&'static str),
    /// The input is no number with a slider here: a text, a selector, or an optional number
    /// left blank with no result to start from.
    NotANumber,
    /// One more step its way is past its slider (`SliderRange::step_from`).
    AtEnd,
}

/// `design` with the input at `path` one slider step up ([`Step::Raise`]) or down
/// ([`Step::Lower`]), as a check guide's fix moves it (`SliderRange::step_from`); every other
/// input keeps its value. A count stays a whole number. An optional number left blank starts
/// from the result it enters at (`api::OPTIONAL_SEEDS`, as its input row enters it).
pub fn step_input(design: &DesignInputs, path: &str, step: Step) -> Result<DesignInputs, Unmoved> {
    let up = step.up().ok_or(Unmoved::Choice)?;
    let row = input_rows(design)
        .into_iter()
        .find(|r| r.path == path)
        .ok_or(Unmoved::NoSuchInput)?;
    if let Some(pick) = set_by_pick(design, path) {
        return Err(Unmoved::Held(pick));
    }
    let range = row.meta.range.ok_or(Unmoved::NotANumber)?;
    let x = match row.value {
        Value::Num(x) => x,
        Value::Int(n) => n as f64,
        Value::None => {
            let (_, seed) = OPTIONAL_SEEDS
                .iter()
                .find(|(input, _)| *input == path)
                .ok_or(Unmoved::NotANumber)?;
            match compute_all(design).get(seed) {
                Some(Value::Num(x)) => x,
                _ => return Err(Unmoved::NotANumber),
            }
        }
        Value::Text(_) => return Err(Unmoved::NotANumber),
    };
    let next = range.step_from(x, up).ok_or(Unmoved::AtEnd)?;
    let value = match row.value {
        Value::Int(_) => Value::Int(next.round() as i64),
        _ => Value::Num(next),
    };
    let mut moved = design.clone();
    moved
        .set(path, value)
        .expect("a number on its slider is a value the input takes");
    Ok(moved)
}
```

```rust
    /// The per-note physics review's sheet (slice-2 spec section 4): each note, or each named
    /// in `NOTES_FOR_REVIEW` (ids, comma-separated), its title and sources once, then at each
    /// probe design its sentences, change entries and watch-outs as the panel draws them; a
    /// change entry with its input's display label, the reason it is not a link there, and
    /// its aim's value before and after one step. A text the parser refuses or the plain-words
    /// guard flags is marked "<<<". Written to `NOTES_REVIEW_OUT` (a path from `magcoupling-rs/`;
    /// default `target/notes-for-review.txt` there).
    #[test]
    #[ignore = "a review tool, not a check: NOTES_FOR_REVIEW=id1,id2 NOTES_REVIEW_OUT=<file> cargo test --manifest-path magcoupling-rs/Cargo.toml --features app --lib notes_for_review -- --ignored --nocapture"]
    fn notes_for_review() {
        use std::fmt::Write as _;

        use crate::engine::explain::note_text::segments;
        use crate::engine::explain::plain::plain_text_violations;
        use crate::engine::explain::probes::{probe_designs, step_input};
        let wanted: Vec<String> = std::env::var("NOTES_FOR_REVIEW")
            .map(|ids| {
                ids.split(',')
                    .map(|id| id.trim().to_owned())
                    .filter(|id| !id.is_empty())
                    .collect()
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let unknown: Vec<&String> = wanted
            .iter()
            .filter(|id| notes::note(id).is_none())
            .collect();
        assert!(
            unknown.is_empty(),
            "NOTES_FOR_REVIEW names no note: {unknown:?}"
        );
        let chosen: Vec<&Note> = notes::NOTES
            .iter()
            .filter(|n| wanted.is_empty() || wanted.iter().any(|id| id == n.id))
            .collect();
        let designs: Vec<(&str, DesignInputs, DesignResults)> = probe_designs()
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(name, inputs)| {
                let results = compute_all(&inputs);
                (name, inputs, results)
            })
            .collect();
        // A raw text the parser refuses, or a drawn text the guard flags, is marked.
        let marks = |raw: &str, drawn: &str| {
            let mut found = Vec::new();
            if let Err(fault) = segments(raw) {
                found.push(fault);
            }
            let banned = plain_text_violations(drawn);
            if !banned.is_empty() {
                found.push(format!("plain words: {banned:?}"));
            }
            if found.is_empty() {
                String::new()
            } else {
                format!("   <<< {}", found.join("; "))
            }
        };
        let sizing = SizingState::default();
        let mut sheet = String::new();
        for note in &chosen {
            let status = match note.review {
                Review::Draft => "Draft",
                Review::Reviewed { .. } => "Reviewed",
            };
            writeln!(sheet, "==== {} ({status})", note.id).unwrap();
            writeln!(
                sheet,
                "Title: {}{}",
                note.title,
                marks(note.title, note.title)
            )
            .unwrap();
            writeln!(sheet, "{WHERE_FROM}:").unwrap();
            for source in note.sources {
                writeln!(sheet, "  - {source}{}", marks(source, source)).unwrap();
            }
            for (name, inputs, results) in &designs {
                let held = |path: &str| held_reason(&sizing, inputs, path);
                let view = NoteView {
                    inputs,
                    results,
                    held: &held,
                };
                writeln!(sheet, "\n-- at the {name} design").unwrap();
                writeln!(sheet, "What it is:").unwrap();
                for (i, sentence) in note.sentences.iter().enumerate() {
                    let drawn = note_text_on(sentence, &view);
                    writeln!(sheet, "  {}. {drawn}{}", i + 1, marks(sentence, &drawn)).unwrap();
                }
                if !note.change.is_empty() {
                    writeln!(sheet, "{WHAT_TO_CHANGE}:").unwrap();
                }
                for change in note.change {
                    let reason =
                        unlinked_reason(change, &view).map_or(String::new(), |r| format!(" ({r})"));
                    let drawn = note_text_on(change.text, &view);
                    writeln!(
                        sheet,
                        "  - {} {}{reason}: {drawn}{}",
                        change.step.word(),
                        label_for(change.input),
                        marks(change.text, &drawn)
                    )
                    .unwrap();
                    let Some((aim, sense)) = change.aim else {
                        continue;
                    };
                    let outcome = match step_input(inputs, change.input, change.step) {
                        Err(why) => format!("not stepped here: {why:?}"),
                        Ok(stepped) => match (results.get(aim), compute_all(&stepped).get(aim)) {
                            (Some(Value::Num(before)), Some(Value::Num(after)))
                                if before.is_finite() && after.is_finite() =>
                            {
                                let holds = match sense {
                                    notes::Sense::Up => after > before,
                                    notes::Sense::Down => after < before,
                                };
                                let verdict = if holds {
                                    "moves as it says"
                                } else {
                                    "DOES NOT MOVE AS IT SAYS"
                                };
                                format!("{before} -> {after}: {verdict}")
                            }
                            (before, after) => {
                                format!("no numbers to compare: {before:?} -> {after:?}")
                            }
                        },
                    };
                    writeln!(sheet, "      aim {aim} {sense:?}, one step: {outcome}").unwrap();
                }
                if !note.watch_out.is_empty() {
                    writeln!(sheet, "{WATCH_OUT}:").unwrap();
                }
                for line in note.watch_out {
                    let drawn = note_text_on(line, &view);
                    writeln!(sheet, "  - {drawn}{}", marks(line, &drawn)).unwrap();
                }
            }
            writeln!(sheet).unwrap();
        }
        let out = std::env::var("NOTES_REVIEW_OUT").map_or_else(
            |_| {
                std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("target/notes-for-review.txt")
            },
            std::path::PathBuf::from,
        );
        if let Some(dir) = out.parent().filter(|dir| !dir.as_os_str().is_empty()) {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).expect("the sheet's folder is made");
        }
        std::fs::write(&out, &sheet).expect("the sheet is written");
        println!(
            "{} notes at {} designs: {}",
            chosen.len(),
            designs.len(),
            out.display()
        );
    }
```

```rust
/// What a `{path}` in a note shows on the design whose results are `results` (slice-2 spec
/// 3.2): the result's number with its unit, as the readouts show it
/// (`guidance::result_text`); `None`, drawn as [`note_text::NO_VALUE`], for a
/// path no result has, a number that is not finite, and a text (a result that reads "n/a"
/// where it has no number, or a verdict: a live value is a number).
pub fn live_value(results: &DesignResults, path: &str) -> Option<String> {
    match results.get(path)? {
        Value::Num(x) if x.is_finite() => Some(result_text(results, path)),
        Value::Int(_) => Some(result_text(results, path)),
        Value::Num(_) | Value::Text(_) | Value::None => None,
    }
}

/// A note's text as drawn on `view`'s design: each `{path}` replaced by its live value
/// ([`live_value`]), then through `glyph_safe`.
fn note_text_on(text: &str, view: &NoteView<'_>) -> String {
    glyph_safe(&note_text::render(text, |path| {
        live_value(view.results, path)
    }))
}
```

```rust
// Guidance slice 2: live values in the notes, at the five probe designs, and the change
// entries' directions (spec 3.2 and section 6, tests 2 and 3)

/// The probe designs (`probes::probe_designs`), each with its name and its results.
fn probe_points() -> Vec<(&'static str, DesignInputs, DesignResults)> {
    probes::probe_designs()
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(name, inputs)| {
            let results = compute_all(&inputs);
            (name, inputs, results)
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A live value as these engine tests put it into note text: a finite number or a whole
/// number as Rust prints it; `None` (read as `note_text::NO_VALUE`) otherwise. The panel's
/// own text (four significant digits and the unit) is tested in `gui::explorer`.
fn engine_value(results: &DesignResults, path: &str) -> Option<String> {
    match results.get(path)? {
        Value::Num(x) if x.is_finite() => Some(x.to_string()),
        Value::Int(n) => Some(n.to_string()),
        Value::Num(_) | Value::Text(_) | Value::None => None,
    }
}

/// The placeholders in `text` followed by their own unit typed again: the value is drawn with
/// its unit, so `{model.pullout_Nm} N·m` would show the unit twice.
fn units_typed_after(text: &str, unit_of: &dyn Fn(&str) -> &'static str) -> Vec<String> {
    let Ok(pieces) = note_text::segments(text) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    pieces
        .windows(2)
        .filter_map(|pair| match pair {
            [
                note_text::Segment::Value(path),
                note_text::Segment::Text(after),
            ] => {
                let unit = unit_of(path);
                let typed = !unit.is_empty() && unit != "-" && after.trim_start().starts_with(unit);
                typed.then(|| (*path).to_owned())
            }
            _ => None,
        })
        .collect()
}

#[test]
fn a_unit_typed_after_a_live_value_is_found() {
    let unit_of = |path: &str| {
        if path == "model.pullout_Nm" {
            "N·m"
        } else {
            ""
        }
    };
    assert_eq!(
        units_typed_after("Here {model.pullout_Nm} N·m.", &unit_of),
        ["model.pullout_Nm"]
    );
    assert!(units_typed_after("Here {model.pullout_Nm}.", &unit_of).is_empty());
    assert!(units_typed_after("Here {model.f_end} at the ends.", &unit_of).is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn every_note_placeholder_names_a_number_result_and_renders_at_every_probe_design() {
    let points = probe_points();
    let rows = result_rows(&points[0].2);
    let types: BTreeMap<&str, FieldType> =
        rows.iter().map(|r| (r.path.as_str(), r.meta.ty)).collect();
    let units: BTreeMap<&str, &'static str> = rows
        .iter()
        .map(|r| (r.path.as_str(), r.meta.unit))
        .collect();
    let unit_of = |path: &str| units.get(path).copied().unwrap_or("");
    let mut failures = Vec::new();
    for note in notes::NOTES {
        // A title, a sentence 0 and a source hold no brace: no live value stands there.
        let plain = [note.title]
            .into_iter()
            .chain(note.sentences.first().copied())
            .chain(note.sources.iter().copied());
        for text in plain {
            if text.contains(['{', '}']) {
                failures.push(format!("{}: a brace in {text:?}", note.id));
            }
        }
        for text in note_text::rendered_texts(note) {
            if let Err(fault) = note_text::segments(text) {
                failures.push(format!("{}: {fault}", note.id));
            }
            for path in units_typed_after(text, &unit_of) {
                failures.push(format!("{}: the unit typed after {{{path}}}", note.id));
            }
        }
        for path in note_text::placeholders(note) {
            match types.get(path) {
                None => failures.push(format!("{}: {{{path}}} names no result", note.id)),
                Some(FieldType::F64 | FieldType::I64 | FieldType::NumOrText) => {}
                Some(other) => failures.push(format!(
                    "{}: {{{path}}} is a {other:?} result, not a number",
                    note.id
                )),
            }
        }
        for (name, _, results) in &points {
            for text in note_text::rendered_texts(note) {
                let drawn = note_text::render(text, |path| engine_value(results, path));
                if drawn.contains(['{', '}']) {
                    failures.push(format!("{} at the {name} design: {drawn:?}", note.id));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    assert!(failures.is_empty(), "{failures:#?}");
}

#[test]
#[ignore = "un-ignored in T18 when every note is rewritten"]
fn every_note_reads_in_plain_words_at_every_probe_design() {
    let mut failures = Vec::new();
    for (name, _, results) in &probe_points() {
        for note in notes::NOTES {
            let rendered = note_text::rendered_texts(note)
                .into_iter()
                .map(|text| note_text::render(text, |path| engine_value(results, path)));
            let fixed = [note.title]
                .into_iter()
                .chain(note.sources.iter().copied())
                .map(str::to_owned);
            for text in rendered.chain(fixed) {
                let banned = plain_text_violations(&text);
                if !banned.is_empty() {
                    failures.push(format!(
                        "{} at the {name} design: {banned:?} in {text:?}",
                        note.id
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    assert!(failures.is_empty(), "{failures:#?}");
}

/// One change entry's aim checked at `points`: at each design where the input moves one
/// slider step its way (`probes::step_input`) and the aimed result is a finite number before
/// and after, the result must move the way the entry says. The failures, and at how many
/// designs the aim was checked.
fn aim_failures(
    id: &str,
    change: &Change,
    points: &[(&str, DesignInputs, DesignResults)],
) -> (Vec<String>, usize) {
    let Some((aim, sense)) = change.aim else {
        return (Vec::new(), 0);
    };
    let mut failures = Vec::new();
    let mut checked = 0;
    for (name, inputs, results) in points {
        let Ok(stepped) = probes::step_input(inputs, change.input, change.step) else {
            continue;
        };
        let (Some(Value::Num(before)), Some(Value::Num(after))) =
            (results.get(aim), compute_all(&stepped).get(aim))
        else {
            continue;
        };
        if !(before.is_finite() && after.is_finite()) {
            continue;
        }
        checked += 1;
        let moved = match sense {
            Sense::Up => after > before,
            Sense::Down => after < before,
        };
        if !moved {
            failures.push(format!(
                "{id}: {} {} should move {aim} {sense:?} at the {name} design: {before} -> {after}",
                change.step.word(),
                change.input
            ));
        }
    }
    (failures, checked)
}

#[test]
fn every_change_entry_moves_its_aim_the_way_it_says() {
    let points = probe_points();
    let mut failures = Vec::new();
    for note in notes::NOTES {
        for change in note.change.iter().filter(|c| c.aim.is_some()) {
            let (found, checked) = aim_failures(note.id, change, &points);
            failures.extend(found);
            if checked == 0 {
                failures.push(format!(
                    "{}: {} {} is checked at no probe design (held, at its end or no number at all five)",
                    note.id,
                    change.step.word(),
                    change.input
                ));
            }
        }
    }
    assert!(failures.is_empty(), "{failures:#?}");
}

#[test]
fn the_aim_check_confirms_a_true_direction_and_catches_a_false_one() {
    let points = probe_points();
    let entry = |input, step, aim| Change {
        input,
        step,
        aim: Some(aim),
        text: "",
    };
    // True at every probe design: a smaller gap, longer magnets (stepped from the length in
    // use, the axial length being blank), and a hotter magnet that weakens.
    for truth in [
        entry(
            "metal.face_gap_mm",
            Step::Lower,
            ("model.pullout_Nm", Sense::Up),
        ),
        entry(
            "coupling.magnets.axial_length_mm",
            Step::Raise,
            ("model.pullout_Nm", Sense::Up),
        ),
        entry(
            "coupling.op_temp_C",
            Step::Raise,
            ("model.pullout_Nm", Sense::Down),
        ),
    ] {
        let (failures, checked) = aim_failures("test", &truth, &points);
        assert_eq!(failures, Vec::<String>::new(), "{truth:?}");
        assert_eq!(checked, points.len(), "{truth:?}");
    }
    let false_claim = entry(
        "metal.face_gap_mm",
        Step::Lower,
        ("model.pullout_Nm", Sense::Down),
    );
    let (failures, checked) = aim_failures("test", &false_claim, &points);
    assert_eq!((failures.len(), checked), (points.len(), points.len()));
    // An input a pick sets at every probe design is checked nowhere: the manual Br (the
    // library part sets it, or on the ferrite rings the grade).
    let held = entry(
        "coupling.magnets.manual_inner_br_T",
        Step::Raise,
        ("model.pullout_Nm", Sense::Up),
    );
    assert_eq!(aim_failures("test", &held, &points), (Vec::new(), 0));
}
```

#### Drafter notes

**Assumptions about other tasks.**
- T4 produced exactly the names in its Interfaces block; this task also uses T4's private
  `unlinked_reason` and the test helpers `nothing_held` and `note_frame` (same module).
- T1's `pub mod plain;` sits right after `pub mod notes;` in `explain/mod.rs` (alphabetical). If T1
  placed it elsewhere, put `pub mod probes;` right after `pub mod plain;` wherever it is.
- T1 may already ship an ignored plain-words test over the note fields. Mine,
  `every_note_reads_in_plain_words_at_every_probe_design`, renders the notes at the five designs
  first, as spec 3.4 asks; T18 un-ignores both (or keeps mine and drops a duplicate).
- T11-T17 write placeholders as `{result.path}` only. The physics drafts also use `{= expr}` and
  input paths (`phys-notes-a.md` line 9); both are refused here (spec 3.2: a placeholder names a
  result). A note task that needs a ratio either quotes both results or rewords.
- T20's sign-off sheet renders the new text at the default design with `note_text_on` (or
  `note_text::render` and `live_value`), and reads the old text from T4's snapshot (`## <id>`
  headings).
- T18's `only_the_review_tools_are_ignored` lists `notes_for_review` as a tool (it does, per its
  draft); `every_note_reads_in_plain_words_at_every_probe_design` carries T18's reason string and is
  un-ignored there.

**Decisions made here (each verified in the scratch replay).**
1. *The fifth probe goes through the Size tab's mapping* (`with_ring_radius(default, 20.0)`, the cap
   OD and thread following the cup), the design a user gets by moving Outside diameter. Setting only
   `coupling.inner_back_apothem_mm` to 20 gives the same torque, check and temperature results; it
   differs in the cap and thread inputs (the cap stays 42.8 mm under a 62.0 mm cup).
2. *A live value is a number.* `live_value` returns `None` for a text: a verdict's text carries
   jargon ("raise Metal design C122"), and a number result that reads "n/a" (the cold limit on
   NdFeB rings) means no prediction. The engine test refuses a placeholder on a text result.
3. *One table of seeds.* `step_input` starts a blank optional input (the axial length, the measured
   drag) where its input row enters it, so the length lever is checked at the five designs, where the
   override is blank. `OPTIONAL_SEEDS` moved to `engine::api`; `gui::inputs` re-exports it.
4. *One step.* `step_input` and the GUI's slider-end reason both use `SliderRange::step_from`, the
   step a check guide's fix takes; a count moves by its slider step and stays whole.
5. *The aim test requires each aim to be checked at one design at least*, so an entry whose input is
   held, at its end or not a number at all five designs fails instead of passing unchecked.
6. *A unit typed after a placeholder is refused* (`{model.pullout_Nm} N·m` would draw "N·m N·m").
7. *The review sheet* also prints each entry's held reason at each design and its aim's value before
   and after one step, and marks a text the parser refuses or the plain-words guard flags, so the
   physics reviewer sees in one file what spec section 4 asks them to check.

**Risks.** The aim test compares at one slider step, which is small (0.01 mm on the face gap): a
result flat over that step would read "did not move". None of the self-test's directions is close
(the smallest change seen was about 0.0002 N·m, the Y30 probe's length step, far above rounding). The review sheet depends on `held_reason` with
Auto off; it does not show Auto's hold.

**Open questions, with my proposed ruling.**
- Q1. Derived live values (a ratio such as S1 with steel over S1 in free space): ruling, not in this
  slice (spec 3.2 names results only); a later slice may add a Rust-only result for a ratio a note
  needs.
- Q2. Should the plain-words test also cover the change entries' display labels? Ruling: no; T2's
  coverage test owns every label, help and hint string.

**Review Focus candidates (an input or condition no test here exercises that would bite a user).**
- RF1. A live value inside a sentence whose words stop being true off the default (for example "most
  of the torque" beside the fundamental's share at a low fill). No test can read meaning; the
  per-note reviewer reads every note at the five designs (spec section 4). Proposed: the T11-T17
  review prompt asks for this check by name.
- RF2. A note opened while its result has no prediction (the ferrite probe's hot onsets, or f_end at
  or below 0): the sentence must still read correctly with "no prediction" in it. Tested for the
  rendering, not for the wording. Proposed: the reviewer reads the Y30 block of the sheet for every
  note with a placeholder.
- RF3. Auto on: the aim test and the sheet run with Auto off, and a held free variable is never
  stepped. No test draws a live value on the design Auto shows (the explorer gets `shown`, so it
  should). Proposed: T11's panel test (T4 RF1) also asserts a live value equals `live_value` of
  `shown_inputs()`.
- RF4. The ferrite note's placeholders read "no prediction" on the Example (NdFeB) design by
  design (spec section 5: ferrite-only rows on NdFeB), the first design a user sees. The sentence must
  read correctly that way; no test reads it. Proposed: T16's reviewer reads the default block of the
  sheet for `ferrite_cold_demag`.

```rust
    #[test]
    fn the_legends_and_axes_use_the_on_screen_names() {
        use crate::gui::plain_text::label_for;
        // One name per quantity (spec 3.5): the pull-out and the required torque read as the
        // dashboard and the input rows name them, the band edges name the production variation
        // allowance, the pole sweep's axis the magnet count and its line the ring radius.
        let pullout = label_for("model.pullout_Nm");
        assert!(PULL_OUT.starts_with(pullout), "{PULL_OUT}");
        assert!(
            PULL_OUT_SMALLEST_APOTHEM.starts_with(pullout),
            "{PULL_OUT_SMALLEST_APOTHEM}"
        );
        assert_eq!(REQUIRED, label_for("metal.required_min_Nm"));
        let allowance = label_for("metal.variation").to_lowercase();
        for band in [LOW_BAND, HIGH_BAND] {
            assert!(band.contains(&allowance), "{band}");
        }
        let ring = label_for("coupling.inner_back_apothem_mm").to_lowercase();
        assert!(
            PULL_OUT_SMALLEST_APOTHEM.contains(&ring),
            "{PULL_OUT_SMALLEST_APOTHEM}"
        );
        assert!(!PULL_OUT_SMALLEST_APOTHEM.contains("apothem"));
        // The sweeps' axes: the magnet count's name, and the nominal pull-out in N·m.
        let y_axis = format!("{pullout} [N\u{b7}m]");
        let texts = drawn_texts(&draw(PlotKind::PoleSweep, &DesignInputs::default()));
        assert!(
            texts.iter().any(|t| t == label_for("coupling.npole")),
            "the pole sweep's x axis: {texts:?}"
        );
        assert!(texts.contains(&y_axis), "the sweeps' y axis: {texts:?}");
        // The sweeps' amber status compares the nominal pull-out with the required floor
        // (engine::sweeps), not the hot-low torque with the required torque: the legend says
        // so, and names the floor as its own line does.
        assert!(
            BELOW_MINIMUM.contains(&REQUIRED_FLOOR.to_lowercase()),
            "{BELOW_MINIMUM}"
        );
        // Plain words and the default fonts' glyphs.
        let ctx = egui::Context::default();
        let _ = ctx.run(egui::RawInput::default(), |_| {});
        for text in [
            PULL_OUT,
            PULL_OUT_SMALLEST_APOTHEM,
            LOW_BAND,
            HIGH_BAND,
            REQUIRED,
            BELOW_MINIMUM,
            y_axis.as_str(),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(
                crate::gui::guidance::plain_text_violations(text),
                Vec::<&str>::new(),
                "{text}"
            );
            crate::gui::test_support::assert_glyphs(&ctx, text, "a plot legend or axis");
        }
    }
```

```rust
    /// The rect of `label` in the centre region: its leftmost copy right of the inputs side.
    /// The dashboard, drawn before the centre, can carry the same name (the Size tab's Hot-low
```

```rust
/// `text` followed by the unit as the screen writes it (`display_unit`), unless the unit is
/// empty or `-` (dimensionless).
pub fn with_unit(text: String, unit: &str) -> String {
    let unit = display_unit(unit);
    if unit.is_empty() || unit == "-" {
        text
    } else {
        format!("{text} {unit}")
    }
}

/// A unit as the screen writes it: the sweep tables' workbook header "Nm" reads "N·m", as every
/// other torque's unit does (spec 3.5). The metadata and the exports keep "Nm":
/// `tests/schema.rs` holds the sweep columns to the workbook headers.
fn display_unit(unit: &str) -> &str {
    if unit == "Nm" { "N·m" } else { unit }
}
```
