#### The strings and their evidence

Every direction below was probed with `compute_all` at five designs (the default; 8 magnets per ring; Back
iron material 7 = 304; Y30 grade on both rings with blank parts, the manual dimensions; ring radius 20 mm),
stepping the input by about one slider step (T5 owns the official probe definitions; these match spec 3.2).
"5/5" means the stated direction held at all five.

Requirements and operating conditions:

| Path | Help (words) | Claim -> engine evidence | Probe |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metal.required_min_Nm` (override) | The torque the coupling must hold at the operating magnet temperature. The hot-low torque must reach it; when on, Auto sizes the design to meet it. (26) | hot-low = pull-out at `op_temp_C` x (1 - variation), `metal_design.rs:413`; check `hot_low < required` fails, `:456`; pull-out at op temp `api.rs:224`; Auto meets hot-low, `size_controls.rs:36` | raising it moves the floor and the 20 °C requirement, not hot-low, 5/5 |
| `coupling.op_temp_C` (override) | The magnet temperature in normal running. Magnets weaken as they warm, so the pull-out and hot-low torque fall as it rises; cold-high uses the minimum temperature instead. (27) | `bri = br x br_factor(alpha, op_temp)`, `model.rs:977`; cold = torque_20C x factor(min_temp), `metal_design.rs:412-414` | pull-out and hot-low down, cold-high unchanged, 5/5 (Y30 included) |
| `metal.max_diameter_mm` (override) | Largest diameter the coupling may take, over the cup or the front cap, whichever is larger. Past it, the space claim check fails. (23) | `rot_od = max(cup_od, cap_od)` (no boss), `metal_design.rs:432`; reserve `:486`; "Exceeds the space claim" when over, `housing.rs:146-164`; Bad level `dashboard.rs:331` | rotating OD = max(cup, cap) 5/5 |
| `metal.max_overall_axial_mm` (override) | Longest the coupling may be, from the front cap to the end of the shaft boss. Past it, the space claim check fails. (23) | stack = cap axial + cup depth + web + boss length, `metal_design.rs:431`; reserve `:489` | stack 31.8 = 0.8 + 15.5 + 2.5 + 13 5/5 |
| `metal.max_large_dia_axial_mm` (override) | Longest the full-diameter part may be: front cap, magnet cup and its rear wall, without the shaft boss. Past it, the space claim check fails. (25) | large = cap axial + cup depth + web, `metal_design.rs:433`; reserve `:488` | 18.8 5/5 |
| `coupling.drive_torque_Nm` | Torque the wheel needs while driving. Times its safety factor it can raise the floor for the nominal pull-out in the results table and sweeps; the hot-low check ignores it. (30) | floor = max(drive x SF, required), `model.rs:1031`; model verdict on `T_pull < floor`, `:1158`; sweep status `sweeps.rs:172`; hot-low check reads only `required_min_Nm`, `metal_design.rs:456` | floor up, hot-low unchanged 5/5; at drive 4 N·m the model verdict flips at the default and the 20 mm ring, the hot-low check never moves |
| `coupling.drive_safety_factor` | Margin wanted on the driving torque. Driving torque times this factor sets the floor for the nominal pull-out when it exceeds the torque requirement. (24) | `model.rs:1031` | SF +1.5 leaves the floor at the requirement (0.7 x 2.8 < 2.5) 5/5: "when it exceeds" holds |
| `coupling.gear_ratio` | Reduction ratio of the gearbox; the coupling sits on its wheel side. A higher ratio lowers the coupling torques referred to the gearbox input, such as the slip ripple. /// Help batch A (slice 2, T7) and the hint lines: coverage, caps, plain words and the G-3 review
```rust
/// sheet. The coverage of every input (T2's test, ignored until T8) stays T2's.
#[cfg(test)]
mod help_tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::engine::explain::plain::plain_text_violations;
    use crate::gui::inputs::{InputCatalogue, KEY_DESIGN, WORKFLOW};
    use crate::gui::test_support::{SCREEN, assert_glyphs, sized_frame};

    /// The workflow groups of help batch A: their inputs' help is this batch's.
    const BATCH_A: [&str; 4] = ["operating", "magnets", "gap", "shaft"];

    /// The inputs of the workflow group `id`, in its sections' order.
    fn group_paths(id: &str) -> Vec<&'static str> {
        WORKFLOW
            .iter()
            .find(|group| group.id == id)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no workflow group {id}"))
            .sections
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|section| section.paths.iter().copied())
            .collect()
    }

    /// The inputs of batch A, every group in turn.
    fn batch_a_paths() -> Vec<&'static str> {
        BATCH_A.iter().flat_map(|group| group_paths(group)).collect()
    }

    /// The sentences of `text`: a '.', '?' or '!' that ends the text or is followed by
    /// whitespace ends one.
    fn sentence_count(text: &str) -> usize {
        let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
        chars
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|&(i, &c)| {
                matches!(c, '.' | '?' | '!') && chars.get(i + 1).is_none_or(|n| n.is_whitespace())
            })
            .count()
    }

    #[test]
    fn sentence_count_counts_the_stops_that_end_a_sentence() {
        assert_eq!(sentence_count("One. Two."), 2);
        assert_eq!(sentence_count("A gap: more torque; less clearance."), 1);
        assert_eq!(sentence_count("A 0.5 mm gap."), 1);
        assert_eq!(sentence_count("No stop"), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn batch_a_gives_every_input_of_its_groups_help() {
        let missing: Vec<&str> = batch_a_paths()
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|path| help_for(path).trim().is_empty())
            .collect();
        assert!(
            missing.is_empty(),
            "{} inputs without help: {missing:?}",
            missing.len()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn overlay_keys_are_unique() {
        for (name, table) in [("HELP", HELP), ("HINTS", HINTS)] {
            let mut keys: Vec<&str> = table.iter().map(|&(key, _)| key).collect();
            let count = keys.len();
            keys.sort_unstable();
            keys.dedup();
            assert_eq!(keys.len(), count, "{name} names a key twice");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_help_key_is_an_input() {
        let catalogue = InputCatalogue::get();
        for &(key, _) in HELP {
            assert!(catalogue.entry(key).is_some(), "{key} is not an input");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_help_row_differs_from_the_engine_help() {
        // A row that repeats the engine's help is a no-op that hides nothing and adds nothing.
        let catalogue = InputCatalogue::get();
        for &(key, text) in HELP {
            let engine = catalogue.entry(key).expect("a help key is an input").meta.help;
            assert_ne!(text, engine, "{key}: the row repeats the engine help");
        }

        for &(key, _) in HINTS {

        for &(key, text) in HINTS {

    /// The G-3 review sheet of `groups` (workflow group ids): each input's display label and
    /// path, the help shown and, for an overlay row, the engine help it replaces; then every
    /// hint line.
    fn review_sheet(groups: &[&str]) -> String {
        use std::fmt::Write as _;
        let catalogue = InputCatalogue::get();
        let mut sheet = String::new();
        for &group in groups {
            let workflow = WORKFLOW
                .iter()
                .find(|g| g.id == group)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no workflow group {group}"));
            writeln!(sheet, "# {}\n", workflow.label).unwrap();
            for section in workflow.sections {
                for &path in section.paths {
                    let engine = catalogue
                        .entry(path)
                        .expect("a workflow path is an input")
                        .meta
                        .help;
                    writeln!(sheet, "## {} ({path})", label_for(path)).unwrap();
                    writeln!(sheet, "help: {}", help_for(path)).unwrap();
                    if HELP.iter().any(|&(key, _)| key == path) {
                        let replaced = if engine.is_empty() { "(no help)" } else { engine };
                        writeln!(sheet, "replaces: {replaced}").unwrap();
                    }
                    writeln!(sheet).unwrap();
                }
            }
        }
        writeln!(sheet, "# Hint lines\n").unwrap();
        for &(key, hint) in HINTS {
            writeln!(sheet, "{key}: {hint}").unwrap();
        }
        sheet
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_review_sheet_lists_every_input_of_its_groups_and_every_hint() {
        let sheet = review_sheet(&BATCH_A);
        for path in batch_a_paths() {
            let entry = format!("({path})\nhelp: {}\n", help_for(path));
            assert!(sheet.contains(&entry), "{path}");
        }
        for &(key, hint) in HINTS {
            assert!(sheet.contains(&format!("{key}: {hint}\n")), "{key}");
        }
    }

    /// Writes the review sheet for the G-3 physics review (spec section 4): the groups in
    /// `HELP_REVIEW_GROUPS` (comma-separated workflow group ids; batch A's by default) to
    /// `HELP_REVIEW_OUT` (`target/help-for-review.txt` by default).
    #[test]

        let groups: Vec<String> = match std::env::var("HELP_REVIEW_GROUPS") {
            Ok(list) => list.split(',').map(|id| id.trim().to_owned()).collect(),
            Err(_) => BATCH_A.iter().map(|id| (*id).to_owned()).collect(),
        };
        let groups: Vec<&str> = groups.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
        let out = std::env::var("HELP_REVIEW_OUT")
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| "target/help-for-review.txt".to_owned());
        let sheet = review_sheet(&groups);
        std::fs::write(&out, &sheet).expect("the review sheet is written");
        println!("{sheet}");
    }
}
```

```rust
/// A line of weak text under a control, wrapped to the side's width: an input's hint line
/// ([`hint_line`]) and the Size tab's what-moves-what lines.
pub(crate) fn weak_line(ui: &mut egui::Ui, text: &str) {
    ui.add(egui::Label::new(egui::RichText::new(text).weak()).wrap());
}

/// The hint line under a control (slice 2 spec 3.5): the [`hint_for`] text of `key` (an input
/// path, or one of the Size tab's `plain_text::SIZE_TAB_HINT_KEYS`) as a [`weak_line`];
/// nothing for a key without a hint.
pub(crate) fn hint_line(ui: &mut egui::Ui, key: &str) {
    if let Some(hint) = hint_for(key) {
        weak_line(ui, hint);
    }
}
```

```rust
    /// Which way a help says a result moves when its input rises one slider step.
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
    enum Moves {
        Up,
        Down,
        Stays,
    }
    use Moves::{Down, Stays, Up};

    /// The design a claim is checked on: the example design, or it with one setting changed.
    fn claim_design(name: &str) -> DesignInputs {
        let mut inputs = DesignInputs::default();
        let mut set = |path: &str, value: Value| {
            inputs
                .set(path, value)
                .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{name}: {path}: {e:?}"));
        };
        match name {
            "example" => {}
            "no back iron" => set("coupling.backiron", Value::Int(0)),
            "1018 back iron" => set("materials.parts.back_iron", Value::Int(2)),
            "titanium sleeve" => set("materials.parts.sleeve_liner", Value::Int(2)),
            "7075 cap" => set("materials.parts.cap_housing", Value::Int(2)),
            "class 10.9" => set("clamps.screw_class", Value::Int(2)),
            "class A4-70" => set("clamps.screw_class", Value::Int(3)),
            "coercivity inputs" => set("temperature.demag.coercivity_source", Value::Int(0)),
            "measured drag" => set("metal.measured_drag_Nm", Value::Num(0.05)),
            "manual, no grade" => {
                set("coupling.magnets.part_inner", Value::Text(String::new()));
                set("coupling.magnets.part_outer", Value::Text(String::new()));
            }
            "Y30 grades" => {
                set("coupling.magnets.part_inner", Value::Text(String::new()));
                set("coupling.magnets.part_outer", Value::Text(String::new()));
                set(
                    "coupling.magnets.grade_inner",
                    Value::Text("Y30".to_owned()),
                );
                set(
                    "coupling.magnets.grade_outer",
                    Value::Text("Y30".to_owned()),
                );
            }
            other => panic!("no claim design {other:?}"),
        }
        inputs
    }

    #[test]
    fn batch_b_fills_every_empty_help_of_its_four_groups() {
        // The split with batch A (T7) is by workflow group: these four groups are batch B's.
        let catalogue = InputCatalogue::get();
        let empty_in_batch_b: BTreeSet<&str> = WORKFLOW
            .iter()
            .filter(|group| ["calibration", "materials", "housing", "thermal"].contains(&group.id))
            .flat_map(|group| group.sections.iter())
            .flat_map(|section| section.paths.iter().copied())
            .filter(|&path| {
                catalogue
                    .entry(path)
                    .is_some_and(|e| e.meta.help.is_empty())
            })
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(empty_in_batch_b, BTreeSet::from(BATCH_B_EMPTY));
        for path in BATCH_B_EMPTY {
            assert!(row(HELP, path).is_some(), "{path}: no help row");
            assert_eq!(original_help(path), None, "{path}: nothing to keep");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn batch_b_overrides_replace_a_non_empty_engine_help() {
        for path in BATCH_B_OVERRIDES {
            let (_, engine) = metadata(path).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{path}: no such path"));
            assert!(!engine.is_empty(), "{path}: the engine help is empty");
            assert!(row(HELP, path).is_some(), "{path}: no help row");
            // A Rust-only input's help is rewritten in the engine (T9), never overlaid.
            if let Some(entry) = InputCatalogue::get().entry(path) {
                assert!(!entry.meta.rust_only, "{path} is Rust-only");
            }
            assert!(!BATCH_B_EMPTY.contains(&path), "{path} is in both lists");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_original_note_is_the_spreadsheet_s_own_text() {
        // Under the toggle, "Original spreadsheet note" shows what the spreadsheet said: the
        // engine help, except where a correction reworded it, when the registry keeps the
        // workbook's text (and an empty one shows no note).
        let workbook_text = |path: &str| {
            crate::engine::deviations::REGISTRY
                .iter()
                .flat_map(|deviation| deviation.workbook_help)
                .find(|(key, _)| *key == path)
                .map(|(_, text)| *text)
        };
        let reworded: Vec<&str> = BATCH_B_OVERRIDES
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|&path| workbook_text(path).is_some())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(
            reworded,
            [
                "temperature.slip_loss.web_integral_T2m2",
                "temperature.demag.hcj20_kA_m",
                "temperature.demag.beta_hcj_per_C",
                "temperature.mismatch.adhesive_shear_modulus_GPa",
            ]
        );
        for path in BATCH_B_OVERRIDES {
            let engine = metadata(path).map(|(_, help)| help);
            let spreadsheet = workbook_text(path).or(engine).filter(|t| !t.is_empty());
            assert_eq!(original_help(path), spreadsheet, "{path}");
            if reworded.contains(&path) {
                assert_ne!(original_help(path), engine, "{path}: the corrected text");
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn each_cluster_ends_with_one_shared_caveat() {
        let last_sentence = |path: &str| help_for(path).rsplit(". ").next().unwrap_or_default();
        for cluster in [&STORED_3D[..], &PROTOTYPE[..], &GUESSES[..], &ADAPTER[..]] {
            let caveat = last_sentence(cluster[0]);
            for &path in cluster {
                assert_eq!(last_sentence(path), caveat, "{path} against {}", cluster[0]);
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn no_help_row_repeats_its_input_s_default() {
        // Spec 3.5: no default numbers in help; the tooltip already prints "Default: ...".
        for &(path, text) in HELP {
            let Some(entry) = InputCatalogue::get().entry(path) else {
                continue;
            };
            let default = match entry.default {
                Value::Num(x) => x,
                Value::Int(n) => n as f64,
                _ => continue,
            };
            let repeats = text
                .split(|c: char| c.is_whitespace() || ",;:()".contains(c))
                .filter_map(|token| token.trim_end_matches('.').parse::<f64>().ok())
                .any(|number| number == default);
            assert!(!repeats, "{path}: {text:?} repeats the default");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_direction_a_batch_b_help_states_holds_one_slider_step_up() {
        let catalogue = InputCatalogue::get();
        for &(input, design, result, moves) in CLAIMS {
            assert!(
                BATCH_B_EMPTY.contains(&input) || BATCH_B_OVERRIDES.contains(&input),
                "{input} is not batch B's"
            );
            let before = claim_design(design);
            let step = catalogue
                .entry(input)
                .and_then(|entry| entry.meta.range)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{input}: no slider"))
                .step;
            let raised = match before.get(input) {
                Some(Value::Num(x)) => Value::Num(x + step),
                Some(Value::Int(n)) => Value::Int(n + step as i64),
                other => panic!("{input}: {other:?}"),
            };
            let mut after = before.clone();
            after
                .set(input, raised)
                .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{input}: {e:?}"));
            let value = |inputs: &DesignInputs| match compute_all(inputs).get(result) {
                Some(Value::Num(x)) => x,
                other => panic!("{result}: {other:?}"),
            };
            let (was, now) = (value(&before), value(&after));
            let seen = if now > was {
                Up
            } else if now < was {
                Down
            } else {
                Stays
            };
            assert_eq!(
                seen, moves,
                "{input} one step up on the {design} design: {result} {was} -> {now}"
            );
        }
        // Every batch-B input with a slider and a value has its help's claim checked here; the
        // blank measured drag and the three results are checked in the next test.
        for path in BATCH_B_EMPTY.iter().chain(&BATCH_B_OVERRIDES) {
            let Some(entry) = catalogue.entry(path) else {
                continue;
            };
            if entry.default != Value::None {
                assert!(
                    CLAIMS.iter().any(|claim| claim.0 == *path),
                    "{path}: no claim"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_batch_b_claims_beyond_one_result_hold() {
        let example = DesignInputs::default();
        let number = |inputs: &DesignInputs, path: &str| match compute_all(inputs).get(path) {
            Some(Value::Num(x)) => x,
            other => panic!("{path}: {other:?}"),
        };
        // metal.boss_od_mm: the boss sets the outside diameter only when it is the largest part.
        let outside = dimensions(&example).expect("a size").diameter_mm;
        assert!(example.metal.boss_od_mm < outside);
        let mut big_boss = example.clone();
        big_boss.metal.boss_od_mm = outside + 1.0;
        assert_eq!(
            dimensions(&big_boss).expect("a size").diameter_mm,
            outside + 1.0
        );
        // metal.cap_od_mm: Size-tab diameter changes and Auto on the ring radius move the cap.
        let wider = resize_diameter(&example, outside + 1.0).expect("a wider design");
        assert!(wider.metal.cap_od_mm > example.metal.cap_od_mm);
        let radius = example.coupling.inner_back_apothem_mm + 0.5;
        let larger_ring = with_ring_radius(&example, radius).expect("a larger ring");
        assert!(larger_ring.metal.cap_od_mm > example.metal.cap_od_mm);
        // metal.cup_wall_corner_mm: a thicker wall grows the cup diameter by twice the change.
        let change = 0.1;
        let mut thicker = example.clone();
        thicker.metal.cup_wall_corner_mm += change;
        let grown = number(&thicker, "model.cup_od_mm") - number(&example, "model.cup_od_mm");
        assert!((grown - 2.0 * change).abs() < 1e-9, "{grown}");
        // metal.measured_drag_Nm: a measured drag replaces the estimate in both cases.
        let measured = claim_design("measured drag");
        let heat = measured.metal.measured_drag_Nm.expect("a drag")
            * number(&measured, "temperature.duty.slip_rad_s");
        assert_eq!(number(&measured, "temperature.slip_loss.used_W"), heat);
        assert_eq!(number(&measured, "temperature.slip_loss.high_W"), heat);
        // mass.magnets_g: a picked grade brings its density; an ungraded magnet keeps NdFeB's.
        let (manual, graded) = (claim_design("manual, no grade"), claim_design("Y30 grades"));
        assert_ne!(
            number(&manual, "mass.magnets_g"),
            number(&graded, "mass.magnets_g")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            number(&manual, "model.inner_magnet_density_g_mm3"),
            number(&example, "model.inner_magnet_density_g_mm3")
        );
        // model.inner_temp_check, model.outer_temp_check: no rating without a part or a grade.
        let unknown = Some(Value::Text("unknown".to_owned()));
        for path in ["model.inner_temp_check", "model.outer_temp_check"] {
            assert_eq!(compute_all(&manual).get(path), unknown, "{path}");
            assert_ne!(compute_all(&graded).get(path), unknown, "{path}");
            assert_ne!(compute_all(&example).get(path), unknown, "{path}");
        }
    }
}
```

- Replace `original_help`'s doc comment and keep its body:

```rust
/// The original spreadsheet's note of `path` where `HELP` replaces the engine's help, shown
/// under the spreadsheet-details toggle as "Original spreadsheet note: ...": the engine's help,
/// or the workbook's own text where a correction reworded it; `None` where that note is empty
/// or the overlay has no row.
pub fn original_help(path: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    original_in(HELP, path)
}
```

- Replace T2's `original_in` (its doc line `` /// [`original_help`] over `table`. `` and the function) with:

```rust
/// [`original_help`] over `table`: the original spreadsheet's note of the help a `table` row
/// replaces. That is the engine's help, except where a correction reworded it: then the
/// workbook's own text, which the deviation registry keeps (`spreadsheet_help`). `None` when
/// that note is empty or `table` has no row for `path`.
fn original_in(table: &[(&'static str, &'static str)], path: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    row(table, path)?;
    spreadsheet_help(path)
        .or_else(|| metadata(path).map(|(_, help)| help))
        .filter(|help| !help.is_empty())
}

/// The workbook's text of a help a correction reworded, as the deviation registry records it
/// (`Deviation::workbook_help`, possibly empty); `None` for a help the port kept as the
/// workbook wrote it.
fn spreadsheet_help(path: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    crate::engine::deviations::REGISTRY
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|deviation| deviation.workbook_help)
        .find(|(key, _)| *key == path)
        .map(|(_, text)| *text)
}
```

```rust
// ------------------------------------------------------------------ plain words (slice 2, T9)

/// A table row's path with its row index as `[*]` (`clamps.table[3].length_mm` becomes
/// `clamps.table[*].length_mm`), the form `workbook_help` names a column by; any other path as
/// it is.
fn column_pattern(path: &str) -> String {
    match (path.find('['), path.find(']')) {
        (Some(open), Some(close)) if open < close => {
            format!("{}[*]{}", &path[..open], &path[close + 1..])
        }
        _ => path.to_owned(),
    }
}

/// One field the engine words itself.
struct EngineText {
    path: String,
    label: &'static str,
    help: &'static str,
    choices: Vec<&'static str>,
}

/// What the engine words itself, apart from the Python port (spec ruling R1): every Rust-only
/// input and result, and every ported result or table column whose help an applied correction
/// rewords (Python keeps the workbook text there, so the port's text is free). A ported
/// input's help is Python's; the GUI overlay rewords it on screen (`gui::plain_text`), so it
/// is not here. A table column once.
fn engine_owned_text() -> Vec<EngineText> {
    let reworded = reworded_help();
    let defaults = DesignInputs::default();
    let inputs = input_rows(&defaults)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|row| row.meta.rust_only)
        .map(|row| EngineText {
            path: row.path,
            label: row.meta.label,
            help: row.meta.help,
            choices: row.meta.choices.iter().map(|&(_, text)| text).collect(),
        });
    let results = result_rows(&compute_all(&defaults))
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|row| {
            row.meta.rust_only || reworded.contains_key(column_pattern(&row.path).as_str())
        })
        .map(|row| EngineText {
            path: column_pattern(&row.path),
            label: row.meta.label,
            help: row.meta.help,
            choices: Vec::new(),
        });
    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
    inputs
        .chain(results)
        .filter(|text| seen.insert(text.path.clone()))
        .collect()
}

#[test]
fn the_text_helpers_find_what_they_name() {
    // Provenance: the audit, its decisions, the plans, the explorer's code name, the autofit,
    // the 3D milestone and bare cells; never a plain sentence.
    assert_eq!(
        provenance_words("Audit M9 (the user's decision: a flag)"),
        ["decision", "audit"]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        provenance_words("plan A-3: a term of the equation explorer"),
        ["plan a-", "equation explorer"]
    );
    assert_eq!(provenance_words("Calculator C6 = 0 still selects it"), ["C6"]);
    assert_eq!(
        provenance_words("Addendum A1 autofit, until M3 computes it"),
        ["autofit", "until m3"]
    );
    for clean in [
        "The cup wall check asks for it; n/a without back iron.",
        "20 °C, 1.35e6 S/m",
        "Cold (C) and hot",
        "B842SH blocks",
        "",
    ] {
        assert!(provenance_words(clean).is_empty(), "{clean:?}");
    }
    // Code: snake_case identifiers and dotted paths; never a symbol.
    assert_eq!(code_names("when f_end is 0"), ["f_e"]);
    assert_eq!(code_names("tau7_Pa"), ["7_P"]);
    assert_eq!(code_names("(coupling.max_harmonic)"), ["g.m", "x_h"]);
    for clean in [
        "B_i,1 B_o,1 S_1 / (2 μ0)",
        "τ_n and R_g",
        "0.1 mm",
        "Hk(T) = knee · Hcj",
        "B_gap",
    ] {
        assert!(code_names(clean).is_empty(), "{clean:?}");
    }
    // Counts: words between whitespace; a sentence ends at a stop followed by space or the end.
    assert_eq!(word_count("Blank: the manual Br and no rating."), 7);
    assert_eq!(sentence_count("One. Two at 0.1 mm and 1.35e6 S/m. "), 2);
    assert_eq!(sentence_count("No stop"), 0);
}

#[test]
fn every_result_label_and_help_passes_the_plain_words_guard() {
    // Spec 3.4 and 3.5: a result's hover shows its label and help. The Python port's wording and
    // the engine's own both pass the guard; a table column is checked once.
    let mut failures = Vec::new();
    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
    for row in result_rows(&compute_all(&DesignInputs::default())) {
        let column = column_pattern(&row.path);
        if !seen.insert(column.clone()) {
            continue;
        }
        for (what, text) in [("label", row.meta.label), ("help", row.meta.help)] {
            let hits = plain_text_violations(text);
            if !hits.is_empty() {
                failures.push(format!("{column}: {what} {hits:?}: {text:?}"));
            }
        }
    }
    assert!(failures.is_empty(), "{}", report(&failures));
}

#[test]
fn engine_owned_help_is_plain_and_short() {
    let texts = engine_owned_text();
    // Not vacuous: a Rust-only input, a Rust-only result, a reworded result and a reworded
    // table column are all in the set.
    for path in [
        "coupling.max_harmonic",
        "housing.space_claim_check",
        "metal.steel_cup_mass_g",
        "clamps.table[*].length_mm",
    ] {
        assert!(
            texts.iter().any(|t| t.path == path),
            "{path} is not engine-owned"
        );
    }
    let mut failures = Vec::new();
    for t in &texts {
        let mut strings = vec![("label", t.label), ("help", t.help)];
        strings.extend(t.choices.iter().map(|&choice| ("choice", choice)));
        for (what, text) in strings {
            let guard = plain_text_violations(text);
            let provenance = provenance_words(text);
            let code = code_names(text);
            if !(guard.is_empty() && provenance.is_empty() && code.is_empty()) {
                failures.push(format!(
                    "{}: {what} {guard:?} {provenance:?} {code:?}: {text:?}",
                    t.path
                ));
            }
        }
        // Help style (spec 3.5): at most 30 words, in one or two sentences.
        let (words, sentences) = (word_count(t.help), sentence_count(t.help));
        if words > 30 || sentences > 2 {
            failures.push(format!(
                "{}: help of {words} words in {sentences} sentences: {:?}",
                t.path, t.help
            ));
        }
    }
    assert!(failures.is_empty(), "{}", report(&failures));
}

#[test]
fn the_default_harmonic_set_reads_as_the_default() {
    // Spec 3.8: the choice the harmonic set starts at says "(default)", not the workbook's.
    let row = input_rows(&DesignInputs::default())
        .into_iter()
        .find(|r| r.path == "coupling.max_harmonic")
        .expect("the harmonic set");
    let Value::Int(code) = row.value else {
        panic!("a selector: {:?}", row.value)
    };
    let (_, text) = row
        .meta
        .choices
        .iter()
        .find(|(c, _)| *c == code)
        .expect("the default is a choice");
    assert!(text.ends_with(" (default)"), "{text}");
    assert_eq!(
        row.meta
            .choices
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, t)| t.contains("(default)"))
            .count(),
        1
    );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the helpers to `tests/common/mod.rs`**

Append after `pub fn report` (it ends at line 220):

```rust
/// Words of the engine's own provenance a reader of the screen never needs, beyond what the
/// plain-words guard holds (`engine::explain::plain`): the audit and its decisions, the plans,
/// the explorer's code name, the autofit and the 3D milestone (any case), and a bare workbook
/// cell such as "C6" or "C9" (the guard holds cells of two or three digits). The listed words
/// first, in the list's order, then the cells in text order.
pub fn provenance_words(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    const WORDS: [&str; 6] = [
        "decision",
        "audit",
        "plan a-",
        "equation explorer",
        "autofit",
        "until m3",
    ];
    let lower = text.to_lowercase();
    let mut hits: Vec<String> = WORDS
        .iter()
        .filter(|word| lower.contains(*word))
        .map(|word| (*word).to_owned())
        .collect();
    hits.extend(
        text.split_whitespace()
            .map(|word| word.trim_matches(|c: char| "()[],.;:'\"".contains(c)))
            .filter(|word| {
                word.len() > 1
                    && word.starts_with('C')
                    && word[1..].chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit())
            })
            .map(str::to_owned),
    );
    hits
}

/// The places `text` names code rather than a quantity, each as its three characters: a
/// snake_case identifier (an ASCII lowercase letter or digit, an underscore, an ASCII letter or
/// digit: `f_end`, `tau7_Pa`) or a dotted path (ASCII lowercase letters each side of a dot:
/// `coupling.npole`). A symbol such as B_i,1, S_1 or τ_n starts with a capital or a Greek
/// letter and is no code.
pub fn code_names(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    chars
        .windows(3)
        .filter(|w| {
            let identifier = w[1] == '_'
                && (w[0].is_ascii_lowercase() || w[0].is_ascii_digit())
                && w[2].is_ascii_alphanumeric();
            let path = w[1] == '.' && w[0].is_ascii_lowercase() && w[2].is_ascii_lowercase();
            identifier || path
        })
        .map(|w| w.iter().collect())
        .collect()
}

/// The words of `text` as a reader counts them: the runs between whitespace.
pub fn word_count(text: &str) -> usize {
    text.split_whitespace().count()
}

/// The sentences of `text`: each full stop, question mark or exclamation mark that ends the
/// text or is followed by whitespace (so neither 0.1 mm nor 1.35e6 ends one).
pub fn sentence_count(text: &str) -> usize {
    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    chars
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|&(i, c)| {
            ".!?".contains(*c) && chars.get(i + 1).is_none_or(|next| next.is_whitespace())
        })
        .count()
}
```

```rust
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_stored_3d_input_says_it_is_the_default_design_s_and_stays_fixed() {
        // The help on screen of every stored 3D input ends with one sentence, whether the
        // overlay or the engine words it.
        let catalogue = crate::gui::inputs::InputCatalogue::get();
        for path in STORED_3D_INPUTS {
            assert!(catalogue.entry(path).is_some(), "{path}: not an input");
            let help = crate::gui::plain_text::help_for(path);
            assert!(help.ends_with(STORED_3D_SENTENCE), "{path}: {help:?}");
            assert_eq!(
                guidance::plain_text_violations(help),
                Vec::<&str>::new(),
                "{path}: {help:?}"
            );
        }
    }
```

```rust
/// The rationale of the assumption `id`.
fn rationale(id: &str) -> &'static str {
    ASSUMPTIONS
        .iter()
        .find(|a| a.id == id)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{id}: no assumption"))
        .rationale
}

#[test]
fn every_label_and_rationale_reads_in_plain_words() {
    // Spec 3.4 and R10: the rationale is drawn under each assumption and is the hover text of a
    // dashboard Why link, so it names no spreadsheet cell, correction, audit, decision or code
    // name. The source keeps its cells (the test above) and is drawn only with Show spreadsheet
    // details on.
    let mut failures = Vec::new();
    for a in &ASSUMPTIONS {
        for (what, text) in [("label", a.label), ("rationale", a.rationale)] {
            let guard = plain_text_violations(text);
            let provenance = provenance_words(text);
            let code = code_names(text);
            if !(guard.is_empty() && provenance.is_empty() && code.is_empty()) {
                failures.push(format!(
                    "{}: {what} {guard:?} {provenance:?} {code:?}: {text:?}",
                    a.id
                ));
            }
        }
    }
    assert!(failures.is_empty(), "{failures:#?}");
}

#[test]
fn the_end_effect_and_calibration_rationales_state_what_was_checked() {
    // R10: the end factor's band against free-space 3D, as the end-effect note states it.
    let end = rationale("end_effect");
    assert!(
        end.contains("within 2 % of free-space 3D for magnets 3.2 mm and longer"),
        "{end}"
    );
    assert!(!end.contains("1 %"), "{end}");
    // PA-18: the measured factor goes to a design that matches the prototype's circuit, magnet
    // count and part, and nothing else is compared.
    let cal = rationale("calibration_factor");
    for named in ["no steel", "magnets per ring", "B842SH", "not compared"] {
        assert!(cal.contains(named), "{named:?} missing: {cal}");
    }
    assert!(!cal.contains("own rings"), "{cal}");
}
```

```rust
    #[test]
    fn the_cup_wall_verdict_names_the_wall_input_on_the_dashboard_only() {
        use crate::engine::compat::fmt_fixed;
        use crate::engine::materials::CUP_WALL_TOO_THIN;
        use crate::engine::meta::NumOrText;
        use crate::gui::plain_text::label_for;
        // Ruling R9: the default design's cup wall fails; the dashboard names the wall by its
        // input's label, with the engine's own number.
        let results = compute_all(&DesignInputs::default());
        let engine = &results.materials.cup_wall_check;
        let NumOrText::Num(wall) = results.materials.cup_wall_suggested_mm else {
            panic!("a steel circuit has a wall rule")
        };
        let want = format!(
            "Too thin: raise {} to at least {} mm",
            label_for("metal.cup_wall_corner_mm"),
            fmt_fixed(wall, 1)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            verdict_display("materials.cup_wall_check", engine).as_deref(),
            Some(want.as_str())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            guidance::plain_text_violations(&want),
            Vec::<&str>::new(),
            "{want}"
        );
        // The engine text is unchanged: the badge reads it, the line (and so the exports) keep it.
        assert!(engine.starts_with(CUP_WALL_TOO_THIN), "{engine}");
        assert_eq!(
            verdict_level("materials.cup_wall_check", engine),
            Some(Level::Bad)
        );
        let line = |results: &DesignResults| {
            dashboard_lines(results)
                .into_iter()
                .find(|l| l.path == "materials.cup_wall_check")
                .expect("the cup wall row")
        };
        assert_eq!(&line(&results).value, engine);
        assert_eq!(line(&results).shown_value(), want);
        // A passing wall, a design without back iron and every other row draw the engine text.
        for inputs in [passing_design(), design(|i| i.coupling.backiron = 0)] {
            let results = compute_all(&inputs);
            let row = line(&results);
            assert_eq!(row.shown_value(), row.value, "{}", row.value);
        }
        // Not that verdict, or its number not a finite number: no display text (the engine text
        // is drawn), never a panic.
        let nan = format!("{CUP_WALL_TOO_THIN}nan mm");
        let inches = format!("{CUP_WALL_TOO_THIN}2.0 inches");
        let words = format!("{CUP_WALL_TOO_THIN}two mm");
        for (path, text) in [
            ("materials.cup_wall_check", "OK"),
            ("materials.cup_wall_check", "No back iron"),
            ("materials.cup_wall_check", nan.as_str()),
            ("materials.cup_wall_check", inches.as_str()),
            ("materials.cup_wall_check", words.as_str()),
            ("metal.hot_min_check", engine.as_str()),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(verdict_display(path, text), None, "{path}: {text}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_dashboard_draws_the_cup_wall_verdict_in_plain_words() {
        use crate::engine::materials::CUP_WALL_TOO_THIN;
        let ctx = egui::Context::default();
        let results = compute_all(&DesignInputs::default());
        let shown = verdict_display("materials.cup_wall_check", &results.materials.cup_wall_check)
            .expect("the default cup wall fails");
        let texts = drawn_texts(&dashboard_frame(&ctx, &DesignInputs::default()));
        assert_eq!(texts.iter().filter(|t| **t == shown).count(), 1, "{shown}");
        let engine_words = CUP_WALL_TOO_THIN.trim_end();
        assert!(
            !texts.iter().any(|t| t.contains(engine_words)),
            "the engine's cell-named verdict is drawn"
        );
    }
```

```rust
            END_EFFECT_GREYED,
        ]
        .map(str::to_owned)
        .to_vec();
        texts.extend(InputOrder::ALL.map(|order| order.label().to_owned()));
        for group in &WORKFLOW {
            texts.push(group.label.to_owned());
            texts.extend(group.sections.iter().map(|section| section.label.to_owned()));
        }
        texts.push(term_tag(TermStyle {
            kind: TermKind::CellOnly,
            changed_from_default: false,
            affected_by_modified_assumption: false,
        }));
        for path in [
            "coupling.drive_torque_Nm",
            "metal.face_gap_mm",
            "model.pullout_Nm",
        ] {
            texts.push(Trace::of(path).expect("a traceable path").banner());
        }
        texts.push(
            end_effect_banner(&compute_all(&short_magnets()))
                .expect("short magnets are out of the end-effect range"),
        );
        let defaults = DesignInputs::default();
        let notes = crate::gui::geometry::geometry(&defaults, &compute_all(&defaults)).notes;
        assert_eq!(notes.len(), 3, "the wall rule and both design checks at the defaults");
        texts.extend(notes.into_iter().map(|note| note.text));
        for text in &texts {
            assert_eq!(
                crate::gui::guidance::plain_text_violations(text),
                Vec::<&str>::new(),
                "{text:?}"
            );
            let lower = text.to_lowercase();
            for word in INTERNAL {
                assert!(!lower.contains(word), "{word:?} in {text:?}");
            }
        }
    }
```

```rust

/// The input whose wall the cup wall verdict asks to raise.
const CUP_WALL_INPUT: &str = "metal.cup_wall_corner_mm";

/// What the dashboard draws for a check's verdict in place of the engine's text (ruling R9):
/// the cup wall's "Too thin" verdict names the wall by its input's on-screen label instead of
/// the original spreadsheet's cell. [`verdict_level`] has already read the engine text, and the
/// number is the engine's own, kept as written. `None` for any other path or text, and for a
/// number that is not a finite number: the engine text is then drawn.
pub fn verdict_display(path: &str, text: &str) -> Option<String> {
    if path != "materials.cup_wall_check" || verdict_level(path, text) != Some(Level::Bad) {
        return None;
    }
    let number = text.strip_prefix(CUP_WALL_TOO_THIN)?.strip_suffix(" mm")?;
    number.parse::<f64>().ok().filter(|x| x.is_finite())?;
    Some(format!(
        "Too thin: raise {} to at least {number} mm",
        label_for(CUP_WALL_INPUT)
    ))
}
```

- σ (`model.tau_Pa`) is the summed shear stress at the pull-out angle (`model.rs:997-999`; its label
  "Total magnetic shear stress at pull-out", `model.rs:324`).
- N does not enter R_g (`model.rs:917-970`); it sets τ_p and the fills (`:971-973`) and, for flat
  blocks, the pocket radius r_pocket = (A_back + bond)/cos(π/N) (`:958-963`), so fewer flat blocks
  grow the cup.

```rust
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Slice-2 notes: what the note text claims about the engine
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The pull-out of `inputs` after `edit`.
fn pullout_after(inputs: &DesignInputs, edit: impl FnOnce(&mut DesignInputs)) -> f64 {
    let mut edited = inputs.clone();
    edit(&mut edited);
    compute_all(&edited).model.pullout_Nm
}

/// The probe design named `name` (spec 3.2, `probes::probe_designs`).
fn probe_inputs(name: &str) -> DesignInputs {
    probe_designs()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|(design, _)| *design == name)
        .map(|(_, inputs)| inputs)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no probe design {name:?}"))
}

/// `torque_from_shear` states two things about the engine. Its length entry: on the example
/// design a millimetre of magnet length adds more pull-out than a millimetre of ring radius.
/// Its first watch-out: a larger ring at the same magnet count can lower the pull-out (the
/// 8-magnet probe design, 1 mm larger).
#[test]
fn torque_from_shear_claims_hold_on_the_engine() {
    let example = DesignInputs::default();
    let results = compute_all(&example);
    let (base, length) = (results.model.pullout_Nm, results.model.inner_length_mm);
    let per_mm_length = pullout_after(&example, |i| {
        i.coupling.magnets.axial_length_mm = Some(length + 1.0);
    }) - base;
    let per_mm_radius =
        pullout_after(&example, |i| i.coupling.inner_back_apothem_mm += 1.0) - base;
    assert!(
        per_mm_radius > 0.0 && per_mm_length > per_mm_radius,
        "per mm: length {per_mm_length}, ring radius {per_mm_radius}"
    );
    let eight = probe_inputs("8 magnets per ring");
    let before = compute_all(&eight).model.pullout_Nm;
    let after = pullout_after(&eight, |i| i.coupling.inner_back_apothem_mm += 1.0);
    assert!(after < before, "8 magnets, ring radius +1 mm: {before} -> {after}");
}

/// Inputs that are blank by default (an optional number) and the result whose value a user's
/// first edit starts from (decision M41-12: the axial override enters at the inner ring's
/// length in use). An aim on such an input is checked from that value, so a blank input never
/// leaves an aim unchecked.
const BLANK_SEEDS: [(&str, &str); 1] = [(
    "coupling.magnets.axial_length_mm",
    "model.inner_length_mm",
)];

/// Spec section 6 test 2 for the inputs the general aim test cannot step: every `aim` on an
/// input that is blank at a probe design holds there from the value the input enters at, one
/// slider step in the entry's direction.
#[test]
fn an_aim_on_a_blank_input_holds_from_the_value_it_enters_at() {
    let steps: BTreeMap<String, f64> = input_rows(&DesignInputs::default())
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|row| row.meta.range.map(|range| (row.path, range.step)))
        .collect();
    let mut checked = 0;
    for note in notes::NOTES {
        for change in note.change {
            let Some((result, sense)) = &change.aim else {
                continue;
            };
            for (design, inputs) in probe_designs() {
                if inputs.get(change.input) != Some(Value::None) {
                    continue;
                }
                let (_, seed) = BLANK_SEEDS
                    .iter()
                    .find(|(path, _)| *path == change.input)
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| {
                        panic!(
                            "{}: {} is blank at {design}; add the result it enters at to BLANK_SEEDS",
                            note.id, change.input
                        )
                    });
                let Some(Value::Num(start)) = compute_all(&inputs).get(seed) else {
                    panic!("{seed} at {design}");
                };
                let delta = match change.step {
                    notes::Step::Raise => steps[change.input],
                    notes::Step::Lower => -steps[change.input],
                    notes::Step::Choose => {
                        panic!("{}: an aim on a choice ({})", note.id, change.input)
                    }
                };
                let at = |x: f64| {
                    let mut edited = inputs.clone();
                    edited
                        .set(change.input, Value::Num(x))
                        .expect("a number the input accepts");
                    match compute_all(&edited).get(result) {
                        Some(Value::Num(v)) => v,
                        other => panic!("{result} at {design}: {other:?}"),
                    }
                };
                let (before, after) = (at(start), at(start + delta));
                let (moved, way) = match sense {
                    notes::Sense::Up => (after > before, "up"),
                    notes::Sense::Down => (after < before, "down"),
                };
                assert!(
                    moved,
                    "{} at {design}: {} {} from {start} by {delta} should move {result} {way}: {before} -> {after}",
                    note.id,
                    change.step.word(),
                    change.input
                );
                checked += 1;
```

Engine facts the notes state (verified at b0166ad with a probe crate outside the repo):
- Fill: `model.rs:508-513` `pitch_share` = width / (2π·(back apothem + thickness/2)/N), each ring at
  its own magnet mid-radius, clamped at 1 (`:972-973`); harmonic amplitude
  B_n = Br·4/(nπ)·sin(nπλ/2) (`:646-649`); each harmonic pairs only with its own (`:679-711`).
- Steel: `geometry_factor` (`:632-642`): S_iron/S_free > 1 for every k, growing as k·t falls; the
  free factor carries e^(−k·g), k_1 = π/τ_p (`records/torque.rs:22-23`).
- Pull-out: `:1003` T_pull = T_2D·f_end·f_cal at `coupling.op_temp_C` (`:977-978`); the E7 search
  (`:727-745`, `:856-891`) moves the peak off half a pitch only when −A1 + 9·A3 − 25·A5 > 0 (a
  same-sign third harmonic above about A1/9); the torque-angle curve is Σ A_n sin(nφ).
- Probe values (rendered as on screen):

| Probe design | fills in / out | σ_1 of σ | S_1 steel / free | op temp | pull-out angle | harmonics 7-11 vs 1, 3, 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | 0.8612 / 0.6198 | 200000 of 201400 Pa | 0.2445 / 0.1392 | 50 °C | 1.571 rad | < 0.01 % |
| 8 magnets per ring | 0.6890 / 0.4959 | 149100 of 151800 Pa | 0.2373 / 0.1188 | 50 °C | 1.571 rad | +0.29 % max |
| 304 back iron | 0.8612 / 0.6198 | 113800 of 115100 Pa | 0.2445 / 0.1392 | 50 °C | 1.571 rad | −0.05 % max |
| Y30 ferrite, custom dimensions | 0.8612 / 0.6198 | 15400 of 15510 Pa | 0.2445 / 0.1392 | 50 °C | 1.571 rad | < 0.01 % |
| 20 mm ring radius | 0.4682 / 0.3864 | 64870 of 71440 Pa | 0.2096 / 0.0878 | 50 °C | 0.9243 rad (53° electrical, 10.6° twist) | +0.56 % max |

- At the 20 mm design the third harmonic moves the pull-out from 2.889 (fundamental only) to
  2.530 N·m (−12.4 %) and its angle to 0.9234 rad; A3/A1 = +0.216 there, −0.011 at the default.
- Aims, one slider step, every design where the input is free: face gap −0.01 mm raises the
  pull-out (all five); operating temperature −0.5 °C raises the pull-out (all five); outer
  manual width +0.01 mm raises the pull-out and outer thickness +0.01 mm raises S_1 with steel
  (Y30 design only: elsewhere the library part sets them); magnets per ring +2 raises the outer
  fill (all five, never clamped). The axial override's aim is checked by T11's blank-input test.
- B842-N52 instead of B842SH on the inner ring (same block): pull-out ×1.115385 = the inner Br
  ratio exactly; rated 80 °C against 150 °C.
- Back-iron codes: only 7 (304) and 8 (6061-T6) give the free-space circuit; with Back iron 0
  every code does.
- Trap found while drafting (not written in any note): more magnets do not always make the
  coupling stiffer. At the 20 mm design, 10 -> 12 magnets moves the twist at pull-out from 10.6°
  to 15.0°, because the low-fill third harmonic pulls the peak below 90° at 10 magnets.

```rust
    #[test]
    fn the_torque_angle_diagram_dashes_the_fundamental_alone_peaking_at_90_degrees() {
        // TC-22: the summed curve with a strong third harmonic is the unusual case (the test
        // above keeps its E7 peak); beside it the fundamental alone, dashed, peaks at 90°, half
        // a pole pitch, where a tick and its label sit. Each curve is named in its colour.

        let (left, right) = (summed[0].x, summed[summed.len() - 1].x);
        let degrees = |x: f32| (x - left) / (right - left) * 180.0;
        let dashed = label_color(&shapes, FUNDAMENTAL_ALONE);
        let dashes: Vec<Pos2> = shapes
            .iter()

                _ => None,
            })
            .flatten()
            .collect();

        let top = dashes
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .min_by(|a, b| a.y.total_cmp(&b.y))
            .expect("the dashes");
        assert!((degrees(top.x) - 90.0).abs() < 5.0, "peak at {}°", degrees(top.x));
        // It rises from the axis at 0° and comes back to it near 180°, as the summed curve does.
        let axis = summed[0].y;
        assert!(dashes.iter().any(|p| degrees(p.x).abs() < 1e-3 && (p.y - axis).abs() < 1e-3));
        assert!(dashes.iter().any(|p| (degrees(p.x) - 180.0).abs() < 5.0));
        assert!(dashes.iter().all(|p| p.y <= axis + 1e-3), "above the axis");
        // The 90° label sits under 90°.

            .iter()

                }

            (degrees(tick.center().x) - 90.0).abs() < 0.5,
            "{}",
            degrees(tick.center().x)
        );

            .iter()
            .filter_map(|s| match s {

                }
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect();
        brackets.sort_by(|p, q| p.0.total_cmp(&q.0));
        let [(l0, l1, ly0, ly1), (r0, r1, ry0, ry1)] = brackets[..] else {
            panic!("two brackets: {brackets:?}")
        };
        let lost = END_LOSS * block.width();
        assert!((l0 - block.left()).abs() < 1e-3 && (l1 - l0 - lost).abs() < 1e-3);
        assert!((r1 - block.right()).abs() < 1e-3 && (r1 - r0 - lost).abs() < 1e-3);
        for y in [ly1, ry0, ry1] {

        }
```

(c) `magcoupling-rs/tests/explain.rs`, after T11's test

banner), add:

```rust
/// `harmonics` states two things about the engine. Its harmonic-set entry: summing past the
/// fifth moved the pull-out under 2 % where checked (the five probe designs). Its watch-out: at
/// low fill the third harmonic can change the pull-out by more than a tenth and move its angle
/// (the 20 mm ring radius design, both fills under one half).
#[test]
fn harmonics_claims_hold_at_the_probe_designs() {
    let with_set = |inputs: &DesignInputs, set: i64| {
        let mut edited = inputs.clone();
        edited.coupling.max_harmonic = set;
        compute_all(&edited).model
    };
    for (design, inputs) in probe_designs() {
        let five = with_set(&inputs, 5).pullout_Nm;
        for set in [7, 9, 11] {
            let more = with_set(&inputs, set).pullout_Nm;
            assert!(
                (more / five - 1.0).abs() < 0.02,
                "{design}, harmonics to {set}: {more} against {five}"
            );
        }
    }
    let low_fill = probe_inputs("20 mm ring radius");
    let (first, third) = (with_set(&low_fill, 1), with_set(&low_fill, 3));
    assert!(
        third.fill_inner < 0.5 && third.fill_outer < 0.5,
        "{} {}",
        third.fill_inner,
        third.fill_outer
    );
    assert!(
        (third.pullout_Nm / first.pullout_Nm - 1.0).abs() > 0.1,
        "{} against {}",
        third.pullout_Nm,
        first.pullout_Nm
    );
    assert!(
        (third.pullout_angle_rad - FRAC_PI_2).abs() > 0.1,
        "{}",
        third.pullout_angle_rad
    );
}

/// `back_iron_factor`'s two choice entries: among the back-iron materials only 304 and
/// aluminium switch the torque model to free space, and with no back iron it is free space
/// whatever material is picked.
#[test]
fn back_iron_factor_claims_hold_on_the_engine() {
    use magcoupling::engine::material_library::BACK_IRON_CHOICES;
    let circuit = |code: i64, backiron: i64| {
        let mut inputs = DesignInputs::default();
        inputs.materials.parts.back_iron = code;
        inputs.coupling.backiron = backiron;
        compute_all(&inputs).materials.circuit_backiron
    };
    let free_space: Vec<&str> = BACK_IRON_CHOICES
        .iter()
        .filter(|&&(code, _)| circuit(code, 1) == 0)
        .map(|&(_, id)| id)
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(free_space, ["304_annealed", "6061_T6"]);
    for &(code, id) in &BACK_IRON_CHOICES {
        assert_eq!(circuit(code, 0), 0, "{id} with no back iron");
    }
}

/// `pullout_angle`'s grade entry, on the example design: a stronger grade on the inner ring
/// (B842-N52 for B842SH, the same block) raises the pull-out in proportion to that ring's Br,
/// and is rated for less heat.
#[test]
fn pullout_angle_claims_hold_on_the_engine() {
    use magcoupling::engine::meta::NumOrText;
    let example = DesignInputs::default();
    let base = compute_all(&example).model;
    let mut stronger = example.clone();
    stronger.coupling.magnets.part_inner = "B842-N52".to_owned();
    let n52 = compute_all(&stronger).model;
    assert!(n52.inner_br_T > base.inner_br_T);
    let (torque, br) = (
        n52.pullout_Nm / base.pullout_Nm,
        n52.inner_br_T / base.inner_br_T,
    );
    assert!((torque / br - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12, "{torque} against {br}");
    match (n52.inner_tmax_C, base.inner_tmax_C) {
        (NumOrText::Num(rated), NumOrText::Num(base_rated)) => {
            assert!(rated < base_rated, "{rated} against {base_rated}")
        }
        other => panic!("{other:?}"),
    }
}
```

(d) Replace the whole `torque_angle` function and its doc comment (from
`/// Torque against electrical angle over 0 to π with a third harmonic, its peak marked.` to the
function's closing `}`) with:

```rust
/// Torque against electrical angle over 0 to π (TC-22): the fundamental alone, dashed, its peak
/// at 90° (half a pole pitch, the tick "90°"), and the sum with a strong third harmonic, solid,
/// its peak marked.
fn torque_angle(fonts: &Fonts, r: Rect, pens: &Pens) -> Vec<Shape> {
    let plot = Rect::from_min_max(
        pos2(r.left() + 14.0, r.top()),
        pos2(r.right(), r.bottom() - 14.0),
    );
    let torque = |t: f32| (t * PI).sin() + TORQUE_THIRD * (3.0 * t * PI).sin();
    let points = curve(plot, 0.0, 1.2, 181, torque);
    let fundamental = curve(plot, 0.0, 1.2, 181, |t| (t * PI).sin());
    // The fundamental's top: its middle sample, t = 0.5.
    let fundamental_top = fundamental[90];
    let peak = points
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .min_by(|a, b| a.y.total_cmp(&b.y))
        .unwrap_or(plot.center());
    let half_pitch = pos2(plot.center().x, plot.bottom());
    let mut shapes = vec![
        Shape::line_segment(
            [plot.left_bottom(), plot.right_bottom()],
            Stroke::new(1.0, pens.weak),
        ),
        Shape::line_segment(
            [plot.left_bottom(), plot.left_top()],
            Stroke::new(1.0, pens.weak),
        ),
        Shape::line_segment(
            [half_pitch, half_pitch - vec2(0.0, 4.0)],
            Stroke::new(1.0, pens.weak),
        ),
        Shape::line(points, Stroke::new(1.5, pens.first)),
        Shape::circle_filled(peak, 3.5, pens.second),
        label(
            fonts,
            peak - vec2(6.0, 0.0),
            Align2::RIGHT_CENTER,
            "pull-out",
            pens.second,
        ),
        label(
            fonts,
            fundamental_top - vec2(0.0, 2.0),
            Align2::CENTER_BOTTOM,
            FUNDAMENTAL_ALONE,
            pens.ink,
        ),
        label(
            fonts,
            plot.left_bottom(),
            Align2::LEFT_TOP,
            STRONG_THIRD,
            pens.first,
        ),
        label(fonts, half_pitch, Align2::CENTER_TOP, "90°", pens.weak),
        label(
            fonts,
            plot.right_bottom(),
            Align2::RIGHT_TOP,
            "φ: 0 to 180°",
            pens.ink,
        ),
        label(fonts, plot.left_top(), Align2::RIGHT_TOP, "T", pens.ink),
    ];
    shapes.extend(Shape::dashed_line(
        &fundamental,
        Stroke::new(1.0, pens.ink),
        4.0,
        3.0,
    ));
    shapes
}
```

```rust
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Slice 2 note claims: the end-effect and calibration notes (plan T13)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The input both rings' magnet length follows: blank on every probe design, so each ring keeps
/// its part's length.
const AXIAL_LENGTH: &str = "coupling.magnets.axial_length_mm";

/// The slider step of the input at `path`: the move a note's "What to change" entry makes
/// (spec section 6 test 2).
fn lever_step(path: &str) -> f64 {
    input_rows(&DesignInputs::default())
        .into_iter()
        .find(|row| row.path == path)
        .and_then(|row| row.meta.range)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{path}: an input with a slider"))
        .step
}

/// `design` with both rings one slider step of the axial length longer. A blank length starts
/// from the inner ring's length in effect, as the panel's optional-input seed does
/// (`gui::inputs::OPTIONAL_SEEDS`): the generic aim test skips a blank input, so the notes'
/// length levers are checked through this.
fn one_step_longer(design: &DesignInputs) -> DesignInputs {
    let from = design
        .coupling
        .magnets
        .axial_length_mm
        .unwrap_or_else(|| compute_all(design).model.inner_length_mm);
    let mut longer = design.clone();
    longer.coupling.magnets.axial_length_mm = Some(from + lever_step(AXIAL_LENGTH));
    longer
}

#[test]
fn the_end_effect_note_s_levers_move_the_end_factor_as_it_says() {
    use magcoupling::engine::explain::notes::{Sense, Step};
    use magcoupling::engine::explain::probes::probe_designs;
    let note = notes::note("end_effect").expect("the end-effect note");
    let levers: Vec<&str> = note.change.iter().map(|c| c.input).collect();
    // Magnet length first (lengthen first), then the magnet count, then the assumption that
    // only evidence should move.
    assert_eq!(levers, [AXIAL_LENGTH, "coupling.npole", "coupling.c_end"]);
    assert!(note.change.iter().all(|c| matches!(c.step, Step::Raise)));
    assert_eq!(note.change[0].aim, Some(("model.f_end", Sense::Up)));
    assert_eq!(note.change[1].aim, Some(("model.f_end", Sense::Up)));
    assert_eq!(note.change[2].aim, Some(("model.f_end", Sense::Down)));
    for (name, design) in probe_designs() {
        let base = compute_all(&design);
        // Entry 1: a smaller share lost at the ends, more torque, and the trade-off it names:
        // cold-high and the clamp's demand rise with it.
        let r = compute_all(&one_step_longer(&design));
        assert!(r.model.f_end > base.model.f_end, "{name}: f_end");
        assert!(r.model.pullout_Nm > base.model.pullout_Nm, "{name}: pull-out");
        assert!(
            r.metal.torque_cold_high_Nm > base.metal.torque_cold_high_Nm,
            "{name}: cold-high"
        );
        assert!(r.clamps.required_Nm > base.clamps.required_Nm, "{name}: clamp");
        // Entry 3: every torque falls, cold-high and the clamp load included; the bench
        // prototype's own end factor does not move.
        let mut c_end = design.clone();
        c_end.coupling.c_end += lever_step("coupling.c_end");
        let r = compute_all(&c_end);
        assert!(r.model.pullout_Nm < base.model.pullout_Nm, "{name}");
        assert!(r.metal.torque_cold_high_Nm < base.metal.torque_cold_high_Nm, "{name}");
        assert!(r.clamps.required_Nm < base.clamps.required_Nm, "{name}");
        assert_eq!(r.calibration.f_end, base.calibration.f_end, "{name}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_end_effect_note_s_length_claims_hold_at_every_probe_design() {
    use magcoupling::engine::explain::probes::probe_designs;
    use magcoupling::engine::model::END_EFFECT_OUT_OF_RANGE;
    for (name, design) in probe_designs() {
        let base = compute_all(&design);
        let at = |length: f64| {
            let mut d = design.clone();
            d.coupling.magnets.axial_length_mm = Some(length);
            compute_all(&d)
        };
        // Sentence 4: every extra millimetre of overlap adds the same torque.
        let l = base.model.active_length_mm;
        let t: Vec<f64> = [l, l + 1.0, l + 2.0]
            .iter()
            .map(|&x| at(x).model.pullout_Nm)
            .collect();
        assert!(t[1] > t[0], "{name}: {t:?}");
        assert!(
            ((t[2] - t[1]) - (t[1] - t[0])).abs() <= 1e-9 * (t[1] - t[0]),
            "{name}: {t:?}"
        );
        // Watch-out 2: at or below c_end·τ_p there is no prediction and the check flags it;
        // just above it, a prediction.
        let lost = design.coupling.c_end * base.model.pole_pitch_mm;
        assert_eq!(
            at(0.999 * lost).model.end_effect_check,
            END_EFFECT_OUT_OF_RANGE,
            "{name}"
        );
        assert_eq!(at(1.001 * lost).model.end_effect_check, "OK", "{name}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_calibration_note_s_levers_and_rule_hold_at_every_probe_design() {
    use magcoupling::engine::explain::notes::{Sense, Step};
    use magcoupling::engine::explain::probes::probe_designs;
    let note = notes::note("calibration").expect("the calibration note");
    let levers: Vec<&str> = note.change.iter().map(|c| c.input).collect();
    assert_eq!(
        levers,
        [
            "calibration.f_cal_original",
            "calibration.measured_torque_Nm",
            "calibration.test_temp_C",
        ]
    );
    assert!(matches!(note.change[0].step, Step::Lower));
    assert!(note.change[1..].iter().all(|c| matches!(c.step, Step::Raise)));
    // A prototype match ignores the assumed factor, so entry 1 claims no direction a test could
    // check at every design: it is checked here, design by design.
    assert_eq!(note.change[0].aim, None);
    assert_eq!(note.change[1].aim, Some(("calibration.f_cal_updated", Sense::Up)));
    assert_eq!(note.change[2].aim, Some(("calibration.f_cal_updated", Sense::Up)));
    // A prototype match by the rule's own terms (sentence 3).
    let is_match = |d: &DesignInputs, r: &DesignResults| {
        r.materials.circuit_backiron == 0
            && d.coupling.npole as f64 == r.calibration.poles_per_ring
            && d.coupling.magnets.part_inner == "B842SH"
            && d.coupling.magnets.part_outer == "B842SH"
    };
    let (mut matching, mut other) = (0, 0);
    for (name, design) in probe_designs() {
        let base = compute_all(&design);
        let matched = is_match(&design, &base);
        // Entry 1: every torque outside a match falls in proportion, cold-high included; a
        // match ignores it.
        let mut lower = design.clone();
        lower.calibration.f_cal_original -= lever_step("calibration.f_cal_original");
        let r = compute_all(&lower);
        if matched {
            matching += 1;
            assert_eq!(base.model.f_cal, base.calibration.f_cal_updated, "{name}");
            assert!(
                (r.model.pullout_Nm / base.model.pullout_Nm - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12,
                "{name}: a match ignores the assumed factor"
            );
        } else {
            other += 1;
            assert_eq!(base.model.f_cal, design.calibration.f_cal_original, "{name}");
            let ratio = lower.calibration.f_cal_original / design.calibration.f_cal_original;
            for (before, after) in [
                (base.model.pullout_Nm, r.model.pullout_Nm),
                (base.metal.torque_hot_low_Nm, r.metal.torque_hot_low_Nm),
                (base.metal.torque_cold_high_Nm, r.metal.torque_cold_high_Nm),
            ] {
                assert!((after / before - ratio).abs() < 1e-12, "{name}: {before} -> {after}");
            }
        }
        // Entry 2: the measured factor rises with the measurement, and only a match uses it.
        let mut more = design.clone();
        more.calibration.measured_torque_Nm += lever_step("calibration.measured_torque_Nm");
        let r = compute_all(&more);
        assert!(r.calibration.f_cal_updated > base.calibration.f_cal_updated, "{name}");
        assert_eq!(r.model.f_cal != base.model.f_cal, matched, "{name}: only a match uses it");
        // Entry 3: a warmer test weakens the modelled prototype, so the measured factor rises.
        let mut warmer = design.clone();
        warmer.calibration.test_temp_C += lever_step("calibration.test_temp_C");
        let r = compute_all(&warmer);
        assert!(
            r.calibration.model_torque_Nm < base.calibration.model_torque_Nm,
            "{name}: a weaker modelled prototype"
        );
        assert!(r.calibration.f_cal_updated > base.calibration.f_cal_updated, "{name}");
    }
    assert!(matching >= 1 && other >= 1, "the probe designs hold a match and others");
}

#[test]
fn the_calibration_note_s_match_claims_hold() {
    use magcoupling::engine::explain::probes::probe_designs;
    // The probe design without steel at the prototype's count and parts.
    let (_, matched) = probe_designs()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|(name, _)| *name == "304 back iron")
        .expect("the 304 probe design");
    let bench = compute_all(&matched);
    assert_eq!(bench.model.f_cal, bench.calibration.f_cal_updated);
    // Sentence 4: the rule ignores ring radius, gap and magnet length.
    let mut resized = matched.clone();
    resized.coupling.inner_back_apothem_mm = 20.0;
    resized.metal.face_gap_mm = 2.0;
    resized.coupling.magnets.axial_length_mm = Some(20.0);
    assert_eq!(compute_all(&resized).model.f_cal, bench.calibration.f_cal_updated);
    // Sentence 5: leaving the match (another magnet count) switches to the assumed factor.
    let mut left = matched.clone();
    left.coupling.npole = 8;
    assert_eq!(compute_all(&left).model.f_cal, left.calibration.f_cal_original);
    // The watch-out: "matching" the prototype inputs to the new count makes a match again, with
    // a factor far from the bench one: the prototype model at another count, not a measurement.
    let mut faked = left.clone();
    faked.calibration.total_magnets = 2 * faked.coupling.npole;
    let fake = compute_all(&faked);
    assert_eq!(fake.model.f_cal, fake.calibration.f_cal_updated);
    assert!(
        fake.model.f_cal / bench.model.f_cal - 1.0 > 0.4,
        "{} against the bench {}",
        fake.model.f_cal,
        bench.model.f_cal
    );
}
```

Engine facts (b0166ad, `compute_all`; values at the five probe designs "default", "8 magnets per
ring", "304 back iron", "Y30 ferrite, custom dimensions", "20 mm ring radius"):
- Hot-low = pull-out at `coupling.op_temp_C` × (1 − `metal.variation`); cold-high = cold
  pull-out at `metal.min_temp_C` × (1 + variation) (`src/engine/metal_design.rs:417-419`; records
  `records/torque.rs:207-210`). Hot-low 2.285, 1.673, 1.443, 0.1760, 2.158 N·m; cold-high 3.823,
  2.799, 2.414, 0.3381, 3.611 N·m; required 2.5 N·m: hot-low fails at all five.
- `metal.required_20C_Nm` = required / (Br factors at op × (1 − v)) (`metal_design.rs:438`):
  3.165 N·m (3.329 at Y30, whose rings use the grade's α). Hot-low >= required exactly when
  `model.pullout_20C_Nm` >= `metal.required_20C_Nm` (algebra of the two records; checked with the
  requirement at 0.99 and 1.01 × hot-low at all five).
- Clamp: `clamps.max_torque_Nm` = cold-high; `clamps.required_Nm` = it × `clamps.safety_factor`
  (`src/engine/clamps.rs:333`): 7.647 N·m at the default.
- Gearbox: `metal.cold_high_input_Nm` = cold-high / (ratio × efficiency) = 0.8049 N·m at the
  default against `coupling.gearbox_input_rating_Nm` 0.6 N·m; no dashboard row, guide or check
  compares them (BL-059).
- Hot-day start = hot ambient + driving rise (`src/engine/temperature.rs:906`): 65 °C; hot-day
  torque 2.589 N·m reads "Meets it nominally (no variation allowance)" while hot-low fails
  (`temperature.rs:1324-1336`).
- Levers, one slider step at all five designs: axial length (seeded 12.7 mm) +0.01 -> hot-low
  and cold-high up, clamp demand up; variation −0.005 -> hot-low up, cold-high down; operating
  temperature −0.5 °C -> hot-low up, cold-high unchanged to 1e-15; minimum temperature −0.5 °C ->
  cold-high up, hot-low bit-identical; operating temperature +0.5 °C -> pull-out down,
  `model.pullout_20C_Nm` unchanged; coefficient input +1e-5 (nearer zero) -> pull-out up and the
  cold torque down at the four library designs, nothing moves at Y30 (both rings graded:
  `src/engine/model.rs:420-425`); hot ambient +0.5 °C -> hot-day torque and
  `temperature.summary.margin_hot_day_C` down, pull-out unchanged.
- Grades on custom dimensions at 50 °C: N42SH keeps 0.929 of its 20 °C pull-out (2.688 N·m);
  SmCo_2_17_30 (α −0.035 %/°C) keeps 0.979 but gives 1.991 N·m; at 120 °C 2.240 against 1.894.

```rust
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```
