```rust
#[test]
fn the_torque_band_note_s_levers_move_hot_low_and_cold_high_as_it_says() {
    use magcoupling::engine::explain::notes::{Sense, Step};
    use magcoupling::engine::explain::probes::probe_designs;
    let note = notes::note("hot_low_cold_high").expect("the torque-band note");
    let levers: Vec<&str> = note.change.iter().map(|c| c.input).collect();
    assert_eq!(
        levers,
        [
            AXIAL_LENGTH,
            "metal.variation",
            "coupling.op_temp_C",
            "metal.min_temp_C",
        ]
    );
    assert!(matches!(note.change[0].step, Step::Raise));
    assert!(note.change[1..].iter().all(|c| matches!(c.step, Step::Lower)));
    let hot_low_up = Some(("metal.torque_hot_low_Nm", Sense::Up));
    assert_eq!(note.change[0].aim, hot_low_up);
    assert_eq!(note.change[1].aim, hot_low_up);
    assert_eq!(note.change[2].aim, hot_low_up);
    assert_eq!(note.change[3].aim, Some(("metal.torque_cold_high_Nm", Sense::Up)));
    let close = |a: f64, b: f64| (a / b - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12;
    for (name, design) in probe_designs() {
        let base = compute_all(&design);
        let (hot, cold) = (base.metal.torque_hot_low_Nm, base.metal.torque_cold_high_Nm);
        // Entry 1: longer magnets raise both edges (the trade-off it names) and the clamp's
        // demand with cold-high.
        let r = compute_all(&one_step_longer(&design));
        assert!(
            r.metal.torque_hot_low_Nm > hot && r.metal.torque_cold_high_Nm > cold,
            "{name}: length"
        );
        assert!(r.clamps.required_Nm > base.clamps.required_Nm, "{name}: clamp");
        // Entry 2: a smaller allowance narrows the band both ways.
        let mut d = design.clone();
        d.metal.variation -= lever_step("metal.variation");
        let r = compute_all(&d);
        assert!(
            r.metal.torque_hot_low_Nm > hot && r.metal.torque_cold_high_Nm < cold,
            "{name}: allowance"
        );
        // Entry 3: a cooler operating temperature raises hot-low; cold-high stays.
        let mut d = design.clone();
        d.coupling.op_temp_C -= lever_step("coupling.op_temp_C");
        let r = compute_all(&d);
        assert!(r.metal.torque_hot_low_Nm > hot, "{name}: operating");
        assert!(close(r.metal.torque_cold_high_Nm, cold), "{name}: cold-high stays");
        // Entry 4: a colder minimum raises cold-high; hot-low stays.
        let mut d = design.clone();
        d.metal.min_temp_C -= lever_step("metal.min_temp_C");
        let r = compute_all(&d);
        assert!(r.metal.torque_cold_high_Nm > cold, "{name}: minimum");
        assert_eq!(r.metal.torque_hot_low_Nm, hot, "{name}: hot-low stays");
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_torque_band_note_s_sentences_hold_at_every_probe_design() {
    use magcoupling::engine::explain::probes::probe_designs;
    let close = |a: f64, b: f64| (a / b - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12;
    for (name, design) in probe_designs() {
        let base = compute_all(&design);
        let m = &base.metal;
        // Sentence 3: the clamp is sized to cold-high times its safety factor.
        assert_eq!(base.clamps.max_torque_Nm, m.torque_cold_high_Nm, "{name}");
        assert!(
            close(
                base.clamps.required_Nm,
                m.torque_cold_high_Nm * design.clamps.safety_factor
            ),
            "{name}"
        );
        // Sentence 4: hot-low passes exactly when the 20 °C pull-out reaches the requirement
        // taken back to 20 °C with the allowance; the requirement just either side of hot-low.
        for scale in [0.99, 1.01] {
            let mut d = design.clone();
            d.metal.required_min_Nm = scale * m.torque_hot_low_Nm;
            let r = compute_all(&d);
            let passes = r.metal.torque_hot_low_Nm >= d.metal.required_min_Nm;
            assert_eq!(passes, scale < 1.0, "{name} at {scale}");
            assert_eq!(
                passes,
                r.model.pullout_20C_Nm >= r.metal.required_20C_Nm,
                "{name} at {scale}"
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_torque_band_note_s_watch_outs_hold() {
    // Watch-out 1: hot-low reads the operating temperature, not the hot-day start, and the
    // hot-day torque is compared with the requirement without the allowance: on the example
    // design hot-low fails while the hot-day torque meets the requirement.
    let defaults = DesignInputs::default();
    let r = compute_all(&defaults);
    let required = defaults.metal.required_min_Nm;
    assert!(r.metal.torque_hot_low_Nm < required);
    assert!(r.temperature.magnet_life.torque_hot_day_Nm >= required);
    assert_ne!(r.temperature.duty.hot_day_start_C, defaults.coupling.op_temp_C);
    let mut hotter_day = defaults.clone();
    hotter_day.temperature.duty.hot_ambient_C += lever_step("temperature.duty.hot_ambient_C");
    assert_eq!(
        compute_all(&hotter_day).metal.torque_hot_low_Nm,
        r.metal.torque_hot_low_Nm
    );
    // Watch-out 2: cold-high at the gearbox input is cold-high through the ratio and the
    // efficiency, above the input rating on the example design (the GUI test
    // `nothing_checks_a_gearbox_torque_against_its_rating_yet` holds the "nothing checks it").
    let c = &defaults.coupling;
    assert!(
        (r.metal.cold_high_input_Nm * c.gear_ratio * c.gear_efficiency
            / r.metal.torque_cold_high_Nm
            - 1.0)
            .abs()
            < 1e-12
    );
    assert!(r.metal.cold_high_input_Nm > c.gearbox_input_rating_Nm);
}

#[test]
fn the_temperature_note_s_levers_hold_at_every_probe_design() {
    use magcoupling::engine::explain::notes::{Sense, Step};
    use magcoupling::engine::explain::probes::probe_designs;
    let note = notes::note("br_temperature").expect("the temperature note");
    let levers: Vec<&str> = note.change.iter().map(|c| c.input).collect();
    assert_eq!(
        levers,
        [
            "coupling.op_temp_C",
            "calibration.alpha_br_per_C",
            "coupling.magnets.grade_inner",
            "temperature.duty.hot_ambient_C",
        ]
    );
    assert!(matches!(note.change[0].step, Step::Raise));
    assert!(matches!(note.change[1].step, Step::Raise));
    assert!(matches!(note.change[2].step, Step::Choose));
    assert!(matches!(note.change[3].step, Step::Raise));
    assert_eq!(note.change[0].aim, Some(("model.pullout_Nm", Sense::Down)));
    // The coefficient moves only library rings, and which way the torque goes depends on the
    // temperature: no single direction to check, so it is checked here, design by design.
    assert_eq!(note.change[1].aim, None);
    assert_eq!(note.change[2].aim, None);
    assert_eq!(
        note.change[3].aim,
        Some(("temperature.magnet_life.torque_hot_day_Nm", Sense::Down))
    );
    let close = |a: f64, b: f64| (a / b - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12;
    let (mut library, mut graded) = (0, 0);
    for (name, design) in probe_designs() {
        let base = compute_all(&design);
        // Entry 1: hotter running lowers the pull-out and hot-low, never the 20 °C row.
        let mut d = design.clone();
        d.coupling.op_temp_C += lever_step("coupling.op_temp_C");
        let r = compute_all(&d);
        assert!(r.model.pullout_Nm < base.model.pullout_Nm, "{name}");
        assert!(r.metal.torque_hot_low_Nm < base.metal.torque_hot_low_Nm, "{name}");
        assert!(close(r.model.pullout_20C_Nm, base.model.pullout_20C_Nm), "{name}");
        // Entry 2 and watch-out 1: the coefficient input moves only rings without a picked
        // grade; there, nearer zero, less is lost hot (the pull-out at the warmer operating
        // temperature rises) and less is gained cold (the cold torque falls).
        let mut d = design.clone();
        d.calibration.alpha_br_per_C += lever_step("calibration.alpha_br_per_C");
        let r = compute_all(&d);
        let inner = r.model.inner_alpha_br_per_C != base.model.inner_alpha_br_per_C;
        let outer = r.model.outer_alpha_br_per_C != base.model.outer_alpha_br_per_C;
        assert_eq!(inner, outer, "{name}: the probe designs have both rings of one kind");
        if inner {
            library += 1;
            assert!(design.coupling.op_temp_C > 20.0, "{name}: runs warm");
            assert!(r.model.pullout_Nm > base.model.pullout_Nm, "{name}");
            assert!(r.metal.torque_cold_Nm < base.metal.torque_cold_Nm, "{name}");
        } else {
            graded += 1;
            assert_eq!(r.model.pullout_Nm, base.model.pullout_Nm, "{name}");
            assert_eq!(r.metal.torque_cold_Nm, base.metal.torque_cold_Nm, "{name}");
        }
        // Entry 4: a hotter day lowers the hot-day torque and its temperature margin, not the
        // pull-out at the operating temperature.
        let mut d = design.clone();
        d.temperature.duty.hot_ambient_C += lever_step("temperature.duty.hot_ambient_C");
        let r = compute_all(&d);
        assert!(
            r.temperature.magnet_life.torque_hot_day_Nm
                < base.temperature.magnet_life.torque_hot_day_Nm,
            "{name}"
        );
        assert!(
            r.temperature.summary.margin_hot_day_C < base.temperature.summary.margin_hot_day_C,
            "{name}"
        );
        assert_eq!(r.model.pullout_Nm, base.model.pullout_Nm, "{name}");
    }
    assert!(library >= 1 && graded >= 1, "library and graded rings among the probes");
}

#[test]
fn only_a_ring_with_a_picked_grade_keeps_its_own_coefficient() {
    // Watch-out 1 of the temperature note, on a mixed design: the inner ring on custom
    // dimensions with Y30, the outer on its library part; the input moves the outer ring only.
    let mut mixed = DesignInputs::default();
    mixed.coupling.magnets.part_inner = String::new();
    mixed.coupling.magnets.grade_inner = "Y30".to_owned();
    let base = compute_all(&mixed);
    let mut moved = mixed.clone();
    moved.calibration.alpha_br_per_C += lever_step("calibration.alpha_br_per_C");
    let r = compute_all(&moved);
    assert_eq!(r.model.inner_alpha_br_per_C, base.model.inner_alpha_br_per_C);
    assert_eq!(r.model.outer_alpha_br_per_C, moved.calibration.alpha_br_per_C);
    assert_ne!(base.model.inner_alpha_br_per_C, base.model.outer_alpha_br_per_C);
}

#[test]
fn a_grade_nearer_zero_loses_less_when_hot_but_starts_weaker() {
    // Entry 3 of the temperature note: both rings on custom dimensions with one grade.
    let graded = |grade: &str| {
        let mut d = DesignInputs::default();
        let m = &mut d.coupling.magnets;
        m.part_inner = String::new();
        m.part_outer = String::new();
        m.grade_inner = grade.to_owned();
        m.grade_outer = grade.to_owned();
        compute_all(&d)
    };
    let (ndfeb, smco) = (graded("N42SH"), graded("SmCo_2_17_30"));
    let kept = |r: &DesignResults| r.model.pullout_Nm / r.model.pullout_20C_Nm;
    assert!(smco.model.inner_alpha_br_per_C.abs() < ndfeb.model.inner_alpha_br_per_C.abs());
    assert!(kept(&smco) > kept(&ndfeb), "loses less when hot");
    assert!(smco.model.pullout_Nm < ndfeb.model.pullout_Nm, "starts weaker");
}
```

```rust
    /// Words as the spec's caps count them (slice-2 spec 3.1): whitespace-separated, each
    /// `{result.path}` placeholder counted as two (its value and its unit, as it renders).
    fn cap_words(text: &str) -> usize {
        text.split_whitespace().count() + text.matches('{').count()
    }

    /// The slice-2 caps for the note `id` (spec 3.1): 3 to 5 sentences of at most 25 words,
    /// the first with no placeholder, ϑ, superscript minus or ∝ (it is counted raw on screen);
    /// 1 to 5 change entries of at most 25 words; at most 2 watch-outs of at most 30 words.
    /// T4's cap test holds every note to the same caps once T18 un-ignores it.
    fn assert_caps(id: &str) {
        let n = note(id).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no note {id}"));
        assert!(
            (3..=5).contains(&n.sentences.len()),
            "{id}: {} sentences",
            n.sentences.len()
        );
        for s in n.sentences {
            assert!(cap_words(s) <= 25, "{id}: {} words: {s}", cap_words(s));
        }
        for glyph in ['{', '}', '\u{3d1}', '\u{207b}', '\u{221d}'] {
            assert!(
                !n.sentences[0].contains(glyph),
                "{id}: sentence 0 holds {glyph:?}"
            );
        }
        assert!(
            (1..=5).contains(&n.change.len()),
            "{id}: {} change entries",
            n.change.len()
        );
        for c in n.change {
            assert!(
                cap_words(c.text) <= 25,
                "{id}: {} words: {}",
                cap_words(c.text),
                c.text
            );
        }
        assert!(
            n.watch_out.len() <= 2,
            "{id}: {} watch-outs",
            n.watch_out.len()
        );
        for w in n.watch_out {
            assert!(cap_words(w) <= 30, "{id}: {} words: {w}", cap_words(w));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_slip_notes_keep_the_caps() {
        for id in ["when_slipping", "slip_heating", "thermal_time_constant"] {
            assert_caps(id);
        }
    }

        for path in ["model.gearbox_input_ripple_Nm", "metal.slip_freq_Hz"] {
```

```rust
    #[test]
    fn the_heating_curve_marks_the_limit_and_the_time_to_reach_it() {
        // The thermal note's "time to the limit" (TC-24): how long unbroken slip takes to heat
        // the coupling to its limit, a level below the steady temperature that the rise crosses.
        let rect = Rect::from_min_size(pos2(40.0, 30.0), DIAGRAM_SIZE);
        let (shapes, texts) = shapes_of(Diagram::HeatingCurve, rect);
        for want in [
            "\u{3c4}_th: 63 %",
            "steady temperature",
            "limit",
            "time to the limit",
        ] {
            assert!(texts.iter().any(|t| t == want), "{want}: {texts:?}");
        }
        let curve = only_path(&shapes);
        let (left, right, bottom) = (curve[0].x, curve[curve.len() - 1].x, curve[0].y);
        let levels: Vec<f32> = horizontal_lines(&shapes)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|y| *y < bottom - 1.0)
            .collect();
        let steady = levels.iter().copied().reduce(f32::min).expect("the steady level");
        let limit = levels.iter().copied().reduce(f32::max).expect("the limit");
        assert!(limit > steady + 1.0, "a limit below the steady level: {levels:?}");
        let rise = |y: f32| (bottom - y) / (bottom - steady);
        assert!((rise(limit) - LIMIT_SHARE).abs() < 1e-4, "{}", rise(limit));
        // One dashed guide from the limit down to the time axis, where the curve reaches the
        // limit: rise = 1 - e^(-t/τ_th), five time constants across the plot.
        let guides: Vec<[Pos2; 2]> = shapes
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|s| match s {
                Shape::LineSegment { points: [a, b], .. }
                    if a.x == b.x && a.y != b.y && (a.x - left).abs() > 1.0 =>
                {
                    Some([*a, *b])
                }
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect();
        assert!(!guides.is_empty(), "the time-to-the-limit guide");
        let x = guides[0][0].x;
        assert!(guides.iter().all(|[a, _]| (a.x - x).abs() < 1e-3), "{guides:?}");
        let ys = || guides.iter().flat_map(|g| g.iter().map(|p| p.y));
        let top = ys().fold(f32::INFINITY, f32::min);
        let foot = ys().fold(f32::NEG_INFINITY, f32::max);
        assert!((top - limit).abs() < 1e-3, "{top} {limit}");
        assert!(bottom - foot <= 6.5, "{foot} {bottom}");
        let time_constants = (x - left) / (right - left) * 5.0;
        assert!(
            (time_constants + (1.0 - LIMIT_SHARE).ln()).abs() < 1e-3,
            "{time_constants}"
        );
        assert!((y_at(curve, x) - limit).abs() < 0.5, "{} {limit}", y_at(curve, x));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_heating_curve_s_labels_do_not_overlap() {
        let rect = Rect::from_min_size(pos2(40.0, 30.0), DIAGRAM_SIZE);
        let (shapes, _) = shapes_of(Diagram::HeatingCurve, rect);
        let labels: Vec<(String, Rect)> = shapes
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|s| match s {
                Shape::Text(t) => Some((
                    t.galley.text().to_owned(),
                    t.galley.rect.translate(t.pos.to_vec2()),
                )),
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(labels.len(), 5, "{labels:?}");
        for (i, (a, ra)) in labels.iter().enumerate() {
            for (b, rb) in &labels[i + 1..] {
                assert!(!ra.intersects(*rb), "{a:?} {ra:?} overlaps {b:?} {rb:?}");
            }
        }
    }
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Draw the limit and the time to reach it**

In `magcoupling-rs/src/gui/diagrams.rs`:

7a. Module doc: replace

```rust
//! demagnetization curve with its knee and three load lines; first-order heating with the time
//! constant at 63 %.
```

with

```rust
//! demagnetization curve with its knee and three load lines; first-order heating with the time
//! constant at 63 %, a limit below the steady temperature and the time the rise takes to reach
//! it.
```

7b. Replace the whole `heating_curve` function, from its doc line
`/// First-order heating toward a steady temperature over five time constants, τ at 63 %.`
through its closing `}` (just above `/// Allocates [`DIAGRAM_SIZE`] and paints the diagram`), with:

```rust
/// The heating curve's temperature limit as a share of its steady rise: below the steady
/// temperature, so the rise crosses it (the case "time to the limit" names), and late enough
/// (2.66 time constants) that the crossing's guide clears the τ_th label.
const LIMIT_SHARE: f32 = 0.93;

/// First-order heating toward a steady temperature over five time constants: τ_th at 63 %, a
/// temperature limit below the steady level, and the time the rise takes to reach it.
fn heating_curve(fonts: &Fonts, r: Rect, pens: &Pens) -> Vec<Shape> {
    let plot = Rect::from_min_max(
        pos2(r.left() + 14.0, r.top() + 4.0),
        pos2(r.right(), r.bottom() - 14.0),
    );
    let span = 5.0;
    let rise = |t: f32| 1.0 - (-t * span).exp();
    let tau = pos2(
        plot.left() + plot.width() / span,
        plot.bottom() - rise(1.0 / span) / 1.1 * plot.height(),
    );
    let steady = plot.bottom() - plot.height() / 1.1;
    let limit = plot.bottom() - LIMIT_SHARE / 1.1 * plot.height();
    // The rise reaches LIMIT_SHARE of the steady rise after -ln(1 - LIMIT_SHARE) time
    // constants, five of which span the plot.
    let reach = plot.left() - (1.0 - LIMIT_SHARE).ln() / span * plot.width();
    let mut shapes = vec![
        Shape::line_segment(
            [plot.left_bottom(), plot.right_bottom()],
            Stroke::new(1.0, pens.weak),
        ),
        Shape::line_segment(
            [plot.left_bottom(), plot.left_top()],
            Stroke::new(1.0, pens.weak),
        ),
        Shape::line(
            curve(plot, 0.0, 1.1, 121, rise),
            Stroke::new(1.5, pens.first),
        ),
        Shape::circle_filled(tau, 3.5, pens.second),
        label(
            fonts,
            tau + vec2(6.0, 2.0),
            Align2::LEFT_TOP,
            "τ_th: 63 %",
            pens.second,
        ),
        label(
            fonts,
            plot.right_bottom(),
            Align2::RIGHT_TOP,
            "time slipping",
            pens.ink,
        ),
    ];
    shapes.extend(Shape::dashed_line(
        &[pos2(plot.left(), steady), pos2(plot.right(), steady)],
        Stroke::new(1.0, pens.weak),
        4.0,
        3.0,
    ));
    shapes.push(label(
        fonts,
        pos2(plot.right(), steady - 2.0),
        Align2::RIGHT_BOTTOM,
        "steady temperature",
        pens.weak,
    ));
    shapes.extend(Shape::dashed_line(
        &[pos2(plot.left(), limit), pos2(plot.right(), limit)],
        Stroke::new(1.0, pens.north),
        4.0,
        3.0,
    ));
    shapes.push(label(
        fonts,
        pos2(plot.left() + 3.0, limit + 2.0),
        Align2::LEFT_TOP,
        "limit",
        pens.north,
    ));
    shapes.extend(Shape::dashed_line(
        &[pos2(reach, limit), pos2(reach, plot.bottom())],
        Stroke::new(1.0, pens.weak),
        3.0,
        3.0,
    ));
    shapes.push(label(
        fonts,
        pos2(reach, plot.bottom() + 1.0),
        Align2::CENTER_TOP,
        "time to the limit",
        pens.weak,
    ));
    shapes
}
```

(Layout checked with egui 0.32.3's default proportional font at 11 points: "time to the limit"
76.2 points wide centred 139 points into the 262-point plot, "time slipping" 62.1 points at the
right edge, "limit" 22.2 points at the left; the τ_th label ends 33 points left of the guide.)

```rust
    /// The text a note draws as prose: its sentences, its change entries' texts and its
    /// watch-outs (titles and sources aside).
    fn note_texts(n: &Note) -> Vec<&'static str> {
        n.sentences
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .chain(n.change.iter().map(|c| c.text))
            .chain(n.watch_out.iter().copied())
            .collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_demagnetization_and_clamp_notes_keep_the_caps() {
        for id in ["demagnetization", "ferrite_cold_demag", "clamp_preload"] {
            assert_caps(id);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_demagnetization_and_clamp_notes_own_the_rows_spec_3_3_gives_them() {
        let owner = |path: &str| note_for_any_status(path).map(|n| n.id);
        for path in [
            "temperature.magnet_life.margin_onset_C",
            "temperature.magnet_life.margin_limit_C",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(owner(path), Some("demagnetization"), "{path}");
        }
        for path in ["clamps.max_torque_Nm", "clamps.required_Nm"] {
            assert_eq!(owner(path), Some("clamp_preload"), "{path}");
        }
        // R7: the ferrite note drops the NdFeB knee picture, which shows the knee moving the
        // wrong way for ferrite; the demagnetization note keeps it.
        assert_eq!(note("ferrite_cold_demag").map(|n| n.diagram), Some(None));
        assert_eq!(
            note("demagnetization").map(|n| n.diagram),
            Some(Some(Diagram::DemagKnee))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_rewritten_notes_type_no_editable_default() {
        // Spec section 8 (slice 1, trap 6) and audit theme T6: a note never presents an
        // editable default (a stored reverse field, the knee fraction, the design margin, the
        // clamp's friction, preload share or stripping factor) as a fact about the design.
        let d = crate::DesignInputs::default();
        let demag = &d.temperature.demag;
        let mut demag_defaults: Vec<String> = [
            demag.h_rev_aligned_kA_m,
            demag.h_rev_pullout_kA_m,
            demag.h_rev_likepole_kA_m,
            demag.h_rev_single_ring_kA_m,
        ]
        .iter()
        .map(|h| format!("{h}"))
        .collect();
        demag_defaults.push(format!("{} °C", demag.design_margin_C));
        demag_defaults.push(format!("{}", demag.knee_fraction));
        let c = &d.clamps;
        let clamp_defaults = [
            format!("{}", c.friction),
            format!("{}", c.preload_fraction),
            format!("{} %", c.preload_fraction * 100.0),
            format!("{}", c.strip_sf),
        ];
        for (id, defaults) in [
            ("demagnetization", &demag_defaults[..]),
            ("ferrite_cold_demag", &demag_defaults[..]),
            ("clamp_preload", &clamp_defaults[..]),
        ] {
            for text in note_texts(note(id).unwrap()) {
                for value in defaults {
                    assert!(!text.contains(value.as_str()), "{id}: {value:?} in {text:?}");
                }
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn no_note_says_the_coupling_protects_the_gearbox() {
        // BL-059 and spec section 8: nothing checks the cold-high torque at the gearbox input
        // against a rating, so no note may claim the coupling protects the gearbox.
        for n in NOTES {
            for text in note_texts(n) {
                let lower = text.to_lowercase();
                assert!(
                    !(lower.contains("gearbox") && lower.contains("protect")),
                    "{}: {text}",
                    n.id
                );
            }
        }
    }
```


with

```rust
/// What the start-here bar adds on the ferrite step: its check reads n/a on NdFeB rings (spec
/// 3.3, TC-32).
pub const FERRITE_ONLY: &str = "(ferrite rings only)";

/// The start of the start-here bar: "Start here 13 of 14 (ferrite rings only): <title>" on the
/// ferrite step, the step and its title alone on every other one.
pub fn start_here_text(step: usize) -> String {
    let (id, _) = START_HERE[step];
    let title = reviewed_note(id).map_or_else(String::new, |n| glyph_safe(n.title));
    let only = if id == "ferrite_cold_demag" {
        format!(" {FERRITE_ONLY}")
    } else {
        String::new()
    };
    format!(
        "{START_HERE_BUTTON} {} of {}{only}: {title}",
        step + 1,
        START_HERE.len()
    )
}
```

At the end of the same `mod tests` (after `fn steel_rules_need_the_steel_circuit() { ... }`,

```rust
    // ---- R11 (slice 2): which library picks fire which rule, through the whole engine. The
    // ---- warning notes name these picks, so these tests pin what the notes say.

    /// The rule ids that fire on `inputs`, through the whole engine (`api::compute` feeds the rules
    /// the materials in effect).
    fn fired_on(inputs: &DesignInputs) -> Vec<&'static str> {
        let results = compute_all(inputs);
        WARNING_RULES
            .iter()
            .filter(|rule| {
                results.get(&format!("warnings.{}", rule.id)) != Some(Value::Text(String::new()))
            })
            .map(|rule| rule.id)
            .collect()
    }

    /// The default design with the back iron `code`, the circuit selector `circuit` (1 steel, 0
    /// none) and `plating_mm` of plating per surface.
    fn with_back_iron(code: i64, circuit: i64, plating_mm: f64) -> DesignInputs {
        let mut inputs = DesignInputs::default();
        inputs.materials.parts.back_iron = code;
        inputs.coupling.backiron = circuit;
        inputs.materials.nickel.thickness_mm = plating_mm;
        inputs
    }

    /// The back-iron codes whose pick fires `rule` on the circuit `circuit` at `plating_mm`.
    fn back_irons_firing(rule: &str, circuit: i64, plating_mm: f64) -> Vec<i64> {
        BACK_IRON_CHOICES
            .iter()
            .map(|&(code, _)| code)
            .filter(|&code| fired_on(&with_back_iron(code, circuit, plating_mm)).contains(&rule))
            .collect()
    }

    /// The name a note gives a library back iron: its id's leading token ("12L14_cold_drawn" ->
    /// "12L14", "17-4PH_H900" -> "17-4PH").
    fn short_name(code: i64) -> &'static str {
        let id = BACK_IRON_CHOICES
            .iter()
            .find(|&&(c, _)| c == code)
            .map(|&(_, id)| id)
            .unwrap();
        id.split('_').next().unwrap()
    }

    /// The default plating per surface (above zero).
    fn plated() -> f64 {
        DesignInputs::default().materials.nickel.thickness_mm
    }

    #[test]
    fn low_saturation_fires_for_12l14_416_and_both_17_4ph_conditions_only() {
        // R11: on the steel circuit, the back irons with no design flux density of their own or a
        // sourced saturation below LOW_SATURATION_T fire it; with the circuit off nothing can.
        let fires = back_irons_firing("low_saturation", 1, plated());
        assert_eq!(fires, [3, 4, 5, 6]);
        // The same codes from the library's own data: the rule and the data agree.
        let from_data: Vec<i64> = BACK_IRON_CHOICES
            .iter()
            .filter(|&&(code, id)| {
                let m = material(id).unwrap();
                m.ferromagnetic
                    && (m.bsat_T.value.is_some_and(|b| b < LOW_SATURATION_T)
                        || (code != BACK_IRON_CHOICES[0].0 && m.design_flux_density_T.is_none()))
            })
            .map(|&(code, _)| code)
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(fires, from_data);
        let names: Vec<&str> = fires.iter().map(|&code| short_name(code)).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, ["12L14", "416", "17-4PH", "17-4PH"]);
        assert!(back_irons_firing("low_saturation", 0, plated()).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn uncoated_fires_for_4140_1018_and_12l14_at_zero_plating_only() {
        // R11: the plain and low-alloy steels, unplated, on the steel circuit.
        assert!(plated() > 0.0);
        let bare = back_irons_firing("uncoated_low_alloy_steel", 1, 0.0);
        assert_eq!(bare, [1, 2, 3]);
        let from_data: Vec<i64> = BACK_IRON_CHOICES
            .iter()
            .filter(|&&(_, id)| {
                let m = material(id).unwrap();
                m.ferromagnetic && m.needs_plating
            })
            .map(|&(code, _)| code)
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(bare, from_data);
        let names: Vec<&str> = bare.iter().map(|&code| short_name(code)).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, ["4140", "1018", "12L14"]);
        assert!(back_irons_firing("uncoated_low_alloy_steel", 1, plated()).is_empty());
        assert!(back_irons_firing("uncoated_low_alloy_steel", 0, 0.0).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_open_circuit_and_expansion_rules_fire_for_304_and_6061_or_the_circuit_switched_off() {
        // R11: a non-magnetic pick selects free space; so does the circuit selector at 0 with any
        // pick. Either way the hub is non-magnetic metal, and its expansion is past the limit.
        let non_magnetic: Vec<i64> = BACK_IRON_CHOICES
            .iter()
            .filter(|&&(_, id)| !material(id).unwrap().ferromagnetic)
            .map(|&(code, _)| code)
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(non_magnetic, [7, 8]);
        let names: Vec<&str> = non_magnetic.iter().map(|&code| short_name(code)).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, ["304", "6061"]);
        let every: Vec<i64> = BACK_IRON_CHOICES.iter().map(|&(code, _)| code).collect();
        for rule in ["non_ferromagnetic_back_iron", "cte_mismatch_with_magnets"] {
            assert_eq!(back_irons_firing(rule, 1, plated()), non_magnetic, "{rule}");
            assert_eq!(
                back_irons_firing(rule, 0, plated()),
                every,
                "{rule}: circuit off"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn with_plating_only_4140_and_1018_fire_no_warning() {
        // R11: 416, 17-4PH and 12L14 trade the plating caution for the low-saturation one.
        let quiet: Vec<i64> = BACK_IRON_CHOICES
            .iter()
            .map(|&(code, _)| code)
            .filter(|&code| fired_on(&with_back_iron(code, 1, plated())).is_empty())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(quiet, [1, 2]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn no_sleeve_choice_fires_a_sleeve_warning_but_a_316l_conductivity_typed_above_the_threshold_does()
    {
        // R11: every listed sleeve and liner is non-magnetic and conducts no better than 316L.
        for &(code, id) in &SLEEVE_LINER_CHOICES {
            let mut inputs = DesignInputs::default();
            inputs.materials.parts.sleeve_liner = code;
            let fired = fired_on(&inputs);
            assert!(fired.is_empty(), "{id}: {fired:?}");
            assert!(!material(id).unwrap().ferromagnetic, "{id}");
        }
        // The threshold is a constant, not the 316L entry: 316L typed above it fires the caution;
        // another pick, which overrides that entry, does not.
        let mut typed = DesignInputs::default();
        typed.temperature.slip_loss.sigma_316_S_m = SLEEVE_SIGMA_BASELINE_S_M * 1.01;
        assert_eq!(fired_on(&typed), ["high_conductivity_sleeve_or_liner"]);
        typed.materials.parts.sleeve_liner = SLEEVE_LINER_CHOICES[1].0;
        assert!(fired_on(&typed).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn each_back_iron_warning_note_names_the_library_picks_that_fire_it() {
        // The notes list the steels by name; the library decides which fire. A library change that
        // moves a pick in or out of a rule fails here until the note follows.
        let cases = [
            (
                "low_saturation",
                back_irons_firing("low_saturation", 1, plated()),
            ),
            (
                "uncoated_low_alloy_steel",
                back_irons_firing("uncoated_low_alloy_steel", 1, 0.0),
            ),
            (
                "non_ferromagnetic_back_iron",
                back_irons_firing("non_ferromagnetic_back_iron", 1, plated()),
            ),
            (
                "cte_mismatch_with_magnets",
                back_irons_firing("cte_mismatch_with_magnets", 1, plated()),
            ),
        ];
        for (rule_id, codes) in cases {
            let rule = WARNING_RULES.iter().find(|r| r.id == rule_id).unwrap();
            let text = note(rule.note_id).unwrap().sentences.join(" ");
            assert!(!codes.is_empty(), "{rule_id} fires for some pick");
            for code in codes {
                let name = short_name(code);
                assert!(
                    text.contains(name),
                    "{}: the note names {name}",
                    rule.note_id
                );
            }
        }
    }
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the widened release gate and the three new engine tests**

In `magcoupling-rs/tests/explain.rs`, replace the whole block from
`/// The A4 accuracy gate for release (the M4 hands-on checklist runs it): every note the` through the closing `}` of
`fn release_notes_are_reviewed()` (HEAD :1033-1055) with:

```rust
/// The A4 accuracy gate for release (spec section 4, test 7), on since slice 2: every note a
/// user can open by id has passed the physics review: each "start here" step's, each A5
/// warning's and, with the `gui` feature, each check guide's and each dashboard row's Why note
/// (gate 7 runs that part, gate 4 the rest). `note_for` keeps a draft off the screen; this
/// keeps a draft out of a release.
#[test]
fn release_notes_are_reviewed() {
    let mut linked: Vec<&str> = notes::START_HERE.iter().map(|(id, _)| *id).collect();
    linked.extend(
        magcoupling::engine::warnings::WARNING_RULES
            .iter()
            .map(|r| r.note_id),
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "gui")]
    {
        use magcoupling::gui::guidance::{CHECK_GUIDES, Learn, ROW_LEARN};
        let guides = CHECK_GUIDES.iter().map(|g| g.learn);
        let rows = ROW_LEARN.iter().map(|&(_, learn)| learn);
        let before = linked.len();
        linked.extend(guides.chain(rows).filter_map(|learn| match learn {
            Learn::Note(id) => Some(id),
            Learn::Assumption(_) | Learn::None(_) => None,
        }));
        assert!(
            linked.len() > before,
            "the guides and the rows link notes (the widened gate is not vacuous)"
        );
    }
    linked.sort_unstable();
    linked.dedup();
    let drafts: Vec<&str> = linked
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|id| {
            !matches!(
                notes::note(id).map(|n| n.review),
                Some(notes::Review::Reviewed { .. })
            )
        })
        .collect();
    assert!(drafts.is_empty(), "not yet reviewed: {drafts:?}");
}

/// Spec section 4 (S2-6): every note ships as reviewed by the slice-2 physics review, its
/// record names its own section of the committed review report, and the report holds that
/// section exactly once (a re-review goes under the note's section as a `###` subsection).
#[test]
fn every_note_names_its_committed_review_section() {
    const REPORT: &str = "docs/analyses/2026-10-14-magcoupler-notes-review.md";
    let report = include_str!("../../docs/analyses/2026-10-14-magcoupler-notes-review.md");
    let iso_date = |date: &str| {
        date.len() == 10
            && date.bytes().enumerate().all(|(i, b)| {
                if i == 4 || i == 7 {
                    b == b'-'
                } else {
                    b.is_ascii_digit()
                }
            })
    };
    for n in notes::NOTES {
        let notes::Review::Reviewed {
            reviewer,
            date,
            record,
        } = n.review
        else {
            panic!("{}: not reviewed", n.id);
        };
        assert_eq!(reviewer, "physics reviewer (session model)", "{}", n.id);
        assert!(iso_date(date), "{}: {date}", n.id);
        assert_eq!(record, format!("{REPORT}#{}", n.id), "{}", n.id);
        let heading = format!("## {}", n.id);
        let sections = report
            .lines()
            .filter(|line| line.trim_end() == heading)
            .count();
        assert_eq!(sections, 1, "{}: its section of {REPORT}", n.id);
    }
}

/// Spec 3.3 (R4) and section 6 test 5: Start here is fourteen steps, the torque note first,
/// each note once, each step opening an equation its note explains; with the six warning
/// notes that is every note.
#[test]
fn start_here_is_the_fourteen_step_order() {
    let order: Vec<&str> = notes::START_HERE.iter().map(|&(id, _)| id).collect();
    assert_eq!(
        order,
        [
            "torque_from_shear",
            "harmonics",
            "back_iron_factor",
            "pullout_angle",
            "end_effect",
            "calibration",
            "br_temperature",
            "hot_low_cold_high",
            "when_slipping",
            "slip_heating",
            "thermal_time_constant",
            "demagnetization",
            "ferrite_cold_demag",
            "clamp_preload",
        ]
    );
    for &(id, path) in notes::START_HERE {
        let note = notes::note(id).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no note {id}"));
        assert!(
            note.equations.iter().any(|e| notes::covers(e, path)),
            "start here {id}: the note does not explain {path}"
        );
    }
    let mut reached: BTreeSet<&str> = order.iter().copied().collect();
    assert_eq!(reached.len(), order.len(), "each note once");
    reached.extend(
        magcoupling::engine::warnings::WARNING_RULES
            .iter()
            .map(|r| r.note_id),
    );
    let all: BTreeSet<&str> = notes::NOTES.iter().map(|n| n.id).collect();
    assert_eq!(reached, all, "every note is a Start here step or a warning's note");
}

/// The note, help and guide checks this slice wrote red and ignored run for good (spec section
/// 6, tests 1, 7 and 9): in the files that hold them only the review tools stay ignored, the
/// tests that print or write a file for a reviewer instead of checking anything.
#[test]
fn only_the_review_tools_are_ignored() {
    const TOOLS: [&str; 4] = [
        "review_sheet",
        "guidance_strings_for_review",
        "notes_for_review",
        "notes_signoff_sheet",
    ];
    let sources = [
        (
            "src/engine/explain/notes.rs",
            include_str!("../src/engine/explain/notes.rs"),
        ),
        ("src/gui/plain_text.rs", include_str!("../src/gui/plain_text.rs")),
        ("src/gui/explorer.rs", include_str!("../src/gui/explorer.rs")),
        ("src/gui/guidance.rs", include_str!("../src/gui/guidance.rs")),
        ("tests/explain.rs", include_str!("explain.rs")),
    ];
    // Spelled in two pieces, so that this file's own text does not hold the attribute.
    let attribute = concat!("#[", "ignore");
    let mut checks = Vec::new();
    for (file, text) in sources {
        for (at, _) in text.match_indices(attribute) {
            let name = text[at..]
                .split_once("fn ")
                .and_then(|(_, rest)| rest.split('(').next())
                .unwrap_or("?")
                .trim();
            if !TOOLS.contains(&name) {
                checks.push(format!("{file}: {name}"));
            }
        }
    }
    assert!(checks.is_empty(), "ignored checks: {checks:?}");
}
```

```rust
/// The text of a Why link drawn outside a dashboard row: "Why: " and the note's title, one
/// link (a warning's; the Size tab's and the end-effect banner's, spec 3.7). Not a "Why:" label
/// and the bare title: Start here draws its step's title exactly once, and the Size tab links
/// its first step's note.
pub fn why_note_text(note: &notes::Note) -> String {
    format!("{WHY}: {}", glyph_safe(note.title))
}

/// Draws the Why link to the note `id` ([`why_note_text`]); nothing for a note that has not
/// passed review (the release gate keeps every linked note reviewed). Returns whether it was
/// clicked.
pub(crate) fn why_note_link(ui: &mut egui::Ui, id: &str) -> bool {
    reviewed_note(id).is_some_and(|note| ui.link(why_note_text(note)).clicked())
}

/// The end-effect banner while f_end <= 0 ([`end_effect_banner`]), drawn over the dashboard and
/// over the centre region (decision M42-1), with the Why link to the end-effect check's note
/// under it (spec 3.7, CG-10), which asks for that note. Returns whether the banner shows.
pub(crate) fn end_effect_banner_ui(
    ui: &mut egui::Ui,
    results: &DesignResults,
    readouts: &mut Readouts,
) -> bool {
    let Some(banner) = end_effect_banner(results) else {
        return false;
    };
    ui.colored_label(ui.visuals().error_fg_color, banner);
    if why_note_link(ui, BANNER_NOTE) {
        readouts.open_note(BANNER_NOTE);
    }
    true
}
```

```rust
    /// The fewest steps from `path` down the registry's terms to every path upstream of it,
    /// level by level (the test's own walk, apart from `upstream_nearest_first`'s queue).
    fn depths(path: &str) -> std::collections::BTreeMap<String, usize> {
        let mut depth = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
        let mut level = BTreeSet::from([path.to_owned()]);
        let mut steps = 0;
        while !level.is_empty() {
            steps += 1;
            let next: BTreeSet<String> = level
                .iter()
                .filter_map(|p| registry().equation_for(p))
                .flat_map(|eq| eq.terms.iter().cloned())
                .filter(|t| t != path && !depth.contains_key(t))
                .collect();
            for t in &next {
                depth.insert(t.clone(), steps);
            }
            level = next;
        }
        depth
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_offered_note_is_the_nearest_upstream_and_a_note_outranks_an_assumption() {
        // TC-29a, TC-30, over every explained result without a note of its own and without a
        // dashboard Why link (those lead first: the next test).
        let assumption_paths =
            |p: &str| ASSUMPTIONS.iter().any(|a| a.paths.contains(&p));
        let mut seen = [0_usize; 3];
        for eq in registry().equations() {
            let path = eq.target.as_str();
            if notes::note_for(path).is_some() || row_learn(path).is_some() {
                continue;
            }
            let depth = depths(path);
            let nearest_note = depth
                .iter()
                .filter(|(p, _)| notes::note_for(p).is_some())
                .map(|(_, &d)| d)
                .min();
            let nearest_assumption = depth
                .iter()
                .filter(|(p, _)| assumption_paths(p))
                .map(|(_, &d)| d)
                .min();
            match note_fallback(path) {
                NoteFallback::Note(note) => {
                    seen[0] += 1;
                    let at = depth
                        .iter()
                        .filter(|(p, _)| notes::note_for(p).map(|n| n.id) == Some(note.id))
                        .map(|(_, &d)| d)
                        .min();
                    assert_eq!(at, nearest_note, "{path}: {}", note.id);
                }
                NoteFallback::Assumption(assumption) => {
                    seen[1] += 1;
                    assert_eq!(nearest_note, None, "{path}: a note upstream outranks {}", assumption.id);
                    let at = depth
                        .iter()
                        .filter(|(p, _)| assumption.paths.contains(&p.as_str()))
                        .map(|(_, &d)| d)
                        .min();
                    assert_eq!(at, nearest_assumption, "{path}: {}", assumption.id);
                }
                NoteFallback::Reason(reason) => {
                    seen[2] += 1;
                    assert_eq!(reason, NO_NOTE, "{path}");
                    assert_eq!((nearest_note, nearest_assumption), (None, None), "{path}");
                }
            }
        }
        assert!(seen.iter().all(|&n| n > 0), "each kind of offer occurs: {seen:?}");
    }
```

```rust
/// What Explain offers under an equation no reviewed note explains (spec 3.7, TC-29a, TC-30).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum NoteFallback {
    /// A reviewed note to read instead.
    Note(&'static Note),
    /// An assumption whose rationale explains the value.
    Assumption(&'static Assumption),
    /// Neither: why (a dashboard row's own reason, or [`NO_NOTE`]).
    Reason(&'static str),
}

/// [`NoteFallback`] for `path`, in this order: the dashboard row's Why link, when it leads to a
/// reviewed note or an assumption (what the row itself says); else the reviewed note of the
/// nearest result upstream (what `path` is computed from, fewest steps first, ties to the term
/// its equation lists first); else the nearest assumption upstream; else the dashboard row's
/// reason for having no note; else [`NO_NOTE`]. A reviewed note anywhere upstream outranks any
/// assumption: a note explains more than a rationale. The walk runs on every frame Explain
/// shows it: a few hundred paths at most.
pub fn note_fallback(path: &str) -> NoteFallback {
    let row = row_learn(path);
    if let Some(Learn::Note(id)) = row
        && let Some(note) = reviewed_note(id)
    {
        return NoteFallback::Note(note);
    }
    if let Some(Learn::Assumption(id)) = row
        && let Some(assumption) = ASSUMPTIONS.iter().find(|a| a.id == id)
    {
        return NoteFallback::Assumption(assumption);
    }
    let mut nearest_assumption = None;
    for term in upstream_nearest_first(path) {
        if let Some(note) = notes::note_for(&term) {
            return NoteFallback::Note(note);
        }
        if nearest_assumption.is_none() {
            nearest_assumption = ASSUMPTIONS
                .iter()
                .find(|a| a.paths.contains(&term.as_str()));
        }
    }
    match (nearest_assumption, row) {
        (Some(assumption), _) => NoteFallback::Assumption(assumption),
        (None, Some(Learn::None(reason))) => NoteFallback::Reason(reason),
        (None, _) => NoteFallback::Reason(NO_NOTE),
    }
}

/// Every path `path`'s equation reads, transitively, nearest first: breadth first over the
/// registry's terms, each equation's terms in its own order, each path once. Empty for a path
/// without an equation record.
fn upstream_nearest_first(path: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut seen = BTreeSet::from([path.to_owned()]);
    let mut order = Vec::new();
    let mut queue = VecDeque::from([path.to_owned()]);
    while let Some(at) = queue.pop_front() {
        let Some(eq) = registry().equation_for(&at) else {
            continue;
        };
        for term in &eq.terms {
            if seen.insert(term.clone()) {
                order.push(term.clone());
                queue.push_back(term.clone());
            }
        }
    }
    order
}
```

```rust
/// Explain's lines under an equation no reviewed note explains ([`note_fallback`]): the closest
/// note as a link, an assumption's label and rationale, or the reason and where the notes are.
/// Returns the note asked for.
fn note_fallback_ui(ui: &mut egui::Ui, path: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    match note_fallback(path) {
        NoteFallback::Note(note) => {
            let mut asked = None;
            ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
                ui.weak(NEAREST_NOTE);
                if ui.link(glyph_safe(note.title)).clicked() {
                    asked = Some(note.id);
                }
            });
            asked
        }
        NoteFallback::Assumption(assumption) => {
            ui.weak(format!("{NEAREST_ASSUMPTION} {}", assumption.label));
            ui.add(egui::Label::new(glyph_safe(assumption.rationale)).wrap());
            None
        }
        NoteFallback::Reason(reason) => {
            ui.weak(reason);
            ui.weak(START_HERE_HINT);
            None
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
/// A placeholder's value as a note draws it (spec 3.2): the result's display text with its
/// unit, as the readouts show it; `None` (drawn as `note_text::NO_VALUE`) for a result that is
/// missing, empty or not a finite number.
pub(crate) fn note_value(results: &DesignResults, path: &str) -> Option<String> {
    match results.get(path)? {
        Value::None => None,
        Value::Num(x) if !x.is_finite() => None,
        value => Some(with_unit(
            format_value(&value),
            result_info(path).map_or("", |info| info.meta.unit),
        )),
    }
}
```

  and change every inline value closure passed to `render(` in `note_ui` (and in `notes_for_review`, if it builds its

```rust
    );

    /// `before`'s sections in file order: each `## <id>` heading's id and the lines under it up
    /// to the next heading, trimmed.
    fn before_sections(before: &str) -> Vec<(&str, String)> {
        let mut sections: Vec<(&str, String)> = Vec::new();
        for line in before.lines() {
            if let Some(id) = line.strip_prefix("## ") {
                sections.push((id.trim(), String::new()));
            } else if let Some((_, text)) = sections.last_mut() {
                text.push_str(line);
                text.push('\n');
            }
        }
        for (_, text) in &mut sections {
            *text = text.trim().to_owned();
        }
        sections
    }

    /// A note as it ships, rendered at `results` as the panel draws it: the sentences, each
    /// "What to change" entry as "<Step word> <display label>: <text>", the watch-outs and the
    /// sources, every placeholder filled.
    fn note_now(note: &Note, results: &DesignResults) -> String {
        use crate::engine::explain::note_text::render;
        use crate::gui::plain_text::label_for;
        let value = |path: &str| note_value(results, path);
        let mut text = String::from("**What it is**\n\n");
        for (i, sentence) in note.sentences.iter().enumerate() {
            text.push_str(&format!("{}. {}\n", i + 1, render(sentence, &value)));
        }
        text.push_str(&format!("\n**{WHAT_TO_CHANGE}**\n\n"));
        if note.change.is_empty() {
            text.push_str("(none)\n");
        }
        for entry in note.change {
            text.push_str(&format!(
                "- {} {}: {}\n",
                entry.step.word(),
                label_for(entry.input),
                render(entry.text, &value)
            ));
        }
        text.push_str(&format!("\n**{WATCH_OUT}**\n\n"));
        if note.watch_out.is_empty() {
            text.push_str("(none)\n");
        }
        for line in note.watch_out {
            text.push_str(&format!("- {}\n", render(line, &value)));
        }
        text.push_str(&format!("\n**{WHERE_FROM}**\n\n"));
        for source in note.sources {
            text.push_str(&format!("- {source}\n"));
        }
        text
    }

    /// The owner's sign-off sheet (spec section 4, S2-6): for each note its text before slice 2
    /// and the text it ships with at the default design, and its review record.
    fn signoff_sheet(before: &str) -> String {
        let results = crate::compute_all(&DesignInputs::default());
        let sections = before_sections(before);
        let mut sheet = format!(
            "# Magcoupler teaching notes: owner sign-off sheet (guidance slice 2)\n\n\
             Generated by `notes_signoff_sheet` (magcoupling-rs/src/gui/explorer.rs). Regenerate with\n\
             `cargo test --manifest-path magcoupling-rs/Cargo.toml --features app --lib notes_signoff_sheet -- --ignored`.\n\n\
             For each of the {} notes: **Before** is the note at the start of slice 2 (commit b0166ad, from\n\
             `docs/analyses/2026-10-14-magcoupler-notes-before.txt`); **Now** is the note as it ships, rendered at\n\
             the default design: live values filled in, each \"{WHAT_TO_CHANGE}\" entry with the input's name as the\n\
             screen shows it. On screen \"{WHERE_FROM}\" starts closed. Each note passed its physics review;\n\
             \"Review\" names its section of `docs/analyses/2026-10-14-magcoupler-notes-review.md`.\n\n\
             Owner sign-off (spec S2-6, S2-10). Signed: ____________________  Date: ____________\n",
            notes::NOTES.len()
        );
        for note in notes::NOTES {
            let record = match note.review {
                Review::Reviewed { record, .. } => record,
                Review::Draft => "NOT REVIEWED",
            };
            sheet.push_str(&format!(
                "\n## {}: {}\n\nReview: {record}\n\n### Before\n\n",
                note.id, note.title
            ));
            match sections.iter().find(|(id, _)| *id == note.id) {
                Some((_, text)) => sheet.push_str(&format!("```text\n{text}\n```\n")),
                None => sheet.push_str(&format!("{NEW_IN_SLICE}\n")),
            }
            sheet.push_str(&format!(
                "\n### Now (default design)\n\n{}",
                note_now(note, &results)
            ));
        }
        sheet
    }

    #[test]
    #[ignore = "writes the owner's sign-off sheet; run by hand before release"]
    fn notes_signoff_sheet() {
        std::fs::write(SIGNOFF_SHEET, signoff_sheet(BEFORE)).expect("write the sign-off sheet");
        println!("wrote {SIGNOFF_SHEET}");
    }
```

#### Drafter notes

- **Assumptions about other tasks.**
  - T4's snapshot `docs/analyses/2026-10-14-magcoupler-notes-before.txt` heads each note `## <id>`. The contract fixes
    the file, not its heading form; the plan's assembler should make T4's draft write that form. Step 6 has the
    one-line fallback if it does not, and the non-ignored test fails loudly on a mismatch, never silently.
  - T3 put `SHOW_DETAILS` in `panel.rs` or `inputs.rs` (contract); Step 2 covers both.
  - T4 made `Step::word` callable from the GUI (its renderer draws the word) and named the headings
    `WHAT_TO_CHANGE`, `WATCH_OUT` (existing) and `WHERE_FROM` in `gui/explorer.rs` (contract).
  - T5's GUI value text follows the contract (format_value + unit, `None` for missing or non-finite); Step 4 reuses
    it, or extracts it, so the sheet and the screen cannot disagree.
  - T19's Step 14.3 bullet text is the `note_fallback` bullet of Step 10.6 (one source of truth).
- **Risks.**
  - The smoke's three new checks are canvas clicks found in screenshots, the fragile kind (like "Load design"). The
    prompt allows two attempts per target and asks for the reason in notes; T21 re-runs once before treating a
    failure as real.
  - Step 9.2 replaces the whole Teaching notes bullet. If an earlier task wrote a detail the new text lacks, the
    reviewer must merge it in; the replacement text was written against spec 3.1-3.7 and the contract.
  - `include_str!` of `README.md` and `03-structure.yaml` from a test makes a docs typo a test failure; that is the
    point (F36), but a reword of "the N A4 teaching notes" or "its N steps" or "NOTES (N notes" must keep the phrase.
- **Open questions with proposed rulings.**
  - Commit the generated sheet in T20? Ruling: no. T21 generates it after the whole-branch review's fix wave, so the
    owner signs what ships; T20 only proves the generator (Step 7 deletes its output).
  - Should the sheet show held states ("held by Auto") for change entries? Ruling: no. At the default design Auto is
    off and the sheet is about the text; the on-screen held state is tested by T4.
- **Review Focus candidates.**
  - A note whose placeholder renders "no prediction" at the default design (a value missing on the default): Step 7's
    grep flags it before T21; the T5 placeholder tests should already forbid it, but nothing else would show the owner.

### Task 21: Release: whole-branch review, the gate with gate 12 running, web build and gui-smoke, the sign-off sheet, STOP for the owner; then merge, push and the deploy check

Executor: the controller (this task dispatches reviewers and runs the release; it writes no feature code). Review
and fix waves run on the session model (CLAUDE.md section 5: final whole-branch reviews keep the session model;
a fix of a physics-text finding is session model; a retry is never downgraded). Spec section 7 (S2-10), R12, R14.

All commands run from the repository root `C:/Users/Cole/source/repos/linkage_simulation` in Git Bash, on branch
`magcoupling/guidance-2`. Logs go to `magcoupling-rs/target/release-s2/` (gitignored by `magcoupling-rs/.gitignore`).

Rules that hold through every step:
- Never `git add -A` or `git add .`: the owner's untracked `docs/analyses/2026-05-28-press-4bar-analysis.md` stays
  untracked and unstaged. Stage files by name.
- Never commit `docs/chebyshev_lambda/*.png` (gate 1 rewrites them); restore with `git checkout -- docs/chebyshev_lambda`.
- Never `git worktree prune` (Codex works from a WSL worktree of this repo).
- Nothing is merged to `main` or pushed before the owner's sign-off message (Step 9). Pushing `main` deploys the site.
- The only review report this task commits is the sign-off sheet; the whole-branch review record goes to
  `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-magcoupler-guidance-slice-2/final-review.md` (gitignored, as slice 1's was).

**Files:**
- Create (generated, committed): `docs/analyses/2026-10-14-magcoupler-notes-signoff.md`.
- Create (gitignored): `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-magcoupler-guidance-slice-2/final-review.md`,
  `magcoupling-rs/target/release-s2/{gate.log,build-web.log}`.
- Modify: `docs/ai/05-update-tracker.md` (slice-2 entry), `docs/ai/backlog.yaml` (BL-056 `notes`, then `status`),
  `docs/ai/04-memory.yaml` (the slice-2 active issue written by T20).
- Modify (only through fix waves): whatever the whole-branch review's must-fix items name.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: T1-T20 committed; T18's gates (`release_notes_are_reviewed`, `every_note_names_its_committed_review_section`,
  `start_here_is_the_fourteen_step_order`, `only_the_review_tools_are_ignored`); T20's `notes_signoff_sheet` (ignored
  test) and the gui-smoke fields `first_view`, `details_toggle`, `share_link_loaded`, `sizing_solved`,
  `design_file_loaded`, `explorer_ready`, `why_link_opened`, `tooltip_plain`, `dashboard_scrolls`; the oracle venv
  `reference/magcoupling-py/.venv/Scripts/python.exe`; `linkage-sim-rs/scripts/{gate.sh,build_web.sh,serve_web.sh}`;
  the `gui-smoke` skill (the workflow `.claude/workflows/gui-smoke.js`); `gh`.
- Produces: the committed sign-off sheet; the tracker and BL-056 records; after sign-off the merge commit on `main`,
  the push and a checked deploy.

```bash
grep -rn -A2 '#\[ignore' magcoupling-rs/src magcoupling-rs/tests | grep -o 'fn [a-z_]*' | sort -u
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Whole-branch review (fresh context, session model)**

Dispatch one reviewer on the session model (omit `model`) with this prompt, verbatim:

> You are the whole-branch reviewer for magcoupler guidance slice 2 (branch `magcoupling/guidance-2` of
> C:/Users/Cole/source/repos/linkage_simulation, crate `magcoupling-rs`). Read the spec
> `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-magcoupler-guidance-2-design.md` (binding; sections 2, 3, 5, 6 and the physics
> traps of section 8 and of the slice-1 spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-magcoupler-guidance-design.md`
> section 8), the plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-magcoupler-guidance-slice-2.md` and its contract, then the
> diff `git diff main...magcoupling/guidance-2`. Read-only: change no file. Check, with file:line evidence:
> (1) every spec decision S2-1..S2-10 and ruling R1-R14 is implemented or explicitly deferred by the spec;
> (2) no on-screen string written by the slice states a section-8 trap, calls a torque "guaranteed", types an input
> label instead of `label_for`, quotes a typed default value as a fact about the user's design, or shows a
> spreadsheet cell, audit id or code name with "Show spreadsheet details" off;
> (3) every note's text matches its review record: compare each note's current text with the last review section of
> `docs/analyses/2026-10-14-magcoupler-notes-review.md` for that id and list any note edited after its review;
> (4) the Python-locked labels, help, cells and choices, the engine verdict strings, `reference/` and
> `tests/data/python_schema.json` are unchanged (`git diff main...magcoupling/guidance-2 --stat -- reference tests/data/python_schema.json`
> must be empty; `tests/data/input_schema.json` may change only for Rust-only inputs);
> (5) every test the spec's section 6 lists exists and asserts computed values, not copied literals, except pinned
> strings; no check is left ignored;
> (6) the docs (README, docs/ai 02-05, backlog BL-056) describe the code as it is;
> (7) the Review Focus list of the plan: for each line, is it tested, and does the code do what a user expects?
> Return PASS, or a numbered list of must-fix items (file:line, the defect, the exact replacement text or the test to
> add) and a separate list of suggestions. A must-fix that changes a note's sentences, change entries or watch-outs
> also names the note id.

Save the reviewer's full answer to `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-14-magcoupler-guidance-slice-2/final-review.md`.

- [ ] **Step 3: One fix wave, then the re-review**

For each must-fix item, in order, one commit each, on the session model (an implementer that does not spawn agents):
1. Write the failing test the item names (or the one that shows the defect), run it, see it fail.
2. Apply the fix.
3. A fix that changes a note's text (sentences, change entries, watch-outs, title): that note goes back through the
   per-note review of the contract: run
   `NOTES_FOR_REVIEW=<id> NOTES_REVIEW_OUT=magcoupling-rs/target/release-s2/notes-<id>.txt cargo test --manifest-path magcoupling-rs/Cargo.toml --features app --lib notes_for_review -- --ignored --nocapture`,
   dispatch a fresh session-model physics reviewer on that dump (the engine, the traps, the change entries), apply its
   must-fix items, and append its report to the note's existing section of
   `docs/analyses/2026-10-14-magcoupler-notes-review.md` as a `### Re-review after the whole-branch review` subsection:
   never a second `## <id>` heading (`every_note_names_its_committed_review_section` allows exactly one).
4. A fix that changes GUI wording outside the notes: a G-3 review of the changed strings (one fresh session-model
   physics reviewer), as T19 Step 13.
5. Run the touched suites, both clippy runs and `cargo fmt` (Global Constraints), update the docs the fix changes,
   then commit with a message `fix(magcoupler): <what>, from the slice-2 whole-branch review` and the two trailers:
   ```
   Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
   Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UW1Rcc7PfLxGH7NQJ5srin
   ```
Then dispatch a fresh session-model reviewer on `git diff <commit before the fix wave>..HEAD` with the must-fix list,
asking for PASS or the items still open. Append its answer to `final-review.md`. A second round of must-fix items:
apply them the same way and re-review once more; a third: STOP and report to the owner.

- [ ] **Step 4: The gate, with gate 12 running**

Run in the background (it takes about 6 minutes warm; longer cold), with the oracle's Python named explicitly so
gate 12 cannot SKIP:
```bash
mkdir -p magcoupling-rs/target/release-s2
MAGCOUPLING_PYTHON="$PWD/reference/magcoupling-py/.venv/Scripts/python.exe" bash linkage-sim-rs/scripts/gate.sh 2>&1 | tee magcoupling-rs/target/release-s2/gate.log
```
When it exits, run:
```bash
tail -n 1 magcoupling-rs/target/release-s2/gate.log
grep -c 'SKIP gate 12/12' magcoupling-rs/target/release-s2/gate.log
grep -n 'oracle Python:' magcoupling-rs/target/release-s2/gate.log
grep -n '== gate' magcoupling-rs/target/release-s2/gate.log
git checkout -- docs/chebyshev_lambda
git status --short
```
Expected: the last line is `GATE PASS`; the SKIP count is `0`; `oracle Python: .../reference/magcoupling-py/.venv/Scripts/python.exe`;
twelve `== gate N/12` lines; after the restore, `git status` shows only the owner's untracked file.
On a failure: STOP the release. The failing gate's output names the test; fix it as a must-fix of Step 3 (red test,
fix, the reviews it needs, commit) and run this step again from the top. Never edit `gate.sh` to pass.

- [ ] **Step 6: gui-smoke (with the R14 steps)**

Start the server in the background: `bash linkage-sim-rs/scripts/serve_web.sh 8080`. Then invoke the `gui-smoke`
skill with no arguments (it smokes `http://localhost:8080`: the hub, the linkage app and the calculator).
Expected result: `passed: true`; `hub_page: true`, `canvas_present: true`, `title_warning: false` for the linkage
step; for the calculator `first_view`, `details_toggle`, `share_link_loaded`, `sizing_solved`, `design_file_loaded`,
`explorer_ready`, `why_link_opened`, `tooltip_plain` and `dashboard_scrolls` all `true` and `console_errors` empty.
If only a canvas-click field is false (`design_file_loaded`, `why_link_opened`, `tooltip_plain`,
`dashboard_scrolls`) and its notes say the target was not found, run the skill once more. A field false twice, or
any console error: STOP and treat it as a must-fix (Step 3), with the smoke's notes and screenshots as evidence.
Stop the server afterwards (stop the background task; `Ctrl+C` equivalent).

- [ ] **Step 11: Watch the deploy and check the live page**

Run:
```bash
git rev-parse HEAD
gh run list --workflow "Deploy Web to Vercel" --branch main --limit 1 --json databaseId,headSha,status,conclusion
gh run watch <databaseId from the line above> --exit-status
```
Expected: the run's `headSha` equals `git rev-parse HEAD` (wait and list again if the newest run is still the previous
commit's); `gh run watch` ends with the run `completed` and exit status 0.
Then invoke the `gui-smoke` skill with the arguments `{"url": "https://colesorkness.com"}` (the same steps against
the live site). Expected: `passed: true` with the calculator's `details_toggle` true (the header shows the new
"Show spreadsheet details" toggle, so the new bundle is live, not a cached one).
On a failed deploy or smoke: do not push again blindly; report the run's log (`gh run view <id> --log-failed`) or the
smoke's notes to the owner and fix in a new branch with its own red test.

#### Drafter notes

- **Assumptions about other tasks.**
  - T20's gui-smoke result fields and the ignored `notes_signoff_sheet` exist as T20 writes them; T18's gates exist.
  - The per-note review dump command is the contract's (`NOTES_FOR_REVIEW`, `NOTES_REVIEW_OUT`, `notes_for_review`).
  - The `gui-smoke` skill accepts JSON arguments (`url`, `linkage`, `magcoupling`), as `.claude/workflows/gui-smoke.js`
    reads them; it ran against a local server in slice 1.
- **Facts checked.** The oracle venv exists at `reference/magcoupling-py/.venv/Scripts/python.exe` in this checkout
  (slice 1 borrowed another worktree's); `gate.sh` reads `MAGCOUPLING_PYTHON` first and prints `oracle Python:` or
  `SKIP gate 12/12`; `build_web.sh` builds both bundles and prints `Magcoupling build complete!` (slice 1's run in this
  checkout succeeded without `subst`); the deploy workflow is named "Deploy Web to Vercel" and runs on push to `main`;
  `gh` is installed. `magcoupling-rs/target/` is gitignored.
- **Risks.**
  - Gate 1 rewrites `docs/chebyshev_lambda/*.png`; Step 4 restores them before anything is staged.
  - A note fixed in the wave after its review without a re-review would ship text no reviewer read (F3); Step 3.3 and
    the reviewer's check (3) of Step 2 close that gap; the sign-off sheet is generated after the wave for the same
    reason.
  - The live smoke writes `.playwright-mcp/magcoupling-smoke-design.json` under the repo (gitignored) and deletes it.
- **Open questions with proposed rulings.**
  - Should the release wait for BL-059's gearbox limit? Ruling: no (spec S2-9: slice 2 states the limit as a
    watch-out and the gearbox check is a backlog item); the STOP message asks the question separately.
  - Commit the whole-branch review record? Ruling: no, as slice 1 (gitignored `.superpowers/`); the tracker bullet
    names it, and the committed per-note reviews carry the physics record.
- **Review Focus candidates (for the plan's list).**
  - Gate 12 silently skipping: guarded here by naming `MAGCOUPLING_PYTHON` and grepping for the SKIP line.
  - A cached old bundle on the live site after the deploy: the live smoke's `details_toggle` proves the new bundle.
  - `main` moving between the gate and the merge: Step 10's `--ff-only` pull stops the release if it did.
